title: Spaghetti carbonara
description: Pasta from four ingredients: guanciale, eggs, pecorino and pepper. There is no cream in it and never was. (Spaghetti alla carbonara)

ingredients.text: 100 g Guanciale (cut into short strips; pancetta works)
Salt for the water, to taste

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and salt it properly — this is the only salt in the dish, since the cheese and the guanciale bring their own.
Put the guanciale into a cold pan and turn the heat to medium. The fat should render gradually and the pieces turn golden and crisp at the edges, about 6 to 8 minutes.
While the fat renders, beat the yolks, the whole egg, the grated pecorino and the pepper into a thick paste. Let it sit at room temperature so it does not seize when it meets hot pasta.
Cook the spaghetti a minute short of the packet time. Before draining, save a cup of the cooking water — the sauce will not come together without it.
Take the pan off the heat, add the pasta and toss it through the fat. Let the pan cool for twenty seconds — it should be warm, not hot.
Pour in the egg mixture and stir hard, adding pasta water a spoonful at a time until the sauce turns glossy and coats every strand. Serve immediately.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Risotto alla milanese
description: A saffron risotto built on stock and near-constant stirring, which is what pulls the starch out of the rice and makes it creamy. (Risotto alla milanese)
instructions: Steep the saffron in a ladle of hot stock and set it aside. Keep the rest of the stock at a bare simmer — cold stock stops the cooking.
Melt half the butter and sweat the onion over low heat until soft and translucent without letting it colour, about eight minutes.
Add the rice and stir for a couple of minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges and milky in the centre. This is the tostatura, and it keeps the grains intact.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely — the smell of alcohol has to go.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, waiting until the rice has nearly absorbed it before the next. Around eighteen minutes, until the grain is soft outside with a slight bite in the middle.
Stir in the saffron infusion, take the pan off the heat and beat in the cold butter and parmesan, shaking the pan hard. The risotto should spread slowly across the plate.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ratatouille
description: A Provençal vegetable stew where each vegetable is cooked separately before they meet — otherwise it turns to mush. (Ratatouille niçoise)
instructions: Fry the aubergine over high heat in two spoons of oil until the edges brown, then set it aside. Aubergine drinks oil instantly — do not add more, it gives it back later.
In the same pan, fry the courgette until golden, about four minutes, and add it to the aubergine. It should stay firm.
Fry the pepper until soft with a few charred spots and set it aside as well.
In the remaining oil, sweat the onion until soft, add the garlic and thyme and give it half a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook them down over medium heat into a thick sauce, about twenty minutes. It should hold on a spoon rather than run off it.
Return the vegetables to the pan, season and warm them through together for ten minutes over low heat. Take it off, add the basil and let it stand — ratatouille is better warm than hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: French onion soup
description: Soup from onions, stock and cheese-topped bread. All of the flavour comes from caramelisation, which takes forty minutes rather than twenty. (Soupe à l'oignon gratinée)
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy pot, add the onions and a pinch of salt, and keep them over medium heat, stirring every few minutes. For the first twenty minutes the onions give up water.
Then the caramelisation proper begins: another twenty-five minutes to take the onions to the colour of strong tea. If they catch, lower the heat and add a spoonful of water.
Stir in the flour and cook it out for a couple of minutes so it loses its raw taste.
Pour in the wine and scrape everything stuck to the bottom back into the pot. Let it reduce by half.
Add the stock and thyme, bring to the boil and simmer for twenty minutes. Season at the end, since the stock may already be salty.
Ladle into ovenproof bowls, top each with a slice of baguette, cover with cheese and put them under the grill until bubbling and browned, about three minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Borscht
description: A beetroot soup on beef stock where acid holds both the colour and the flavour. The beetroot is braised separately, never boiled in the pot.
instructions: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it to the boil and skim. Simmer for an hour and a half at a bare tremble — a rolling boil turns the stock cloudy.
Braise the beetroot in a pan with a spoon of oil, the tomato paste and the vinegar, covered, for about twenty minutes. The vinegar is what keeps the colour.
Separately fry the onion and carrot until soft and golden.
Lift the meat out, pull it into pieces and return it to the stock. Add the potatoes and give them ten minutes — before any acid reaches the pot.
Add the cabbage, then after five minutes the beetroot and the fried vegetables. Give it five minutes more, add the bay and garlic and take it straight off the heat.
Let it stand covered for at least twenty minutes. Serve with sour cream, which softens the acid and pulls the flavours together.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Imeretian khachapuri
description: A round flatbread with the cheese inside rather than on top. The dough is made on matsoni, and there is as much filling as there is dough. (იმერული ხაჭაპური)

ingredients.text: 200 ml Matsoni or kefir (at room temperature)

instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm matsoni and leave it ten minutes to foam. No foam means dead yeast, so start again.
Add the egg, the melted butter, the salt and the flour. Knead a soft dough: it should stay slightly tacky, and no more flour goes in.
Cover it and leave it somewhere warm for an hour, until it has doubled.
Mix both cheeses together by hand until even and divide into four balls. Divide the dough into four as well.
Roll each piece of dough into a disc, set a ball of cheese in the middle, gather the edges to the centre and pinch them shut. Turn it seam down and roll it gently to about a centimetre thick.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for about four minutes a side, until dark spots appear. Brush the finished bread with butter.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Miso soup
description: A soup of dashi and miso that takes ten minutes. Miso must never boil: boiling takes out both the aroma and the point of it. (味噌汁)
instructions: Cover the kombu with cold water and set it over low heat. Bring it to the edge of a boil over about ten minutes and lift the seaweed out before bubbles appear.
Bring the water to the boil, add the bonito flakes, take it off the heat at once and let it stand for two minutes until the flakes sink.
Strain the stock through a sieve without pressing the flakes — pressed flakes turn it bitter.
Soak the wakame in cold water for five minutes; it swells several times over.
Warm the dashi, add the tofu and the wakame and hold it at a low heat for a couple of minutes.
Whisk the miso smooth in a ladle of the hot stock, stir it back in and take the pan off the heat immediately. Scatter over the spring onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Guacamole
description: Avocado, lime, onion and chilli crushed with a fork. No blender and no sour cream: both turn it into a dip rather than guacamole.
instructions: Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop the flesh into a bowl. A ripe avocado gives under a finger without collapsing.
Add the lime juice and the salt straight away. The acid needs to reach the flesh before it starts to brown.
Crush with a fork to a coarse, uneven mass. Lumps of avocado should remain — that is the texture you want.
Fold in the onion, the jalapeño and the coriander, taste, and adjust the salt or lime. The tomato goes in last and gently, so it does not water everything down.
Serve at once. If it has to wait, press cling film directly onto the surface — air is what darkens it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tom yum goong
description: A hot and sour prawn soup where the balance is set at the end: fish sauce, lime and sugar go in to taste rather than by the recipe. (ต้มยำกุ้ง)

ingredients.text: 400 g Prawns (heads on, keep the shells)

instructions: Peel the prawns, leaving the tails on. Keep the shells and heads: the broth is built on them.
Fry the shells in the pot for a couple of minutes until bright orange, cover with the water and simmer fifteen minutes. Strain.
Return the broth to the heat, add the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and let them steep at a low simmer for five minutes.
Add the mushrooms and the crushed chillies, then after two minutes the prawns. They are done the moment they curl into a C — beyond that they turn rubbery.
Take the pot off the heat. Add the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar, stir and taste. Adjust a spoon at a time until sour, salty and hot sit where you want them.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the coriander. Leave the lemongrass and galangal in the pot, or warn people not to eat them.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Dal tadka
description: A lentil stew finished by pouring sizzling spiced fat over it. That step is the dish. (दाल तड़का)
instructions: Cover the lentils with three cups of water, add the turmeric and simmer covered for thirty minutes, until the grains collapse into a soft mass.
Mash some of the lentils against the side of the pot and season. The consistency should be that of a thick soup.
Separately fry the onion until golden, add the tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce. Stir that into the lentils.
Heat the ghee in a small pan until it is just short of smoking. Add the mustard seeds; they should crackle within seconds.
Add the cumin at once, the garlic and chillies ten seconds later, the asafoetida twenty seconds after that. The whole thing takes under a minute and cannot be left alone.
Pour the sizzling tadka straight into the lentils — it should hiss. Stir once and serve with rice or flatbread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Paella valenciana
description: Rice in a wide pan with chicken, rabbit and beans. It is never stirred once, and the crust on the bottom depends on that. (Paella valenciana)

ingredients.text: 320 g Bomba rice, or another short grain
300 g Rabbit, in pieces (chicken will do instead)

instructions: Heat the oil in a wide pan and brown the chicken and rabbit on every side. This is not a five-minute job: it takes a good quarter of an hour, and there is no point rushing it — the flavour of the whole dish is laid down here.
Push the meat to the edges, put the green beans in the middle and fry them for a couple of minutes. Add the grated tomato and the paprika and cook until the tomato darkens and stops smelling raw.
Pour in the stock, add the rosemary, saffron and white beans, salt it noticeably harder than feels right and let it boil for ten minutes. This is the last moment you can correct the seasoning.
Scatter the rice in an even layer and level it once with a spoon. After that do not touch the pan again — no stirring, no smoothing.
Cook on a high flame for ten minutes, then drop to medium for another eight, until the stock is gone. The rice should be showing above the surface.
Turn the heat up for half a minute and listen: the moment the sound turns from bubbling to a dry crackle, take it off. That is the socarrat. Cover with a cloth and let it stand for five minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Spanish tortilla
description: A thick omelette of potato and onion, where the potato is not fried but poached in oil until it is nearly a purée. (Tortilla española)

ingredients.text: 400 ml Olive oil (nearly all of it goes back in the bottle)

instructions: Heat the oil in a deep pan until it is warm rather than hot — a slice of potato dropped in should sigh, not crackle. Add the potato and onion and salt them.
Poach for twenty minutes, turning gently now and then. It is ready when a slice breaks easily against the side of the pan. Drain through a colander, keeping the potato.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and fold the warm potato through them. Let it sit for ten minutes: the potato gives up starch and the tortilla holds together for it.
In a 24 cm pan with a spoon of oil, pour the mixture in and cook over medium heat for four minutes, easing the edges towards the middle with a spatula.
Cover with a plate, flip in one movement and slide it back raw side down. Three minutes more leaves the centre slightly loose, which is how it should be.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Moussaka
description: Aubergine, a meat sauce with cinnamon and a thick layer of béchamel, baked until it sets firm enough to cut. (Μουσακάς)
instructions: Salt the aubergine slices and leave them in a colander for half an hour, then pat them dry. Brush with oil and roast at 200 °C for twenty minutes until soft and golden.
Fry the onion until soft, add the mince and cook, breaking up the lumps, until every drop of water has gone and the meat starts to brown. Pour in the wine and let it cook away.
Add the garlic, tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer for twenty minutes. The sauce is right when a spoon drawn across the bottom leaves a track behind it.

Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook for a minute. Pour in warm milk in a thin stream, whisking without stopping, and cook to the thickness of soured cream. Off the heat, add nutmeg, the yolks and half the cheese.
Layer it up: potato, aubergine, meat sauce, aubergine again. Pour the béchamel over and scatter the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes until the top is golden. Let it stand for half an hour before cutting: hot moussaka does not slice, it slumps.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Horiatiki salad
description: The village salad, with no leaves in it: tomato, cucumber, onion, olives and a whole slab of feta on top. (Χωριάτικη σαλάτα)
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into large wedges and salt them straight in the bowl. Leave them five minutes: the juice they give up becomes the base of the dressing.
Add the cucumber, pepper and onion. Mix with your hands rather than a spoon — nothing breaks that way.
Scatter the olives over, lay the slab of feta on top and pour the oil over everything at once. Sprinkle the oregano straight onto the feta, where the oil will open it up.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Phở bò
description: A clear beef broth with charred ginger and whole spices, rice noodles, and beef that finishes cooking in the bowl. (Phở bò)

ingredients.text: Coriander, spring onion, Thai basil, to taste

instructions: Cover the bones with cold water, bring to the boil and let them go for ten minutes. Throw the water away, rinse the bones under the tap and wash the pot. This step is what buys you a clear broth.
Halve the onion and ginger and char the cut faces in a dry pan or straight over the flame until they blacken in patches.
Toast the spices in a dry pan until they smell, then tie them in muslin. Return the bones to the clean pot with the brisket, onion, ginger and spices, and cover with water three fingers above.
Simmer for three hours at the barest tremble. Skim for the first half hour. Lift the brisket out after ninety minutes and let it cool.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and season with fish sauce and sugar. Taste it: it should be slightly saltier than pleasant to drink on its own, because the noodles will take their share.
Cook the noodles and divide them between bowls. Lay the sliced brisket and the raw sirloin on top. Ladle boiling broth over so it covers the meat, and serve the herbs, lime and chilli alongside.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bánh mì
description: A French baguette with Vietnamese filling: pâté, pork, pickled vegetables and coriander in one sandwich. (Bánh mì)
instructions: Stir the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt into 100 ml of warm water until dissolved. Pour it over the carrot and daikon and leave for an hour at room temperature.
Marinate the pork in fish sauce with a spoon of sugar for twenty minutes, then sear it over a high flame for three minutes a side, until the edges caramelise.
Warm the baguettes at 200 °C for five minutes so the crust crisps again. Split them lengthways, not all the way through.
Spread pâté on one half and mayonnaise on the other. Layer in the pork, the drained pickles, cucumber, coriander and chilli. Press it shut with your palm and serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pesto alla genovese
description: Basil ground with garlic and pine nuts. No heat and no blender — a mortar and a cool room. (Pesto alla genovese)
instructions: Wash the basil and dry it completely: any water stops the oil binding to the leaves. Chill the mortar and pestle in the fridge.
Pound the garlic with the coarse salt to a paste. The salt works as an abrasive; without it the garlic just slides around.
Add the pine nuts and work them to a cream, then add the basil a handful at a time. The movement is a pressing circle rather than a pounding: the leaves are crushed against the wall, not smashed.
Work in both cheeses, then trickle the oil in while still grinding. The sauce should come together thick and even.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tacos al pastor
description: Pork in a marinade of dried chillies and pineapple, seared to caramelised edges, in a corn tortilla. (Tacos al pastor)

ingredients.text: 30 g Achiote paste (or a teaspoon of ground annatto)

instructions: Seed the chillies and toast them in a dry pan until they smell — twenty seconds a side, no longer, or they turn bitter. Cover with boiling water for fifteen minutes.
Blend the softened chillies with half the pineapple, the achiote, vinegar, garlic, cumin and oregano to a smooth paste. Season it.
Coat the pork in the marinade and leave it at least two hours, ideally overnight. Do not go past a day: the pineapple will soften the meat to mush.
Get a pan searing hot and cook the meat in batches, two minutes a side. Do not stir until dark edges appear.
Sear the rest of the pineapple in the same pan and dice it. Chop the meat roughly, warm the tortillas twenty seconds a side and build: meat, pineapple, onion, coriander, lime.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Menemen
description: Eggs cooked into tomatoes and green pepper. They are never beaten and rarely stirred, or you end up with ordinary scrambled eggs. (Menemen)
instructions: Slice the peppers into rings and fry them in the two fats for three or four minutes, until the edges start to darken.
Add the tomatoes, salt them and cook over medium heat for ten minutes. Wait for the oil to separate and glisten at the edges — that is the sign the water has gone.
Lower the heat, break the eggs straight into the sauce and scatter the pepper flakes. Stir slowly and only two or three times, leaving streaks of yolk.
Take it off when the white has set and the yolk is still loose: the pan finishes the job. Scatter over the oregano and the cheese.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mercimek çorbası
description: A red lentil soup blended smooth and finished with lemon and paprika butter. (Mercimek çorbası)
instructions: Fry the onion and carrot in a spoon of butter until soft, add the tomato paste and give it another minute, until it darkens.
Add the lentils, potato and water, bring to the boil and simmer for twenty-five minutes, until the lentils have collapsed completely.
Blend until entirely smooth. The soup should be thick but still pourable; loosen it with boiling water if it is not.
Melt the rest of the butter, take it off the heat and stir in the mint and paprika. Ladle out the soup, spoon the butter over and serve with a wedge of lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Khinkali
description: Purses of stiff dough holding chopped meat and broth. The broth appears on its own, from water worked into the filling. (ხინკალი)

ingredients.text: 200 ml Iced water for the filling

instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water and a pinch of salt. It should come out noticeably stiffer than a dumpling dough — hard work to knead. Wrap it and rest it for forty minutes.
Chop the meat by hand into pieces a few millimetres across. Mix it with the onion, coriander, cumin, salt and pepper.
Work the iced water into the filling a little at a time until the mixture turns sticky and stops taking any more. Chill it for twenty minutes.

Roll out discs 12 cm across and about two millimetres thick. Put a tablespoon of filling in the middle and gather the edge in pleats all the way round — eighteen at the least. Twist the top and pinch it shut.
Drop them into a large pot of salted boiling water, swirling the water with a slotted spoon first so they do not stick. Boil for seven or eight minutes after they float.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Butter chicken
description: Yoghurt-marinated chicken, roasted, in a tomato and cream sauce finished with fenugreek. (मुर्ग़ मक्खनी)
instructions: Mix the yoghurt with half the ginger, garlic and spices, season it and marinate the chicken for at least an hour, better overnight.
Roast the chicken at 220 °C for twenty minutes, or sear it in a screaming-hot pan until it takes dark scorch marks. It can stay slightly underdone inside — the sauce will finish it.
Melt the butter and fry the onion with the rest of the ginger and garlic until golden. Add the tomatoes and the spices and cook for fifteen minutes.
Blend the sauce with the soaked cashews until completely smooth and return it to the pan. It is the cashews, not flour, that give the sauce its body.
Return the chicken to the sauce, pour in the cream and warm it through for five minutes without letting it boil. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms, stir it in and take the pan off.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Katsudon
description: A breaded pork cutlet finished in sweet-salt broth with egg and slid onto rice. (カツ丼)

ingredients.text: 2 Pork loin (150 g each, beaten flat)

instructions: Nick the fat rim of each cutlet in a few places so they do not curl, season them and coat in flour, then egg, then panko.
Deep-fry at 170 °C for three minutes a side until golden. Drain on a rack rather than paper, so the underside stays crisp.
Cut the cutlets into strips a centimetre and a half wide without moving them apart — the shape matters when you serve.
In a small pan bring the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar to the boil, add the onion and cook for three minutes until soft.

Slide the cutlet into the broth, pour two thirds of the loosely beaten egg around it and cover for a minute. Add the rest, cover for twenty seconds more and take it off — the top layer of egg should stay loose.
Slide everything in the pan onto the rice in one movement, sauce and all.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Syrniki
description: Curd cheese fritters with as much curd as possible and exactly enough flour to keep them together. (Сырники)

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Plain flour (plus a little for your hands)
Sour cream and jam, to taste

instructions: Push the curd through a sieve or blitz it. Grainy curd makes grainy syrniki; this step is not optional.
Work in the egg, sugar, vanilla and salt, then the flour. The mixture stays sticky; that is correct.
With wet or lightly floured hands shape discs about a centimetre and a half thick. Thicker and the middle stays raw, thinner and they dry out.
Fry over medium heat with a lid on, three or four minutes a side. The lid matters more than the butter: it steams the middle through.

image.credit: Juerg Vollmer from Zürich, Switzerland ; cut by Off-shell

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pad thai
description: Rice noodles fried with tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar. The whole thing takes four minutes. (ผัดไทย)
instructions: Soak the noodles in warm water for twenty minutes. They should bend but still feel firm when you bite one.
Dissolve the palm sugar in the tamarind and fish sauce, warming them together for a minute. Taste it: sour, salty and sweet should all land equally.
Get the wok hot, fry the tofu until crisp, add the garlic and shallot, then after half a minute the prawns. Cook until pink and push them to the side.
Break the eggs into the cleared space, let them set and break them up with the spatula. Add the drained noodles and pour in the sauce.
Fry, tossing constantly, for two minutes until the noodles drink the sauce and soften. Add the sprouts and chives, toss once and take it off.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tiramisu
description: Savoiardi in coffee under a mascarpone cream. No baking, but two places where it can go wrong. (Tiramisù)
instructions: Whisk the yolks with half the sugar over a pan of boiling water, without touching the water, until pale and thick — about seven minutes. Take it off and cool to room temperature.
Fold the cold mascarpone into the cooled yolks with a spoon rather than a mixer. A mixer breaks the fat and the cream turns grainy — the first place tiramisu usually fails.
Whip the whites with the rest of the sugar to firm peaks and fold them into the cream in three additions, lifting from underneath.
Mix the coffee with the marsala. Dip each savoiardo for one second a side and lay them in a tight layer in the dish.
Spread half the cream, level it, then repeat the biscuit and cream layers. Cover and refrigerate for at least six hours, better overnight.
Dust with cocoa through a sieve right before serving. Do it in advance and the cocoa takes on moisture and goes blotchy.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gazpacho
description: A cold tomato soup blended with bread and oil into an emulsion — that is what makes it thick rather than watery. (Gazpacho andaluz)

ingredients.text: 80 g Stale white bread (crumb only, soaked)

instructions: Soak the bread crumb in cold water for ten minutes and squeeze it dry.
Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic and bread until completely smooth. It takes longer than you expect — a good two minutes at full speed.
With the blender still running, pour the oil in a thin stream. The soup pales and thickens: that is the emulsion.
Add the vinegar and salt, taste and season again. Pass it through a sieve for a silkier texture and chill for at least two hours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ham croquetas
description: A thick béchamel with ham, chilled until firm, breadcrumbed and deep-fried. (Croquetas de jamón)
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil, soften the onion until translucent, add the ham and warm it for a minute so the fat renders into the pan.
Add the flour and cook, stirring, for four or five minutes, until it smells nutty and just begins to colour.
Add the warm milk a ladle at a time, stirring smooth before the next goes in. Cook for ten minutes more, until the mixture pulls away from the sides.
Season with nutmeg and salt, spread into a dish two centimetres deep, press cling film onto the surface and chill for at least four hours.
Shape cylinders with wet hands and coat in egg then breadcrumbs. For a sturdier shell, do the coating twice.
Deep-fry at 180 °C for two minutes in small batches. A crowded pan drops the temperature and the croquetas drink oil instead of crisping.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ceviche
description: Raw fish in lime juice with onion and ají. It marinates for minutes, not hours — longer and it is cooked through. (Cebiche)

ingredients.text: 600 g Sashimi-grade white fish (in 2 cm cubes)

instructions: Soak the sliced onion in iced water for ten minutes and pat it dry: the harshness goes, the flavour stays.
Squeeze the limes by hand rather than in a press: pressure on the skin releases bitter oils.
Salt the fish, mix it with the chopped ají and coriander, pour the lime over and leave it exactly three to five minutes. The edges turn opaque and the middle stays translucent.
Add the onion, toss once and serve at once with the sweet potato and corn. Pour the juice from the bowl into small glasses.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lomo saltado
description: Beef seared in a wok with onion and tomato, served with both chips and rice at once. (Lomo saltado)
instructions: Marinate the beef in the soy, vinegar and garlic for fifteen minutes, then pat it dry: a wet surface will not scorch.
Heat the pan until it smokes and sear the beef in two batches, ninety seconds each, leaving it alone for the first forty seconds. Set it aside.
In the same pan fry the onion and ají for ninety seconds — the onion should stay crisp inside.
Return the beef, pour in what is left of the marinade, add the tomatoes and warm through for half a minute. Take it off and stir in the coriander.
Serve with hot chips — some tossed into the pan so they take up the sauce — and a separate helping of rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mapo tofu
description: Tofu in a hot doubanjiang sauce with Sichuan pepper, which numbs rather than burns. (麻婆豆腐)
instructions: Slip the tofu into barely simmering salted water for three minutes and drain it gently.
Fry the pork until browned and its fat has rendered, then push it aside. Add the doubanjiang and fry for a minute, until the oil turns red.
Add the garlic, ginger and black beans, warm for half a minute and pour in the stock. Bring it to the boil.
Slide the tofu in and simmer for three minutes without stirring — swirl the pan instead, or the cubes break up.
Slake the cornflour in cold water and add it in two goes, letting the sauce come back to the boil each time. Off the heat, scatter over the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gong bao chicken
description: Diced chicken with peanuts and dried chillies in a sauce where the vinegar matters more than the sugar. (宫保鸡丁)
instructions: Mix the chicken with the egg white, a spoon of cornflour, a spoon of soy and a pinch of salt, and leave it twenty minutes.
Mix the sauce in advance: vinegar, the rest of the soy, the sugar and the rest of the cornflour with two spoons of water. Keep it within reach — there is no time to mix it later.
Heat the oil and fry the chillies with the Sichuan pepper for twenty seconds, until dark but not black. Burnt chilli turns bitter.
Add the chicken and leave it alone for a minute, then toss and cook through — two minutes more.
Throw in the garlic, ginger and the white of the spring onion, then after half a minute pour in the sauce. It thickens in seconds. Off the heat, add the peanuts and the green of the onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Coq au vin
description: Chicken braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and small onions. Marinating the day before does half the work. (Coq au vin)
instructions: Cover the chicken with the wine, carrot, garlic and herbs and leave it in the fridge overnight. In the morning lift the meat out and dry it, keeping the wine.
Render the bacon in a casserole and lift it out. In that fat, brown the chicken hard on all sides, in batches.
Dust with the flour, stir and cook for two minutes. Pour in the marinade with its vegetables and the stock, bring to the boil and skim.
Braise covered over a low flame or at 160 °C for an hour. The sauce should barely tremble.
While it braises, fry the onions in butter until golden, and separately the mushrooms over a high flame until they colour.
Add the onions, mushrooms and bacon to the pot, give it ten minutes over a low flame and check the sauce for salt.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Crème brûlée
description: A yolk custard baked in a water bath under a lid of burnt sugar. (Crème brûlée)
instructions: Split the vanilla, scrape the seeds into the cream and heat it to just below boiling. Take it off and let it infuse for fifteen minutes.
Work the yolks and sugar together without whipping air in — foam is not wanted here. Pour the warm cream in a thin stream, stirring all the while.
Strain through a sieve and skim any foam off the surface. Divide between ramekins and stand them in a deep tray.
Pour boiling water into the tray to halfway up the ramekins and bake at 150 °C for forty minutes. The centre should wobble.
Cool completely and refrigerate for at least four hours. Only then dust with sugar and burn it with a blowtorch.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Käsespätzle
description: Swabian egg noodles layered with cheese and buried under fried onion. (Käsespätzle)
instructions: Mix the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg and beat the dough with a spoon for a good five minutes, until bubbles rise and it starts to string off the spoon.
While the dough rests, fry the onion in butter over medium heat until deep gold. That is twenty minutes, not five — the sugars need the time to caramelise.
Press the dough into boiling salted water through a spätzle grater or a wide-holed colander. They float within a minute; lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Layer them into a warm dish: spätzle, cheese, spätzle, cheese. The heat of the noodles melts it; no oven is needed.
Bury it under the fried onion and serve at once. The classic side is a green salad with a vinegar dressing, and it is a counterweight rather than a garnish.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rinderrouladen
description: Thin slices of beef rolled around mustard, bacon and gherkin and braised until they give way. (Rinderrouladen)

ingredients.text: 800 g Beef, thinly sliced (150-200 g each, beaten thin)

instructions: Beat the beef to five millimetres, season it and spread with mustard. Lay the bacon, strips of onion and a gherkin along the short edge.
Roll them up, tucking the sides in, and secure with a skewer or string. Firm but not tight — the filling expands.
Brown the rolls hard on every side and lift them out. In the same fat fry the remaining onion and the carrot, add the tomato paste and give it a minute.
Pour in the wine, let it reduce by half, add the stock and bay. Return the rolls, cover and braise over a low flame for an hour and a half.
Lift the rolls out and remove the skewers. Blend the gravy in the pot or crush it with a masher, then reduce it to the thickness you want.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bibimbap
description: Rice under separately cooked vegetables, meat and an egg, mixed with gochujang right before eating. (비빔밥)
instructions: Marinate the beef in soy, garlic and a spoon of sesame oil for twenty minutes.
Blanch the spinach for thirty seconds, squeeze it dry and dress with sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Boil the sprouts three minutes and dress them the same way, with garlic.
Fry the carrot and the mushrooms separately, a couple of minutes each, seasoning each on its own. No need to wash the pan in between.
Sear the beef over a high flame for two minutes. Fry the eggs separately, leaving the yolks runny.
Divide the hot rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables and beef in sections, and top with an egg and a spoon of gochujang. Each person does the mixing.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kimchi jjigae
description: A stew of over-fermented kimchi with pork and tofu. The older the kimchi, the better it works. (김치찌개)
instructions: Fry the pork in the sesame oil over medium heat until the fat has rendered and the meat has colour, about five minutes.
Add the kimchi and fry for five minutes, until the edges darken. This step takes the raw edge off the acidity and rounds the flavour out.
Stir in the gochugaru, gochujang and garlic, pour in the kimchi liquid and the water, and bring it to the boil.
Simmer for twenty minutes, add the onion and tofu and give it five more. Do not stir the tofu; it falls apart.
Off the heat, scatter over the spring onion and serve it in the pot, with a separate bowl of rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Souvlaki
description: Pork on skewers in lemon, oregano and olive oil, cooked fast over a fierce heat. (Σουβλάκι)
instructions: Mix the oil, lemon juice and zest, oregano, crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Coat the meat and leave it two hours, and no more than four.
While it marinates, make the tzatziki: yoghurt with the squeezed cucumber, a clove of garlic, a spoon of oil and salt.
Thread the meat onto skewers loosely — the heat has to get between the pieces. A tightly packed skewer stays raw in the middle.
Cook on a hot grill or griddle, three minutes on each of the four sides. The meat should darken rather than pale.
Rest the meat for five minutes, warm the pitas thirty seconds a side, and serve with the tzatziki and lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chicken biryani
description: Rice and marinated chicken finished together under a lid: the layers cook in steam rather than by stirring. (बिरयानी)
instructions: Fry the onions in ghee to a deep gold — twenty minutes over medium heat. Set half aside: that is the birista, and the main flavour of the dish.
Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt with the ginger, garlic, spices, half the fried onion, mint and salt. Give it an hour, better three.
Boil the rice in plenty of salted water with the whole spices for exactly five minutes and drain. A grain should snap but stay white in the middle.
Spread the marinated chicken over the bottom of a heavy pot and the rice over it in an even layer. Pour the saffron milk over in patches and scatter the rest of the onion and the herbs.
Cover as tightly as you can, sealing the rim with foil if you like. Five minutes on a high flame, then forty on the lowest. Do not lift the lid once.
Let it stand for ten minutes, then fold once from the bottom up, lifting the chicken into the rice rather than stirring everything to a mush.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shoyu ramen
description: Broth, tare and oil — three separate things assembled in the bowl rather than cooked together. (醤油ラーメン)
instructions: Cover the carcasses with cold water, boil for ten minutes and pour it away. Rinse the bones and the pot: the clarity of the broth depends on it.
Cover again with fresh water, add the ginger and garlic and simmer for three hours. Put the kombu in twenty minutes before the end and lift it out before it boils — boiled kombu turns bitter.
For the tare, reduce the soy, mirin, sake and shiitake to a third. What is left is a thick dark liquid — two spoons per bowl.
Boil the eggs for six and a half minutes, cool them in iced water, peel and steep them in the leftover tare for two hours.
Boil the noodles separately, strictly to the time on the packet, drain and put them straight into bowls with the tare in the bottom.
Pour the hot broth over, stir once so the tare disperses, and lay on the pork, the egg and the spring onion. Finish with the sesame oil.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pierogi ruskie
description: Dumplings of potato and curd cheese, served with fried onion and soured cream. (Pierogi ruskie)
instructions: Pour the boiling water with the oil and salt over the flour, work it with a spoon and then, once it cools, by hand for eight minutes. Cover and rest it half an hour.
Fry two of the onions in butter to a deep gold. Half goes into the filling and half is kept for serving.
Mash the warm potato with the curd and the fried onion, and season generously. The filling has to be firm enough to hold its shape.
Roll the dough to two millimetres, cut discs with a glass, add a teaspoon of filling and pinch the edges dry — wet dough will not seal.
Boil in batches in a wide pot of salted water. Lift them out a minute after they float.
Serve with the rest of the fried onion and soured cream. Plenty of people fry the boiled pierogi in butter afterwards, which is equally correct.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Żurek
description: A sour soup on a rye starter with white sausage and egg. The sourness comes from fermentation, not vinegar. (Żurek)
instructions: Render the bacon in a pot, soften the onion in it, add the garlic and marjoram and warm them for half a minute.
Pour in the stock, lower the sausage in whole and simmer for thirty minutes. Do not pierce it, or its juices leave too early.
Lift the sausage out, slice it and return it to the pot. Shake the starter in its jar and pour it in, stirring.
Warm it for five minutes without letting it boil hard, stir in the cream and taste. If it is not sour enough, add more starter; salt at the end.
Ladle into bowls, add half a boiled egg each and serve with horseradish. In Poland żurek often comes in a hollowed loaf.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sauerbraten
description: Beef steeped for days in a vinegar marinade and braised in it, with a gravy thickened on gingerbread. (Rheinischer Sauerbraten)
instructions: Boil the vinegar with the wine, vegetables and spices, cool it completely and pour it over the beef. Keep it in the fridge three to five days, turning once a day.
Lift the meat out, dry it with kitchen paper and brown it hard on every side in a hot casserole. Strain the marinade, keeping the vegetables.
Fry the marinated vegetables in the same fat, add the sugar and let it catch a little colour. Pour in the marinade and bring it to the boil.
Return the meat, cover and braise over a low flame for two hours, turning it once halfway. A fork should meet no resistance.
Take the meat out and keep it warm. Stir the crumbled gingerbread and the raisins into the gravy and cook for fifteen minutes: the gingerbread dissolves and thickens it on its own.
Blend the gravy smooth and taste it for the balance of sour and sweet. Carve the meat across the grain and pour the gravy over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Swabian potato salad
description: Potato dressed in warm stock with vinegar and oil. No mayonnaise — southern Germany does not admit it here. (Schwäbischer Kartoffelsalat)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until done, about twenty minutes from the boil. Test with a knife: it should go in without dropping through.
While they cook, warm the stock with the onion, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper, without letting it boil.
Peel the potatoes while hot, holding them on a fork, and slice them three or four millimetres thick straight into the bowl.
Pour the hot dressing over and leave it twenty minutes, turning it once. The potato drinks almost all of the liquid.
Add the oil, turn it again and taste. It should be slightly sharper than feels right; the flavour settles as it stands.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bucatini all'amatriciana
description: Guanciale, tomato and pecorino. No onion, no garlic, no olive oil — the fat comes from the meat. (Bucatini all'amatriciana)
instructions: Put the guanciale into a cold dry pan and turn on a medium flame. A slow start renders the fat completely; a hot pan burns the outside and leaves it tough within.
When the pieces turn glassy and gold at the edges, lift half of them out for the top. Pour in the wine and let it cook away.
Crush the tomatoes by hand, add them with the chilli and simmer for ten minutes. The sauce should thicken without losing its red.
Boil the bucatini a minute short, move it into the sauce with a ladle of its water and finish it over the flame for half a minute.
Off the heat, stir in the pecorino and serve. The reserved guanciale goes on top with a little more cheese.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a thick sauce of tomato and pepper with cumin and paprika. (שקשוקה)
instructions: Fry the onion and peppers in the oil for ten minutes, until the pepper is soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa and warm them for a minute — to the smell, not to burning.
Pour in the tomatoes, crush them and simmer for fifteen minutes. The sauce is ready when a spoon leaves a track on the bottom.
Make hollows with a spoon and break an egg into each. Cover and give it five to seven minutes: the whites set, the yolks stay loose.
Scatter over the feta and coriander and serve it in the pan with bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Hummus
description: Chickpeas whipped with tahini, lemon and iced water to a cream. The skins come off. (חומוס)
instructions: Drain the soaked chickpeas, cover with fresh water and the bicarbonate and boil for an hour or ninety minutes, until they collapse. Skim off the foam and the floating skins.
Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water. Rub the chickpeas between your palms under cold water and the remaining skins float free.
Blend the tahini with the garlic, lemon juice and salt — it pales and thickens. Add the iced water and blend again: it turns light and aerated.
Add the warm chickpeas with the cumin and blend for at least three minutes, loosening with the cooking water. Three minutes is not an exaggeration; that is where the texture comes from.
Spread it on a plate, sweep a channel round it with the back of a spoon, flood it with olive oil and dust with cumin.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Feijoada
description: Black beans stewed with several cuts of smoked and salted pork, served with orange and greens. (Feijoada)
instructions: Boil the salted meat in fresh water for twenty minutes and drain: the last stage of getting the salt out.
Cover the beans with water three fingers above, add the bay, the ribs and the salted meat, and simmer for an hour and a half.
Add the belly and the sausage and give it another hour. The beans should be collapsing and the liquid thickening on its own.
Fry the onion and garlic until golden, add a ladle of beans, mash them and return it all to the pot. That thickens the stew and deepens it.
Fry the greens over a high flame for two minutes with garlic — they should stay bright green and crisp.
Serve the beans and meat with the rice, greens and orange segments alongside. Everyone builds their own plate.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pão de queijo
description: Cheese balls of tapioca starch — a crust outside, a stretchy hollow inside. No wheat and no yeast. (Pão de queijo)
instructions: Bring the milk, water, oil and salt to just below boiling.
Pour all the hot liquid into the starch at once and stir with a spatula. The mixture looks lumpy and odd; that is correct. Let it cool to warm.
Work in the eggs one at a time, then both cheeses. Knead to an even sticky mass — hands are easier than a spoon.
With wet hands roll walnut-sized balls and space them three centimetres apart on a tray.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes until golden. Do not open the door for the first fifteen: the steam escapes and they collapse.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pad krapow
description: Minced pork fried with chilli, garlic and holy basil. Five minutes from start to plate. (ผัดกะเพรา)
instructions: Pound the garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar. A mortar gives a different result from a knife: the juices come out and reach the oil.
Mix the oyster, fish and soy sauces with the sugar in a cup — there will be no time once the pan is hot.
Heat the wok with two spoons of oil, throw in the paste and fry for twenty seconds, to the smell.
Add the pork and leave it alone for a minute, then break it up and fry two minutes more. Pour in the sauce and let it coat the meat.
Off the heat, stir in the basil — the residual heat wilts it in seconds. In the same pan fry the eggs in the rest of the oil until the edges go lacy.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gyudon
description: Thinly sliced beef simmered with onion in dashi, soy and mirin, over rice. (牛丼)

ingredients.text: Beni shoga pickled ginger, to taste

instructions: Bring the dashi with the soy, mirin, sake, sugar and grated ginger to the boil in a wide pan.
Add the onion and simmer for five minutes over medium heat, until it turns translucent.
Lay the beef over the surface slice by slice rather than in a heap, and cook two or three minutes. Skim any foam.
Take it off the moment the beef loses its pink. Left longer it toughens within a minute.
Divide the rice between bowls, spoon the beef and onion over with two or three spoons of the broth, and serve with the pickled ginger.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Meat solyanka
description: A soup on strong stock with several meats, brined cucumbers, olives and lemon. (Солянка)

ingredients.text: Soured cream and herbs, to taste

instructions: Make a stock from the beef and the smoked ribs: an hour and a half at a bare simmer, skimming. Lift the meat out and pull it apart.
Fry the onion until soft, add the tomato paste and cook three minutes, until it darkens and stops smelling raw.
Add the cucumbers and cook them with the onion for five minutes, so they do not stay hard in the finished soup.
Put the fried mixture, the pulled meat, the sausage and the ham into the stock, pour in the brine and simmer for fifteen minutes.
Add the olives and capers, warm for five minutes and take it off. Check the salt only now: the brine and the smoked meat have already seasoned it.
In the bowl: a slice of lemon, soured cream and herbs. The lemon goes into the bowl rather than the pot, where boiling would turn it bitter.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chicken tagine with preserved lemon
description: Chicken braised with preserved lemons and olives. The sourness comes from the peel, not the flesh. (طاجين الدجاج)
instructions: Grind the garlic, ginger, turmeric, saffron, chopped herbs, oil, salt and pepper into a paste. Rub it over the chicken and leave it an hour.
Spread the onion in an even layer over the base of the tagine or a heavy pan: it keeps the chicken off the bottom and becomes part of the sauce.
Set the chicken on top skin up, pour the water down the side, cover and cook over a low flame for forty minutes without lifting the lid.
Add the preserved lemon peel in strips and the olives, cover and give it twenty minutes more.
Take the lid off and reduce the sauce for five minutes if it is still loose. Check the salt only at the end: the lemon and olives have already provided it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Harira
description: A thick soup of lentils, chickpeas and tomato, bound with a flour slurry and finished with lemon. (حريرة)
instructions: Fry the lamb with the onion, ginger and cinnamon for five minutes, add the chopped celery and herbs and give it two more.
Add the grated tomato and the chickpeas, pour in two litres of water and simmer for an hour, until the chickpeas are soft.
Add the lentils and give it twenty minutes more.
Whisk the flour into a cup of cold water until completely smooth and pour it in as a thin stream, stirring without stopping. Cook five minutes: the soup thickens and turns matt.
Add the vermicelli and cook until done. Serve with lemon and dates — that pairing is not accidental: sweet and sour at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Goulash
description: Beef stewed with onion and paprika. There is as much onion by weight as meat, and it dissolves into the sauce. (Gulyás)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Beef shin or shoulder (in 3 cm cubes)

instructions: Sweat the onion in the lard over a low flame for twenty minutes, until soft and golden. It feels long and pointless, and it is where the sweetness of the sauce comes from.
Take the pan off the heat, add the paprika and caraway and stir. Half a minute later return it to the flame and add the meat.
Cook the meat with the onion covered for half an hour without adding water: it gives up its own. Only then pour in water to the level of the meat.
Simmer for an hour and a half. Add the peppers, tomatoes and garlic forty minutes before the end, the potatoes twenty-five.
Salt it at the very end and let it stand fifteen minutes before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lángos
description: A yeasted flatbread deep-fried, rubbed with garlic and buried under soured cream and cheese. (Lángos)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Mix the flour, mashed potato, salt and the yeast liquid and knead for eight minutes to a smooth soft dough. It stays a little tacky; that is right.
Cover and prove for an hour in the warm: the dough should double.
Divide into four, stretch each by hand into a twenty-centimetre round, leaving the edges thicker.
Deep-fry at 175 °C for ninety seconds a side. It balloons; that is correct, do not press it down.
Rub the hot bread with a cut clove of garlic, spread it with soured cream and pile on the cheese.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fish and chips
description: Cod in beer batter with twice-fried chips. The batter lives on cold and on the gas in the beer. (Fish and chips)
instructions: Rinse the cut potatoes of their starch, dry them thoroughly and fry at 140 °C for six minutes. They should turn soft but stay pale. Set them aside to cool.
Mix the flour, cornflour and baking powder. Pour in the ice-cold beer and whisk only a few strokes — lumps are fine, an over-mixed batter turns tough.
Dry the fish, dust it in plain flour and shake off the excess. Without that the batter slides off in the oil.
Heat the oil to 190 °C. Dip the fish, let the excess run off and lower it in, holding it for a couple of seconds so it does not stick to the bottom. Fry six minutes.
Lift the fish out and finish the chips in the same oil for three minutes, until gold. Salt them at once, while hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shepherd's pie
description: Lamb in a thick gravy under mashed potato, baked to a browned crust. (Shepherd's pie)
instructions: Fry the mince over a high flame, leaving it alone for the first minute so it takes dark colour. Lift it out, pouring off the excess fat.
In the same pan fry the onion and carrot for eight minutes, add the flour and tomato paste and cook two minutes.
Return the meat, pour in the stock and Worcestershire, add the thyme and cook uncovered for twenty minutes, until the gravy is thick.
Boil the potatoes and mash them with the butter and hot milk until smooth, seasoning generously. The mash should be firm rather than pourable.
Stir the peas into the meat, put it in a dish, cover with the mash and score the top with a fork.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes until browned. Let it stand ten minutes before cutting.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Wiener Schnitzel
description: Veal beaten to three millimetres, crumbed and fried in plenty of fat until the coating puffs away. (Wiener Schnitzel)
instructions: Beat the meat between two sheets of film to three millimetres. Use the flat side of the mallet, not the toothed one: teeth tear the fibres.
Beat the eggs to an even liquid without foam. Salt the meat and coat it in flour, then egg, then crumbs.
Do not press the crumbs on. The coating has to sit loosely; only then will it lift and puff.
Heat a centimetre of fat to 170 °C and lower the schnitzel in. Fry two minutes, swirling the pan the whole time so fat washes over the top.
Turn it and give it ninety seconds more, to gold. Drain on a rack and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Apfelstrudel
description: Apples with cinnamon and raisins in a dough stretched until it is transparent. It is pulled by hand, never rolled. (Apfelstrudel)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, oil and a pinch of salt for ten minutes, until smooth and very elastic. Oil it, cover it and leave it an hour.
Fry the breadcrumbs in half the butter until golden. Mix the apples with the sugar, cinnamon, raisins, lemon juice and zest.
Spread a cloth on the table, dust it with flour and stretch the dough with the backs of your hands from the centre outwards, until it is transparent. Trim the thick edges.
Brush the dough with melted butter, scatter the crumbs over a third of it and pile the apples onto them, leaving a border.
Roll it up by lifting the cloth — by hand the dough tears. Tuck the ends under, move it seam down onto a tray and brush with butter.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes, brushing with butter twice along the way. Serve warm, dusted with icing sugar.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bacalhau à brás
description: Salt cod with matchstick potatoes and egg that binds everything without becoming an omelette. (Bacalhau à Brás)

ingredients.text: 500 g Salt cod (soaked for a day)

instructions: Poach the soaked cod for five minutes, cool it and pull it into flakes by hand, discarding skin and bones. By hand rather than with a fork: that is how small bones are found.
Deep-fry the potato matchsticks at 180 °C to a crisp gold, in batches. Drain on a rack and salt them.
In a wide pan sweat the onion in the olive oil for ten minutes until soft and sweet, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the cod and warm it through for three minutes, then tip in the potato and toss.
Take the pan off the heat, pour in the beaten eggs and stir without stopping for half a minute, until they turn creamy. Scatter over the parsley and olives.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pastel de nata
description: Flaky pastry cases of custard baked in extreme heat until the surface blisters black. (Pastel de nata)
instructions: Boil the sugar and water to 100 °C and take it off. Separately bring the milk, cream, cinnamon and lemon peel to just below boiling.
Whisk the flour into a little cold milk until smooth and stir it into the hot mixture. Cook, stirring, to the thickness of soured cream.
Pour the hot syrup into the milk base in a thin stream, take it off the heat and stir in the yolks. Strain it and cool completely.
Roll the pastry into a tight log, cut two-centimetre discs and press each into a tin with your thumbs, taking the walls above the rim.
Heat the oven as high as it goes, at least 250 °C. Fill the cases three-quarters full and bake twelve to fifteen minutes, until the tops blister black.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Argentinian empanadas
description: Pastries of chopped beef, onion and egg. The filling is chilled cold, or the dough will not seal. (Empanadas argentinas)
instructions: Fry the onion in the lard over medium heat for fifteen minutes, until soft and translucent, without letting it colour.
Add the chopped beef, paprika, cumin and chilli and cook five minutes: the meat should only lose its pink, no more.
Season, take it off the heat and cool it completely, then refrigerate for at least four hours.
Fold the chopped egg, olives and spring onion into the cold filling.
Put a tablespoon of filling on each disc, wet the rim, fold it over and crimp it into the plaited repulgue, folding the corners over one another.
Brush with yolk and bake at 220 °C for twenty minutes, until browned.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chimichurri
description: A sauce of parsley, oregano, garlic and vinegar. A knife rather than a blender: texture matters more than smoothness. (Chimichurri)
instructions: Dissolve the salt in the warm water: that spreads it evenly instead of leaving it on the bottom of the jar.
Rub the dried oregano between your palms and steep it in the vinegar for five minutes: it softens and releases its scent.
Chop the parsley and garlic fine with a knife. The garlic is chopped rather than crushed: crushed it gives a sharpness that never leaves.
Mix everything together, pour in the oil and stir. Let it stand two hours at room temperature.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nasi goreng
description: Fried rice with a chilli and shrimp-paste base, sweet soy sauce and an egg on top. (Nasi goreng)

ingredients.text: 600 g Cooked rice (cold, from the day before)
Cucumber and fried shallots, to taste

instructions: Pound the shallot, garlic, chilli and terasi to a paste in a mortar. It smells aggressive; that is correct, frying softens it.
Heat the wok and fry the paste in the oil for two minutes, until it darkens and the smell turns deep.
Add the chicken and fry three minutes, then the prawns and cabbage for two more.
Tip in the cold rice, breaking up the lumps with the spatula, pour in the kecap manis and fry over a high flame for three minutes, tossing constantly.
Fry the eggs separately until the edges are lacy and the yolks loose. Serve the rice with an egg on top, slices of cucumber and fried shallots.

image.credit: shankar s. from Dubai, united arab emirates

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rendang
description: Beef simmered in coconut milk for four hours, until the milk turns to oil and starts frying the meat. (Rendang)
instructions: Soak the dried chillies in boiling water for fifteen minutes, then blend them with the shallot, garlic, galangal, ginger and turmeric to a smooth paste.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan until deep brown and pound it to an oily paste — this is kerisik, and it brings the nutty depth.
Fry the paste in a wide pot for five minutes, add the meat, coconut milk, bruised lemongrass and lime leaves, and bring it to the boil.
Simmer uncovered for two and a half hours, stirring every twenty minutes. The sauce gradually thickens and darkens.
Stir in the kerisik and carry on over medium heat for another hour, stirring more and more often. The milk splits, the oil separates and the meat begins to fry.
It is done when the meat is dark brown and nearly dry and the oil runs clear. Season and let it rest.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chicken adobo
description: Chicken braised in soy sauce with vinegar, garlic and bay. The vinegar is left unstirred for the first ten minutes. (Adobo)
instructions: Marinate the chicken in the soy with the crushed garlic and peppercorns for thirty minutes.
Lift the chicken out, dry it and brown it skin down. Keep the marinade.
Pour in the marinade, water and vinegar, add the bay and sugar. Bring it to the boil and neither stir nor cover for ten minutes.
Cover and simmer for twenty-five minutes, turning the chicken once.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for five to ten minutes, spooning it over the chicken. Serve with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sinigang
description: A sour tamarind soup with pork and vegetables. Sourness is the main flavour here, not an accent. (Sinigang)
instructions: Cover the ribs with water, bring to the boil, skim and simmer for an hour with the onion and tomatoes.
Crush the softened tomatoes in the pot: they give the broth its body.
Add the tamarind paste and fish sauce, then taste. The sourness should be pronounced, not a hint.
Add the taro and daikon and cook ten minutes, then the aubergine and beans for five more.
Throw in the greens and chillies and take the pot off after thirty seconds. The greens should stay bright.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ukrainian borscht with pampushky
description: Borscht on pork ribs with aged salo crushed with garlic, and garlic pampushky alongside. (Український борщ)
instructions: Make a stock from the ribs: an hour and a half at a bare simmer, skimmed. Lift the meat out and pull it apart.
Braise the beetroot separately with a spoon of oil, the tomato paste and the vinegar, covered, for twenty minutes. The vinegar is what holds the colour.
Fry the onion and carrot until soft. Put the potatoes into the stock and give them ten minutes, before any acid reaches the pot.
Add the cabbage, then after five minutes the beetroot, the fried vegetables and the beans. Give it five minutes.
Pound the salo with the garlic and herbs to a paste and stir it into the pot. Take it straight off the heat and let it stand covered for twenty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Cherry varenyky
description: Dumplings of whole cherries and sugar. The juice stays inside if the fruit is tossed in starch first. (Вареники з вишнями)
instructions: Mix the kefir with the bicarbonate and leave it five minutes, until it bubbles. Add the egg, salt and flour and knead for eight minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it half an hour. Meanwhile let the cherries drain in a colander.
Mix the starch with the sugar and toss the cherries in it right before shaping.
Roll the dough to two millimetres, cut discs, put three or four cherries on each and seal the rim dry, pressing the air out.
Boil in batches in a wide pot of salted water. Two minutes after they float, lift them out and butter them at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Svíčková na smetaně
description: Beef in a purée of root vegetables with cream, served with dumplings, lingonberry and lemon. (Svíčková na smetaně)
instructions: Lard the beef with strips of smoked fat laid along the grain. Bury it in the grated roots with the spices and vinegar and refrigerate for a day.
Dry the meat and brown it in butter on all sides. Lift it out.
In the same pan fry the roots from the marinade with the onion for twenty minutes: they should darken noticeably, which is where the colour comes from.
Return the meat, pour in the marinade and enough water to reach the vegetables, and braise covered for two hours over a low flame.
Take the meat out, remove the bay and blend the vegetables with the liquid until smooth. Pass it through a sieve: this is the step that separates a home svíčková from a restaurant one.
Stir in the cream, lemon juice and sugar, warm it without boiling and taste. Carve the meat across the grain and serve with the sauce, lingonberry and a slice of lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Trdelník
description: A ribbon of yeasted dough wound round a spit, baked and rolled in sugar and nuts. (Trdelník)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and let it foam for ten minutes.
Knead a dough from the flour, the yeast liquid, eggs, sugar and salt for ten minutes, then work in the soft butter piece by piece. Prove for an hour.
Roll the dough out and cut two-centimetre ribbons. Butter the spits and roll them in sugar.
Wind a ribbon round each spit, overlapping by a third and pulling it slightly taut. Roll it on the table so the layers bond.
Brush with butter, roll in the sugar, nut and cinnamon mixture and bake at 190 °C for eighteen minutes, turning every five.
Let it cool three minutes and twist it off the spit. Hot, it tears; fully cooled, it sticks.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Köttbullar
description: Meatballs on a panade of bread and cream, in a cream sauce, with lingonberry and mashed potato. (Köttbullar)
instructions: Soak the bread in a hundred millilitres of the cream for ten minutes and mash it to a paste.
Fry the onion in butter until soft and cool it completely: warm onion starts cooking the meat.
Mix both minces with the panade, onion, egg, allspice and salt, and work it for five minutes until tacky.
Roll walnut-sized balls with wet hands and fry them in butter in batches, shaking the pan so they roll and colour evenly.
In the same pan whisk the flour into the remaining fat, pour in the stock and the rest of the cream, add the soy and cook five minutes to a sauce.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and warm them through for five minutes. Serve with mashed potato, lingonberry and pickled cucumber.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kanelbullar
description: Cinnamon buns knotted rather than rolled. The cardamom in the dough matters more than the cinnamon inside. (Kanelbullar)
instructions: Warm the milk to thirty-seven degrees and dissolve the yeast. Mix with the flour, sugar, salt and cardamom and knead for ten minutes.
Work in the soft butter piece by piece until the dough turns smooth and glossy. Prove for an hour.
Beat the butter with the sugar and cinnamon to a paste. Roll the dough into a half-centimetre rectangle and spread the filling over all of it.
Fold the sheet in three, cut two-centimetre strips, twist each one and tie it in a knot. Space them on a tray.
Prove them for forty minutes, brush with egg and scatter with pearl sugar.
Bake at 220 °C for twelve minutes. Short and hot is what keeps the middle moist.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Koshari
description: Rice, lentils and pasta in one bowl under a vinegary tomato sauce and fried onion. (كشري)
instructions: Fry the onion in the oil over medium heat for twenty-five minutes to a deep brown, stirring. Drain it on paper; it crisps as it cools.
Boil the lentils for twenty minutes to soft but not collapsing, and drain.
Cook the rice in the onion oil: fry it two minutes, add water at one and a half to one and cook covered for fifteen minutes.
Boil the pasta and drain it. For the sauce, fry the garlic in a spoon of oil to gold, pour in the vinegar and let it reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes, cumin and chilli and cook twenty minutes to a thick sauce. Season.
Build it in the bowl in layers: rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas, sauce, fried onion. The mixing happens at the table.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ful medames
description: Fava beans stewed to a cream with olive oil, lemon and cumin. (فول مدمس)
instructions: Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water three fingers above and bring to the boil. Skim.
Drop to the lowest possible heat and cook covered for three or four hours, until the beans start to collapse. Top up the water as needed.
Mash about half the beans in the pot with a masher, leaving the rest whole.
Stir in the crushed garlic and season. Divide between bowls.
Into each bowl: olive oil generously, lemon juice, cumin, tomato, parsley and chilli to taste. Serve with flatbread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tabbouleh
description: A parsley salad with a little bulgur in it, not the other way round. There is ten times more herb than grain. (تبولة)
instructions: Rinse the bulgur and pour the juice of one lemon over it. Leave it to swell for fifteen minutes.
Wash the parsley well in advance and dry it thoroughly — an hour on a cloth is not too much. Strip the thick stems and chop it fine but without pulverising it.
Dice the tomatoes small and salt them separately: the juice they give up goes into the bulgur.
Mix everything with the juice of the second lemon, the oil and the allspice. Let it stand ten minutes before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kibbeh nayyeh
description: Raw kibbeh: the freshest lamb pounded with bulgur and spices, served under olive oil. (كبة نية)

ingredients.text: 500 g Freshest lamb (loin or leg, fully trimmed)
Mint and white onion to serve, to taste

instructions: Soak the bulgur in cold water for ten minutes, drain and squeeze it dry. Chill the bowl — everything for nayyeh must stay cold.
Trim the lamb of fat and silverskin down to clean muscle and cube it. Blitz with the onion to a smooth paste without letting the bowl warm up.
Add the bulgur, spices, mint and salt. Knead, wetting your hands with iced water, until the paste is smooth and glossy.
Spread the paste over a cold plate about a centimetre and a half thick, press grooves with the back of a spoon and pour the olive oil over generously.
Serve at once, with mint leaves, white onion wedges and flatbread. Nayyeh is not kept: leftovers are fried as patties the same evening.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ghormeh sabzi
description: Lamb stewed with a mountain of herbs, beans and dried lime. The herbs are fried until nearly black. (قورمه‌سبزی)
instructions: Fry the onion with the turmeric until gold, add the meat and brown it on all sides.
Cover with water, add the beans and simmer for an hour.
Meanwhile chop all the herbs fine and fry them in the oil for twenty minutes, stirring. They shrink to a quarter and darken; that is correct. Add the fenugreek for the last two minutes.
Stir the herbs into the pot, prick the dried limes with a fork and drop them in whole. Simmer for another hour.
Crush the limes against the side of the pot, season and let it stand fifteen minutes. The sauce should be dark and thick, with oil separated on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tahdig
description: Rice with a golden crust on the bottom of the pot, made from rice, potato or flatbread. (ته‌دیگ)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it in salted water for an hour. That removes surplus starch and lets the grains grow longer.
Boil the rice in plenty of salted water for five to seven minutes: a grain should bend but snap under pressure. Drain and rinse with warm water.
Grind the saffron and steep it in two spoons of hot water. Mix a couple of spoons of the rice with the yoghurt and saffron: this becomes the crust.
Heat the fat in the pot, lay the potato rounds edge to edge, spread the rice and yoghurt mixture over them and pile the rest of the rice on top in a mound.
Make five holes down to the base with the handle of a spoon for the steam to travel. Pour melted butter over.
Cover with a lid wrapped in a cloth, five minutes on a high flame and forty-five on the lowest. Do not lift the lid.
Stand the base of the pot in cold water for a minute and the crust releases. Invert it onto a plate in one movement.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Uzbek plov
description: Rice steamed over a zirvak of lamb, carrot and onion. It is never stirred once it goes in. (Palov)

ingredients.text: 100 g Lamb tail fat (or vegetable oil)
700 g Devzira or another firm rice
700 g Yellow and red carrot (in batons)

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and cover it with warm salted water for as long as the zirvak takes.
Render the tail fat in the pot until only crackling is left and lift it out. Brown the meat hard over a high flame.
Add the onion and fry it gold, then the carrot — and leave it alone for five minutes so it sets. Then stir and fry ten minutes more.
Pour in boiling water to the level of the contents, add the chickpeas, cumin, barberries, chilli and the whole garlic bulbs. Simmer for forty minutes: this is the zirvak.
Salt the zirvak noticeably harder than seems right: the rice takes it. Spread the rice over in an even layer with a slotted spoon, without stirring, and pour boiling water two fingers above it.
Cook uncovered over a high flame until the water drops below the rice. Gather the rice into a mound, pierce it to the base in several places, cover and give it twenty minutes on the lowest heat.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Samsa
description: Flaky triangles of chopped lamb and onion, baked to a crisp shell. (Somsa)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, warm water and salt for ten minutes and rest it under film for half an hour.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet, brush it with the melted fat, roll it into a tight log and chill it for half an hour.
Mix the chopped meat with the onion, cumin and pepper. Salt it immediately before shaping, not before that.
Cut the log into two-centimetre discs, set each cut side up and roll it into a round: the layers stay visible.
Add the filling and seal into a triangle, pressing the seams firmly. Set them seam down, glaze with egg and scatter with sesame.
Bake at 220 °C for ten minutes, then drop to 190 °C for twenty-five more, to a deep gold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: New England clam chowder
description: A thick clam soup with cream, potato and bacon. No tomato — that is a matter of principle. (New England clam chowder)
instructions: Scrub the clams and steam them in a cup of water, covered, for five minutes, until they open. Discard any that stay shut. Strain the liquor through muslin: sand settles in it.
Take the meat from the shells and chop it coarsely. Set it aside; it returns at the very end.
Render the bacon in the pot, add the butter, onion and celery, and sweat them for eight minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour, cook it two minutes, pour in the strained clam liquor and the milk, and add the potato, thyme and bay.
Simmer for fifteen minutes until the potato is soft. Crush a few pieces against the side: the soup thickens without more flour.
Pour in the cream, return the clams and warm through for two minutes without boiling. Check the salt and serve with crackers.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Buffalo wings
description: Unbreaded wings in a sauce of hot pepper sauce and butter. Salt draws the moisture out before baking. (Buffalo wings)

ingredients.text: 1.2 kg Chicken wings (split at the joint)

instructions: Dry the wings with kitchen paper, salt them and leave them uncovered on a rack in the fridge for at least four hours, better overnight.
Dust with the baking powder and toss so the coating is thin and even. Too much leaves a soapy taste.
Spread them on a rack over a tray and bake at 120 °C for twenty minutes: the fat renders out.
Raise the oven to 220 °C and bake another twenty-five minutes, to a deep gold and a crisp.
Melt the butter, take it off the heat and whisk in the pepper sauce, vinegar and garlic powder to an even emulsion.
Toss the hot wings with the sauce in a bowl and serve immediately with celery and blue cheese dip.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pizza margherita
description: A long-fermented dough, uncooked tomato, mozzarella and basil. Time decides everything here, not the number of ingredients. (Pizza margherita)

ingredients.text: 300 g Fior di latte mozzarella (sliced and drained)

instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the water, add the flour and mix to a rough dough. Rest it twenty minutes, then work in the salt and knead ten minutes to a smooth ball.
Leave it two hours at room temperature, divide it into four balls and refrigerate for a day.
Take the dough out three hours before baking. Crush the tomatoes by hand with a pinch of salt: the sauce is done.
Heat the oven with a stone or steel at full power for at least an hour. It takes longer than seems necessary and it is not optional.
Stretch a ball with your fingers from the centre outwards, leaving the rim untouched. No rolling pin: it drives the air out of the rim and the crust will not rise.
Spread a thin layer of sauce, lay on the mozzarella and trickle over the oil. Bake seven to nine minutes, until the rim is spotted, and add the basil to the finished pizza.

image.credit: Dale Cruse from San Francisco, CA, USA

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lasagne alla bolognese
description: Layers of pasta, ragù and béchamel. The ragù simmers three hours on milk and wine rather than tomato. (Lasagne alla bolognese)
instructions: Render the pancetta, add the soffritto and sweat it twenty minutes over a low flame until completely soft. There is no hurrying this: the vegetables have to dissolve.
Add both minces and cook over a high flame, breaking up the lumps, until every drop of water has gone and the meat starts to brown.
Pour in the milk and let it cook away entirely, about twenty minutes. Then the wine, likewise to dryness.
Add the tomato paste and the stock, bring it to the boil and simmer three hours on the lowest heat, topping up with water as needed.
Make the béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook it a minute and pour in warm milk in a thin stream, whisking. Cook to the thickness of cream and season with nutmeg.
Build the layers: béchamel, pasta, ragù, béchamel, parmesan — six times over. The top layer is béchamel with parmesan.
Bake at 180 °C for forty minutes, the last ten uncovered. Let it stand twenty minutes before cutting.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Palak paneer
description: Spinach blanched and blended, with cubes of paneer. Spinach must not be stewed or it goes brown. (पालक पनीर)
instructions: Drop the spinach into boiling water for ninety seconds and move it straight into iced water. Squeeze it out and blend it with the chilli to a purée.
Soak the paneer in hot salted water for ten minutes, then drain it.
Fry the cumin seeds in the ghee until they crackle, add the onion and cook it gold, then the ginger and garlic for a minute.
