Add the tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they break down and the fat starts separating at the edges.
Stir in the spinach purée, garam masala and salt, and warm it for exactly a minute. Add the paneer and cream and take it off the heat.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Samosa
description: Triangles of potato and pea in a ghee-rich pastry. Fried on a moderate flame, never a fierce one. (समोसा)
instructions: Rub the ghee into the flour with the ajwain and salt until it looks like damp sand: squeezed in a fist it should hold its shape.
Add cold water a little at a time to a firm, tight dough — stiffer than a dumpling dough. Cover it and rest it half an hour.
Fry the cumin in a spoon of oil, add the chilli, spices, peas and coarsely crushed potato. Warm it five minutes and cool it.
Divide the dough into balls, roll each into an oval and cut it in half. Form a cone from each half, wetting the straight edge.
Fill the cone, pinch the top firmly shut and set it seam up. A weak seam opens in the oil.
Lower them into oil at 150 °C and fry twelve to fifteen minutes, raising it to 180 °C at the end. The pastry should carry fine blisters rather than large ones.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jiaozi dumplings
description: Pork and cabbage dumplings, fried and then steamed in the same covered pan. (饺子)

ingredients.text: Black vinegar for dipping, to taste

instructions: Knead a dough from the flour and warm water for eight minutes and rest it under film for half an hour.
Salt the shredded cabbage and leave it fifteen minutes, then squeeze it dry by hand.
Work the pork with the ginger, soy and sesame oil in one direction, trickling in the stock until the mass turns tacky. Fold in the cabbage and spring onion.
Roll eight-centimetre rounds, thinner at the edge and thicker in the middle. Add filling and pleat one side shut.
Heat the oil in a pan, set the dumplings in seam up and fry three minutes to a golden base.
Pour in a hundred millilitres of water and cover at once. After seven minutes take the lid off and let the water go, back to a crisp base.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Yangzhou fried rice
description: Rice with prawns, ham and egg, where every grain stays separate under a thin film of egg. (扬州炒饭)

ingredients.text: 600 g Cooked rice (cold, from the day before)
Salt and white pepper, to taste

instructions: Separate two yolks and rub them through the cold rice with your hands until every grain is coated. Beat the remaining eggs separately.
Heat the wok with a spoon of oil until it smokes, pour in the beaten eggs, let them set and break them into pieces. Set them aside.
Fry the prawns for ninety seconds, add the ham, carrot and peas and cook a minute more. Add them to the eggs.
Add the rest of the oil, tip in the rice and fry three minutes at full heat, tossing constantly. The grains should be jumping in the wok, not sitting in it.
Return everything to the wok, pour the wine down the side and add the soy, season and toss for thirty seconds more. Scatter over the spring onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chiles rellenos
description: Poblano peppers stuffed with cheese in an airy egg batter, fried and served under tomato sauce. (Chiles rellenos)
instructions: Char the peppers over a flame or under a grill until blistered black all over, close them in a bag for ten minutes and peel the skin away.
Make a lengthways slit, ease the seeds out leaving the stalk in place, stuff with cheese and pin the slit with a cocktail stick.
For the sauce, blend the tomatoes with the onion and garlic, fry the purée in a spoon of oil for ten minutes with the oregano, and season.
Whip the whites to firm peaks, add a pinch of salt and fold in the yolks one at a time, trying not to knock the air out.
Dust a pepper in flour, dip it in the batter and lower it into oil at 180 °C. Fry two minutes a side, spooning oil over the top.
Drain on a rack, remove the sticks and serve with the hot tomato sauce beneath the pepper rather than over it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pozole rojo
description: A soup of pork and hominy in a dried chilli broth, with a pile of fresh garnishes on the table. (Pozole rojo)

ingredients.text: Radish, cabbage, lime, onion, to taste

instructions: Cover the pork with water, add half the onion, three cloves of garlic and the bay, and simmer two hours, skimming.
Seed the chillies, toast them in a dry pan twenty seconds a side and cover them with boiling water for twenty minutes.
Blend the chillies with the remaining onion, garlic and a cup of the broth, and pass the result through a sieve without fail.
Fry the strained sauce in a spoon of fat for five minutes: it darkens and thickens. Pour it into the pot with the meat.
Add the rinsed hominy and the oregano and cook another forty minutes. Pull the meat into shreds and return it.
Serve with bowls of sliced radish, cabbage, onion, lime wedges, oregano and tostadas. Everyone builds their own bowl.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nihari
description: Beef shin stewed overnight in a thick spiced gravy with marrow, bound with a wheat-flour slurry. (نہاری)

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, star anise
Lemon, ginger, coriander, chilli, to taste

instructions: Fry the onions in ghee to a deep gold, about twenty minutes. Set half aside for serving.
Add the ginger and garlic, the spices and the chilli, warm them a minute, then the meat and bones, and sear until the raw colour goes.
Cover with water three fingers above, bring to the boil, skim and cook on the lowest heat for four or five hours. The meat should fall apart at a touch.
Whisk the flour into a cup of cold water until smooth and pour it in as a thin stream, stirring constantly. Cook ten minutes: the gravy thickens and turns glossy.
Lift out the bones and set the marrow aside separately. Serve with the fried onion, matchsticks of ginger, coriander, green chilli and lemon — everyone adds their own.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chapli kebab
description: Flat beef patties with cornmeal, tomato and whole coriander seeds. (چپلی کباب)
instructions: Mix the mince with the cornmeal, egg, onion, chilli, coriander leaf, crushed coriander seed, pomegranate seeds and salt.
Fold in the tomatoes last so they do not weep too early, and chill the mixture for twenty minutes.
With wet hands shape flat patties twelve centimetres across and a centimetre thick.
Heat half a centimetre of ghee and fry them three or four minutes a side over medium heat, uncovered.
Serve with flatbread, onion rings and lemon. Traditionally an egg is broken over each patty in the pan.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Laksa lemak
description: Noodles in a coconut broth built on a rempah paste, with prawns and tofu. The paste is fried until the oil separates. (Laksa lemak)

ingredients.text: Bean sprouts, cucumber, lime, to taste

instructions: Soak the dried chillies in boiling water for fifteen minutes, then blend them with the shallots, lemongrass, galangal, turmeric and belacan to a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat for fifteen minutes, stirring. It is ready when the oil starts separating and rising at the edges.
Pour in the stock, bring it to the boil and simmer ten minutes. Add the prawns and tofu for three minutes.
Add the coconut milk and warm it through without letting it boil hard. Season.
Divide the cooked noodles between bowls, ladle the broth over and serve the sprouts, cucumber and lime alongside.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Roti canai
description: A flatbread stretched translucent and crumpled before frying. The layers come from air rather than butter. (Roti canai)

ingredients.text: 150 ml Neutral oil (for resting the dough)

instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water, egg, condensed milk and salt for fifteen minutes, until it is very elastic and smooth.
Divide into balls, coat each in oil and set them in a bowl covered with more oil. Leave them at least four hours.
On an oiled surface flatten a ball and stretch it from the centre, slapping it with your palms until the sheet turns translucent.
Brush the sheet with ghee, fold the edges to the middle and coil it into a tight spiral. Let it sit ten minutes.
Flatten the spiral into a round and fry it on medium heat, two minutes a side in ghee, until it takes golden spots.
Straight from the pan, crumple the bread between your palms from both sides and the layers open. Serve with dhal or curry.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Stamppot
description: Mashed potato crushed together with curly kale, with smoked sausage and a well of gravy. (Stamppot boerenkool)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for twenty minutes. Seven minutes before the end pile the kale on top to steam.
Meanwhile warm the sausage in water for twenty minutes without letting it boil: boiling splits the skin and the fat leaves.
Render the bacon until crisp and set it aside, keeping the fat.
Drain, crush the potato and kale together with a masher, working in the hot milk, butter, bacon fat and mustard.
Fold in the crackling, divide between plates, make a well and fill it with gravy. Slice the sausage and lay it over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Poffertjes
description: Tiny yeasted pancakes of buckwheat and wheat flour, served with butter and icing sugar. (Poffertjes)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in half the warm milk and let it foam for ten minutes.
Mix both flours with the salt, pour in the yeast liquid, the egg and the rest of the milk, and whisk smooth.
Cover and leave it an hour in the warm. The batter turns bubbly and roughly doubles.
Heat a poffertjes pan or an ordinary one, butter it and spoon batter into the hollows without stirring what is left in the bowl.
After a minute, when the edges set, turn them with a fork and give them forty seconds more.
Serve them hot with a knob of butter on top and a generous dusting of icing sugar.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Doro wat
description: Chicken in a thick berbere sauce, built on a kilo of onion cooked dry until it disintegrates. (ዶሮ ወጥ)
instructions: Marinate the chicken in lemon juice and salt for half an hour.
Cook the onion in a dry pot over medium heat for forty minutes, stirring. It weeps, reduces and turns into a dark paste. Add neither oil nor water.
Add the spiced butter, garlic and ginger, cook five minutes, then stir in the berbere and fry five more: the spices have to open in the fat.
Pour in the wine and a cup of water, add the chicken and braise covered for forty minutes over a low flame.
Score the boiled eggs in several places and slip them into the sauce for the last ten minutes.
Serve with injera. The sauce should be thick and dark red, with oil separated on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Misir wat
description: Red lentils in a berbere sauce. A fasting dish eaten in Ethiopia on fast days all year round. (ምስር ወጥ)
instructions: Cook the onion dry in a pot for thirty minutes over medium heat, stirring, until it becomes a dark paste.
Pour in the oil, add the garlic and ginger and cook three minutes.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste and fry five minutes: the mixture darkens and turns fragrant.
Add the lentils, pour in the water and simmer twenty-five minutes, stirring, until the lentils fall apart.
Season at the end, cook it down to a porridge-thick stew and serve with injera or flatbread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ropa vieja
description: Beef pulled into strands and stewed in sofrito with peppers and olives. The meat is boiled whole in advance. (Ropa vieja)
instructions: Boil the beef whole in salted water with an onion for an hour and a half, until it pulls apart. Keep the broth.
Cool it and pull it apart along the grain into thin strands by hand.
Sweat the onion and peppers in the olive oil for twenty minutes to complete softness, then add the garlic, cumin and oregano for a minute.
Pour in the wine, reduce it by half, add the tomatoes and a cup of the broth. Simmer ten minutes.
Return the meat, add the olives and capers and cook another twenty minutes over a low flame. Serve with rice and fried plantain.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Moros y cristianos
description: Rice cooked in the liquid from black beans, which darkens it and gives it all their flavour. (Moros y cristianos)
instructions: Boil the beans in three litres of water with the bay for an hour, to nearly done. Do not drain: the liquor is the base of the dish.
Fry the onion and pepper in the olive oil for fifteen minutes until soft, adding the garlic, cumin and oregano for a minute.
Measure the bean liquor: two parts liquid to one part rice by volume. Top up with water if there is not enough.
Combine the rice, beans, liquor, half the sofrito and the vinegar, season and bring it to the boil.
Lower the heat, cover and cook twenty minutes without lifting the lid. Let it stand ten minutes and fork the rest of the sofrito through.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jerk chicken
description: Chicken in a marinade of scotch bonnet and allspice, smoked over pimento wood. (Jerk chicken)
instructions: Blend the chillies, allspice, spring onion, thyme, ginger, garlic, soy, lime juice, sugar, nutmeg and oil into a thick paste.
Cut deep slashes into the chicken down to the bone and rub the marinade in with gloved hands, filling the cuts.
Refrigerate for at least eight hours, better a full day.
Bank the coals to one side of the grill and throw soaked allspice berries and wood chips on them. Put the chicken on the far side, away from direct heat.
Cook covered at 150-160 °C for an hour and a half, turning every half hour and adding more chips.
For the last ten minutes move it over direct heat for colour. Serve with lime and festival bread.

image.credit: Marie from Malang, East Java, Indonesia

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ackee and saltfish
description: Jamaica's national dish: ackee fruit, which looks and behaves like scrambled egg, with soaked salt cod. (Ackee and saltfish)
instructions: Boil the soaked cod for twenty minutes, drain, cool it and flake it, discarding skin and bones.
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil for eight minutes, add the thyme and the whole scotch bonnet: uncut, it gives aroma without heat.
Add the cod and tomatoes and cook through for five minutes.
Tip in the ackee, add black pepper and warm it two minutes, swirling the pan only. No spatula.
Lift out the chilli and serve with fried plantain, bread or boiled ground provisions.

image.credit: gailf548 from New York State, USA

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jollof rice
description: Rice cooked in a thick sauce of tomato, pepper and onion. The sauce is reduced dark before the rice goes in. (Jollof rice)
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, peppers, one onion and the scotch bonnet until smooth.
Fry the second onion in the oil until soft, add the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Pour in the purée and reduce it for twenty-five minutes over medium heat, stirring. It darkens, thickens and the oil begins separating at the edges.
Add the curry powder, thyme, bay and stock, season and bring it to the boil.
Stir in the rinsed rice once, cover with foil and a lid, and cook on the lowest heat for twenty-five minutes. Do not lift the lid or stir.
Take it off and let it stand ten minutes. Fork it through from the bottom up, lifting the lower layer.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Suya
description: Beef skewers in a ground peanut and spice rub, applied twice — before and after grilling. (Suya)

ingredients.text: Onion, tomato, cabbage to serve, to taste

instructions: Grind the peanuts to a fine crumb, wrap them in a cloth and press hard: the oil stays on the cloth and the powder comes out dry.
Mix the peanut powder with the ginger, garlic, cayenne, paprika, crumbled stock cube and salt: this is the yaji.
Oil the strips of beef and coat them in half the rub. Leave them half an hour.
Thread the meat onto skewers in waves so the heat gets between the folds, and grill it over a fierce fire two or three minutes a side.
Dust the hot meat with the other half of the rub and serve with onion rings, tomato and cabbage.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Arepas
description: Cakes of precooked corn flour, griddled and split open to be stuffed. (Arepas)
instructions: Dissolve the salt in the warm water and stir in the flour by hand. Add the butter and cheese.
Knead for three minutes and let it stand five. The dough should stop sticking and roll into a ball easily.
Shape cakes ten centimetres across and a centimetre and a half thick. Smooth the edges with wet fingers; cracks widen in the pan.
Griddle them with a drop of oil for four minutes a side, to a firm crust.
Finish them at 180 °C for ten minutes. A done arepa sounds hollow when tapped.
Split them hot lengthways, not all the way through, and stuff them: cheese, avocado, stewed meat or egg.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ajiaco bogotano
description: A chicken soup on three kinds of potato with guascas herb, capers and cream. (Ajiaco bogotano)

ingredients.text: 800 g Chicken breasts on the bone

instructions: Poach the chicken in two and a half litres of water with the spring onion and coriander for forty minutes. Lift it out and shred it; strain the broth.
Return the broth to the pot, add the small yellow potatoes and cook twenty minutes, until they collapse entirely and thicken the soup.
Add the other two potato varieties and the corn and cook twenty minutes more.
Add the guascas five minutes before the end: boiled long, they turn bitter.
Return the chicken, season, and serve with bowls of cream, capers and sliced avocado on the table.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Quiche lorraine
description: A shortcrust base with bacon and a cream and egg custard. No cheese and no onion — the classical recipe has neither. (Quiche lorraine)
instructions: Cut the cold butter into the flour with a pinch of salt to a crumb, add the egg and iced water and bring the dough together without kneading. Chill it an hour.
Roll the pastry out, line the tin, prick it and chill it again for twenty minutes: that is what stops it shrinking.
Line it with paper and weights and blind-bake at 190 °C for fifteen minutes, then remove the weights and give it five minutes more, to a dry base.
Render the bacon until browned and drain it on paper: spare fat splits the custard.
Whisk the eggs with the cream and milk without foaming, and season with nutmeg and pepper. It barely needs salt: the bacon is salty.
Scatter the bacon over the base, pour the custard in and bake at 170 °C for thirty-five minutes. The centre should still wobble slightly when it comes out.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Croissant
description: A laminated yeasted dough with twenty-seven layers of butter. Temperature decides everything: dough and butter must be equally cold. (Croissant)
instructions: Mix the flour, cold milk, yeast, sugar, salt and softened butter for five minutes. No longer: strong gluten fights the rolling later.
Flatten the dough into a rectangle, wrap it and refrigerate at least four hours, better overnight.
Beat the cold butter with a rolling pin into a centimetre-thick square and keep it cold. It should bend without cracking or melting.
Roll the dough to twice the size of the butter square, lay the butter in the middle and fold the edges over it like an envelope, sealing the seams.
Roll it into a long rectangle and fold it in three. Chill forty minutes. Repeat twice more — three folds in all.
Roll the dough to four millimetres, cut triangles with a ten-centimetre base and roll each from the base to the tip, stretching gently.
Prove two hours at 25 °C — no warmer, or the butter runs out. Glaze with egg and bake at 200 °C for eighteen minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tempura
description: Vegetables and prawns in an ice-cold lumpy batter. Whisking it smooth is exactly what must not happen. (天ぷら)

ingredients.text: 500 g Sweet potato, aubergine, pumpkin, pepper (sliced)

instructions: Score the prawns three times on the inner curve and straighten them slightly, so they do not curl into rings in the oil.
Combine the dashi, soy and mirin, bring them to the boil and take them off: this is tentsuyu. Serve it with grated daikon.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Only when it is ready do you mix the batter — not before.
Beat the cold egg into the iced water, tip in the flour and cornflour and stir with chopsticks for five or six strokes. Leave the lumps.
Dust the pieces in dry flour, dip them in the batter and lower them in three or four at a time. Fry ninety seconds to two minutes.
Drain on a rack, never on paper. Between batches skim the floating scraps of batter out of the oil: they burn and taint the flavour.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Okonomiyaki
description: A thick cabbage pancake where the batter only binds. Yam in the batter gives it the airy texture. (お好み焼き)
instructions: Mix the flour, grated yam and dashi and rest it half an hour in the fridge: the batter comes together better.
Fold the eggs into the batter, then the cabbage, spring onion and tenkasu. Fold from underneath and briefly: the cabbage must not start weeping.
Mound a quarter of the mixture onto a hot pan in a fifteen-centimetre round and do not flatten it: the air inside is wanted.
Lay slices of pork belly on top and cook five minutes covered over medium heat.
Turn it with two spatulas in one decisive movement and cook five minutes more, this time uncovered.
Brush with okonomi sauce, pipe lines of mayonnaise and drag a cocktail stick across them. Scatter over katsuobushi and aonori.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lahmacun
description: A paper-thin flatbread with lamb and pepper paste, baked three minutes in a screaming oven. (Lahmacun)

ingredients.text: Lemon and herbs to serve, to taste

instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water, yeast and salt for eight minutes and prove it an hour.
Blend the onion, pepper and tomato and press the purée through a sieve: the spare water is not wanted.
Mix the lamb with the vegetable purée, the pepper paste, chopped parsley, flakes and salt. It should be as thick as a pâté.
Heat the oven with a stone at full power for forty minutes.
Roll the balls of dough paper-thin, twenty-five centimetres across, and spread the topping thinly right to the edges.
Bake on the stone three or four minutes. The edges should colour and the middle stay soft: a lahmacun is rolled up to eat.

image.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Rainer Zenz assumed (based on copyright claims).

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Baklava
description: Forty layers of yufka with pistachio, soaked in syrup. Hot baklava takes cold syrup, and only that way round. (Baklava)
instructions: Make the syrup: bring the sugar and water to the boil, cook fifteen minutes, add the lemon juice and cool it completely.
Melt the butter and let it settle — use only the clear upper layer and discard the sediment.
Lay twenty sheets into a greased tin, brushing each with butter. Scatter the pistachios in an even layer.
Cover with twenty more sheets, brushing each in the same way. Butter the top sheet especially generously.
Cut it into diamonds with a sharp knife, right down to the base of the tin.
Bake at 170 °C for an hour, to a deep gold. Take it out and pour the cold syrup into the cuts at once.
Leave it six hours, better overnight. Cutting and serving earlier is pointless: the syrup has not reached the lower layers.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Spanakopita
description: A filo pie of spinach and feta. The spinach is squeezed bone dry, or the base stays raw. (Σπανακόπιτα)
instructions: Chop the spinach, salt it and leave it twenty minutes. Squeeze it dry by the handful — more water comes out than seems possible.
Fry the spring onion in a spoon of oil until soft and let it cool.
Mix the spinach with the onion, feta, dill, eggs, nutmeg and pepper. Taste before salting: the feta is salty already.
Line the tin with seven sheets of filo, brushing each with olive oil and letting the edges overhang.
Spread the filling, fold the overhanging edges in and cover with six more sheets, brushing each one.
Score the top into portions without cutting through to the filling, flick water over it and bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes, to a deep gold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Patatas bravas
description: Twice-fried potato under a hot paprika sauce. The Madrid version has no tomato in it at all. (Patatas bravas)

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Olive oil for the sauce

instructions: Cut the potato into uneven chunks: broken faces give more crisp surface. Rinse off the starch and dry them thoroughly.
Fry at 140 °C for eight minutes until soft, without letting them colour. Set them aside to cool at least ten minutes.
For the sauce, fry the garlic in olive oil, take the pan off the heat, add the flour and both paprikas and stir. On the flame paprika burns in seconds.
Return it to a low flame, pour in the stock in a thin stream, stirring, and cook five minutes to a sauce. Add the vinegar and salt.
Raise the oil to 190 °C and fry the potato three minutes more, to a deep gold. Salt it at once.
Pile them on a dish and pour the hot sauce over immediately before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Momo
description: Nepali steamed dumplings of buffalo or chicken with an achar of charred tomato. (मम:)

ingredients.text: 500 g Beef or chicken (chopped by hand)

instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, cold water and a pinch of salt for eight minutes and rest it under film for half an hour.
Mix the chopped meat with the onion, ginger, garlic, coriander, timur, a spoon of oil and salt. Do not work it to a paste; pieces should remain.
Char the tomatoes over a flame until blackened, toast the chillies and sesame in a dry pan, and blend everything with salt into a sauce.
Roll eight-centimetre rounds, thinner at the edges. Add a spoon of filling and pleat all the way round, twisting the top shut.
Oil the steamer and cook the momo ten minutes over a fierce steam, keeping them from touching.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Dal bhat
description: Lentil soup with rice and a vegetable tarkari. Nepal's everyday meal, eaten twice a day for a lifetime. (दाल भात)
instructions: Rinse the lentils and boil them in a litre of water with the turmeric for thirty minutes, until they collapse completely. Skim for the first five minutes.
Start the rice. While it cooks, fry the onion, add the potato and cauliflower with a little turmeric and water, and cook fifteen minutes: that is the tarkari.
Fry the greens with garlic over a high flame for two minutes; they should stay bright.
For the jhaneko, heat the ghee and throw in the ajwain, cumin, dried chilli and garlic, frying twenty seconds to the smell.
Pour the sizzling spiced fat straight into the dal — it hisses. Stir, season and serve at once.
Build the plate: rice in the middle, dal in a small bowl, tarkari and greens around it, achar at the edge.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kottu roti
description: Godamba roti chopped on the griddle with vegetables, egg and curry, worked with two cleavers. (කොත්තු රොටි)

ingredients.text: 6 Roti or paratha (from the day before)

instructions: Cut the roti into centimetre strips: that makes the chopping easier later.
Heat a large pan with the oil, fry the onion, leek and chilli two minutes, add the carrot and cabbage and cook three more.
Push the vegetables aside, break the eggs into the cleared space, let them set and break them up.
Add the chicken, curry powder and strips of roti and start chopping with two spatulas, mixing as you go. Three minutes of real work.
Pour the curry sauce down the side and keep chopping a minute more. The mixture should be moist but not wet.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pol sambol
description: Fresh coconut pounded with chilli, onion and lime. Five minutes to make and served with everything. (පොල් සම්බෝල)
instructions: Pound the chilli flakes with the salt and the Maldive fish to a rough paste.
Add the onion and keep pounding: it should give up its juice and stain the paste.
Work the coconut in by hand, rubbing the mixture between your palms until it turns evenly red.
Add the lime juice, mix and taste. The sambol should be hot, sour and salty at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ćevapi
description: Skinless minced-meat sausages over coals, with raw onion and somun flatbread. (Ћевапи)

ingredients.text: Kajmak or soured cream, to taste

instructions: Combine all three minces with the crushed garlic, bicarbonate, paprika, salt and pepper.
Work it by hand for ten minutes, adding the iced water a little at a time, until the mass turns tacky and even.
Press film onto the surface and refrigerate for at least twelve hours.
With wet hands roll sausages eight centimetres long and as thick as a thumb.
Grill over hot coals or on a griddle three minutes a side, turning once.
Split the warm somun, tuck the ćevapi inside and add a pile of raw onion and kajmak.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ajvar
description: A relish of roasted red pepper and aubergine, cooked down in oil to a thick paste. (Ајвар)
instructions: Roast the peppers and aubergines at 220 °C or over a flame until blistered black all over.
Pile them hot into a covered pot for twenty minutes: the steam lifts the skin by itself.
Peel and seed them and leave the flesh in a colander for two or three hours. Do not press: the water should drain on its own.
Put it through a mincer or chop it by hand — not a blender: what is wanted is a coarse texture rather than a purée.
Reduce it in a pot with half the oil over a low flame for an hour, stirring every ten minutes.
Add the garlic, vinegar, salt and the rest of the oil and cook another half hour, until the oil starts separating. Pack it hot into sterilised jars.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Frikadeller
description: Danish meat patties — flat rather than round — fried in butter to a dark crust. (Frikadeller)
instructions: Mix both minces with the grated onion, egg, flour, salt, pepper and allspice.
Work it for five minutes, adding the milk in stages. The mixture should turn tacky and string off the spoon.
Chill it for half an hour: cold farce holds its shape better.
Melt the butter over medium heat. With a spoon dipped in water, scoop the mixture into the pan and flatten each one.
Fry six minutes a side, to a dark brown crust. Do not hurry: the colour is the flavour.
Serve with boiled potatoes, pickled red cabbage and the gravy from the pan.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Smørrebrød
description: An open sandwich on rye with butter. The order of the layers and the thickness of the butter both matter. (Smørrebrød)
instructions: Butter every slice right to the edges. The layer should be visible to the eye rather than translucent.
For herring: a lettuce leaf, then pieces of herring, onion rings and capers. The lettuce keeps the brine off the bread.
For prawns: lay them in tight overlapping rows, then a spoon of mayonnaise, a slice of lemon and dill.
For egg: overlapping rounds of boiled egg, a line of mayonnaise, dill and a pinch of salt over the top.
Serve at once, with a knife and fork. Smørrebrød is not picked up by hand; it is not built for that.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sarmale
description: Cabbage rolls in soured leaves with pork and rice, braised three hours under a layer of shredded cabbage. (Sarmale)

ingredients.text: Soured cream and polenta, to taste

instructions: Take the cabbage apart into leaves and pare down the thick ribs. Rinse leaves that are too sour; soak overly salty ones for twenty minutes.
Fry the finely chopped onion in the oil until soft, add the tomato paste and cook two minutes. Cool it completely.
Mix the pork with the rice, the cooled onion, savory, salt and pepper.
Put a tablespoon of filling on each leaf, roll it up and tuck the ends in with a finger. The rolls should come out small, about two fingers wide.
Line the pot with shredded cabbage and the ribs, pack the rolls in tight layers with bay between them, and cover with the remaining cabbage and leaves.
Add water to the level of the top layer and cook three hours on the lowest heat or at 150 °C in the oven.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mămăligă
description: A firm cornmeal porridge, cut with a thread rather than a knife. (Mămăligă)
instructions: Bring the salted water to the boil. Set aside a handful of the meal; it is wanted at the end.
Pour the meal in as a thin stream, whisking without stopping. Do not pause until all of it is in.
Drop to the lowest heat and cook thirty minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon every three or four minutes. The mass pulls away from the sides.
Add the reserved handful of meal and work it in: it gives the light graininess mămăligă is valued for.
Stir in the butter, turn it out onto a board and let it stand five minutes. Cut it into slabs with thread and serve with the cheese and soured cream.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shopska salad
description: Tomato, cucumber and pepper under a cap of grated white cheese. The vegetables are cut large, the cheese grated fine. (Шопска салата)
instructions: Char the peppers over a flame until the skin blackens, close them in a covered dish for ten minutes and peel them.
Cut the tomatoes and cucumbers into two-centimetre dice and the peppers into strips.
Mix the vegetables with the onion and parsley and dress with the oil, vinegar and salt.
Mound it on a dish and blanket it with the grated cheese without stirring. Finish with olives.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Banitsa
description: A filo spiral with white cheese and eggs, doused in yoghurt and bicarbonate before baking. (Баница)
instructions: Crush the cheese with a fork and work in four of the eggs: the filling should stay crumbly rather than becoming a paste.
Mix the melted butter with the sunflower oil: that lets the sheets crisp without burning.
Lay two overlapping filo sheets, brush with the fat, scatter the filling in a crumbly line along the long edge and roll it loosely.
Coil the roll into a round tin from the centre outwards, leaving a couple of millimetres between the turns.
Whisk the yoghurt with the last egg and the bicarbonate and pour it over, aiming into the gaps between the coils.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, to a deep gold. Cover with a cloth for ten minutes out of the oven.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lohikeitto
description: Finnish salmon soup with potato and cream, a heap of dill and a knob of butter in the bowl. (Lohikeitto)
instructions: Cover the head and bones with a litre and a half of water, add the allspice and bay, and simmer twenty-five minutes, skimming. Strain it.
Fry the leek and carrot in butter for five minutes without letting them colour.
Pour in the strained stock, add the potato and cook fifteen minutes until soft.
Add the cream and warm it without boiling. Season.
Slip in the pieces of salmon and hold them at a bare simmer for exactly five minutes. The fish should stay in whole pieces.
Ladle into bowls and add a knob of butter and a generous handful of dill to each.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Karelian pies
description: A rye shell filled with rice porridge, brushed with butter out of the oven and served with egg butter. (Karjalanpiirakka)
instructions: Cook the rice in the milk over a low flame for forty minutes, to a slightly loose porridge. Season it and cool it.
Knead a dough from the rye flour, water and salt for five minutes. It comes out firm and not sticky.
Divide it into sixteen balls and roll each into an oval half a millimetre thick. Dust with rye flour rather than wheat.
Spoon porridge into the middle, leaving the edges bare, and crimp them into a frill with the filling left open.
Bake at 250 °C for fifteen minutes — short and very hot, or the thin pastry dries out.
Melt half the butter with an equal amount of hot water and dip the hot pies in it. Cover them with a cloth for ten minutes.
Mash the boiled eggs with the rest of the butter, softened, and salt: this is munavoi, egg butter. Serve it with the pies.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Irish stew
description: Lamb with potato and onion, stewed without browning. The meat is never seared, and that is the whole point. (Irish stew)

ingredients.text: 1.2 kg Lamb neck or shoulder (on the bone, in large pieces)

instructions: Put the meat into the pot raw, add the onion, carrot and the first lot of potatoes cut large.
Pour in the stock, bring it to the boil, skim and cook covered for an hour and a half on the lowest heat.
Crush the collapsed potato against the side of the pot: the broth thickens and turns milky white.
Add the second lot of potatoes in large pieces and cook another forty minutes.
Season, and let it stand fifteen minutes. Scatter parsley over before serving.

image.credit: A Healthier Michigan from Detroit, United States

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Soda bread
description: Bread on bicarbonate and buttermilk, with no yeast and no proving. Three minutes from mixing to oven. (Soda bread)
instructions: Heat the oven to 220 °C in advance. The bread has to go in immediately after mixing; it cannot wait.
Mix both flours, the bicarbonate and the salt in a bowl and stir well so the soda spreads evenly.
Pour in the buttermilk and mix with a knife or your hand only until it comes together. The dough is sticky and uneven, which is correct.
Turn it onto a floured tray, shape it into a round loaf and cut a deep cross almost to the base.
Scatter the oats over and bake fifteen minutes at 220 °C, then thirty at 190 °C.
A finished loaf sounds hollow when its base is tapped. Cool it on a rack for at least an hour: hot soda bread will not slice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Black risotto
description: Risotto with cuttlefish and its own ink. The ink goes in at the end, or it turns bitter. (Crni rižot)
instructions: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, add the cuttlefish and cook five minutes; it releases water.
Add half the wine and the tomato paste and stew covered for twenty-five minutes, topping up with stock, until the cuttlefish softens.
Add the rice and toast it two minutes, until the grains turn translucent at the edges. Pour in the rest of the wine.
Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for eighteen minutes. Each addition goes in when the last has nearly been absorbed.
Five minutes before the end stir in the ink. The risotto turns black within seconds.
Off the heat, beat in a spoon of olive oil and the parsley, cover for two minutes and serve.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Zagorje štrukli
description: Thin dough with a curd filling, boiled and then baked under cream. (Zagorski štrukli)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, oil, egg and salt for ten minutes to elasticity. Oil it and rest it half an hour.
Mash the curd with the eggs, soured cream and salt. The filling should be firm rather than pourable.
Stretch the dough on a cloth by hand until translucent, brush it with melted butter and spread the filling over a third of it.
Roll it up by lifting the cloth and cut it into eight-centimetre pieces, sealing the ends by pressing with the edge of your hand.
Boil them in salted water for five minutes after they float and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Lay them in a dish, pour the cream over, trickle on melted butter and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a browned top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gravlaks
description: Salmon cured for two days under a weight with salt, sugar and dill. No heat and no smoke. (Gravlaks)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Salmon fillet, skin on (the middle cut)

instructions: Run your fingers over the fillet for pin bones and pull them with tweezers. Leave the skin on: it holds the shape while curing.
Mix the salt, sugar and crushed pepper. Sprinkle the fish with aquavit and rub the mixture into the flesh.
Lay half the dill in a dish, the fish on it skin down, and bury it under the rest of the dill.
Cover with film, set a board and a kilo weight on top and refrigerate for forty-eight hours.
Every twelve hours pour off the brine that has collected and turn the fish over.
Scrape off the cure, pat the fish dry and slice it thinly on the diagonal, stopping at the skin. Serve with a mustard sauce of mustard, sugar, vinegar and oil.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fårikål
description: Mutton and cabbage in layers with whole peppercorns. Four ingredients and two hours. (Fårikål)

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg Mutton on the bone (in large pieces)

instructions: Lay a layer of meat fat side down in the pot, season it and scatter peppercorns over.
Add a layer of cabbage, more salt and pepper, and a dusting of flour if you want body. Alternate the layers until everything is used.
Pour the water down the side; it should reach halfway up, no higher.
Bring it to the boil, cover and cook two hours on the lowest heat. Do not stir: the layers are meant to stay layers.
It is done when the meat comes away from the bone. Serve with boiled potatoes, spooning broth from the pot over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Moules marinières
description: Mussels steamed in white wine with celery and onion. Five minutes under a lid, no longer. (Moules marinières)
instructions: Sort the mussels: discard any that are cracked or that will not close when tapped. Pull away the beards and rinse them under the tap.
Melt the butter in a wide pot and sweat the shallot, celery and garlic for five minutes without letting them colour.
Pour in the wine, add the thyme and bay and bring it to the boil.
Tip in the mussels, cover at once and hold them over a fierce flame for five minutes, shaking the pot a couple of times.
Lift the lid: the shells should be open. Throw out any that are not. Scatter parsley, add pepper and serve with chips and the broth in a separate cup.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Carbonade flamande
description: Beef braised in dark beer with onion and a slice of mustard-spread bread that thickens the sauce. (Carbonade flamande)
instructions: Dry the meat and brown it in butter in batches until dark. Set it aside.
In the same fat sweat the onion for twenty minutes until soft and gold: it gives the sauce its sweetness and body.
Return the meat, pour in the beer and add the syrup, vinegar, thyme and bay. The liquid should nearly cover the meat.
Spread the bread with mustard and lay it mustard side down on top of the meat. Do not stir it in.
Cover and cook three hours on the lowest heat or at 150 °C in the oven. The bread dissolves on its own.
Stir the sauce, check the balance of sweet and sour and serve with chips.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Cheese fondue
description: Gruyère and Vacherin melted in white wine with starch. The acidity of the wine keeps the cheese from seizing. (Fondue moitié-moitié)
instructions: Rub the inside of the pot with a cut clove of garlic and leave it in.
Toss both grated cheeses with the cornflour by hand until every shred is coated.
Warm the wine with the lemon juice until bubbles appear at the edge, but not to a boil.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring in a figure of eight until each is fully melted before the next goes in.
When the mass turns even and strings from the spoon, add the kirsch and season with nutmeg and pepper.
Move it to the burner and keep the flame at its lowest. The bread is speared through the crust rather than the crumb.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rösti
description: A potato cake of coarsely grated potato fried crisp on both sides. The potatoes are boiled the day before. (Rösti)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Waxy potatoes (boiled the day before)

instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for twenty minutes, to the point where a knife meets resistance. Cool them completely and leave them overnight in the fridge.
Peel them and grate them coarsely straight into a bowl. Do not rinse and do not squeeze.
Season, and if you are using them, fold in the fried bacon and onion and the cheese.
Heat half the butter in a pan, spread the mixture in an even layer and press it once with the spatula.
Fry over medium heat for twelve minutes without touching it. Shake the pan now and then: the rösti should slide as one piece.
Cover with a plate, invert it, add the rest of the butter and fry the second side for ten minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ghapama
description: A whole pumpkin baked with rice, dried fruit and nuts. A festive dish, cut open at the table. (Ղափամա)
instructions: Cut the top off the pumpkin with its stalk; that is the lid. Scoop out the seeds and loose flesh with a spoon, leaving a wall two fingers thick.
Boil the rice in salted water for seven minutes, to half done, and drain.
Cover the dried fruit with boiling water for ten minutes, drain, and chop the apricots and prunes coarsely. Chop the nuts.
Mix the rice with the fruit, nuts, melted butter, honey and cinnamon. Salt it: a sweet filling without salt tastes flat.
Fill the pumpkin, without packing it down, put the cut lid back on and set it on a baking tray.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour and a half. Test at the side with a knife: it should go into the wall without resistance.
Rest fifteen minutes, carry it out whole and cut it into wedges from the crown to the base.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Spas
description: A soup of matsun and wheat groats. The whole difficulty is keeping the yoghurt base from splitting. (Սպաս)
instructions: Soak the dzavar overnight, then boil it in a litre of water until soft, about twenty-five minutes. Keep the water.
Whisk the matsun with the egg and flour until completely smooth. No lumps may remain; each one becomes a curd in the soup.
Pour the mixture into a cold pan and heat it over medium, stirring with a wooden spoon in one direction, until it comes to a boil.
At the first bubbles, stir in the wheat with its cooking water and hold it on a low heat for five more minutes.
Fry the onion in butter until golden and stir it into the soup with the dried mint. Salt to taste.
Ladle out and scatter with coriander. Spas must not be boiled twice; reheat it only until hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shah plov
description: Pilaf baked in a crown of lavash. The crust holds its shape and is cut in wedges like a pie. (Şah plov)
instructions: Soak the rice in salted water for an hour, then boil it seven minutes in plenty of water and drain.
Steep the saffron in three spoons of boiling water and leave it; it gives both colour and scent.
Brown the lamb, add the onion and cook until soft. Add the chestnuts, apricots, raisins and turmeric and stew for twenty minutes.
Butter a deep dish generously and line it with overlapping lavash, letting the edges hang outside.
Layer it: rice, filling, rice again. Pour over the saffron infusion and the rest of the butter.
Fold the lavash edges over the top, cover with foil and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes, then uncover and give it fifteen more to colour.
Rest ten minutes, cover with a platter and invert. Cut it at the table.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kufta bozbash
description: A clear broth with one large meatball per portion, a dried plum and apricot hidden inside it. (Küftə bozbaş)

ingredients.text: 400 g Lamb on the bone (for the broth)

instructions: Cover the bone-in lamb with cold water, bring it up and skim. Add the chickpeas and simmer for an hour.
Work a grated onion, the rice, salt and pepper into the mince and knead for five minutes, until the mass pulls back at your hand.
Divide the mince into four. Hide a plum and an apricot in each and shape a tight ball with no cracks.
Lower the kufta into the barely simmering broth and cook thirty minutes without stirring. For the first five minutes do not touch it at all.
Add the potatoes whole and the turmeric and cook twenty minutes more, until the potatoes are tender.
Into each bowl goes one kufta, one potato and some chickpeas; ladle over the broth and crumble dried mint on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Beshbarmak
description: Boiled meat on sheets of pasta with an onion broth called sorpa. The centrepiece of a Kazakh table. (Бесбармақ)

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg Beef on the bone (brisket or shoulder)

instructions: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim, and simmer on the lowest heat for two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into squares of about eight centimetres.
Slice the onion into rings, pour a ladle of hot broth over it and leave it ten minutes; this is the sorpa that dresses the dish.
Lift out the meat, skim the fat into a separate bowl and boil the dough squares in that broth in batches, three to four minutes each.
Pull the meat apart into thin sheets across the grain. Lay the dough on a large platter, the meat on top, the onions and their broth over that.
Serve the remaining broth hot in bowls with herbs; it is drunk before the dish or alongside it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Baursak
description: Squares of yeast dough deep-fried into hollow puffs. The bread of the tea table and of every feast. (Бауырсақ)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Work in the eggs, melted butter, salt and flour to a soft dough. It should stay slightly tacky.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for an hour, until the dough has doubled.
Knock it back, roll it out a centimetre and a half thick and cut it into three-centimetre squares or diamonds.
Let the pieces stand under a cloth for twenty minutes; this second rise is the reason for the hollow.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry in batches for two to three minutes, turning, to an even gold.
Drain on paper and serve warm, with tea, soured cream or honey.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bryndzové halušky
description: Potato dumplings with sheep's brynza and bacon crackling. Slovakia's national dish. (Bryndzové halušky)
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly; only a little water should go, as a dry mass will not bind.
Mix in the flour, egg and salt. The mass should slide off a spoon slowly rather than pour.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Push the dough into boiling salted water through a colander with large holes. The dumplings are done when they float, after about three minutes.
Drain the dumplings, return them to the warm pan and stir in the brynza with a spoon of the cooking water. Keep the heat off.
Serve into bowls, spoon over the hot fat and scatter the crackling on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kapustnica
description: A soup of sauerkraut with smoked meat, sausage and dried mushrooms. The Slovak Christmas table. (Kapustnica)
instructions: Soak the mushrooms in a cup of warm water for twenty minutes. Keep the water.
Simmer the smoked ribs in two litres of water for forty minutes with the bay.
Squeeze the kraut and set the brine aside. Add the kraut, the mushrooms with their water and the prunes to the broth and cook thirty minutes.
Fry the onion, take it off the heat, stir in the paprika and flour and let it down with a ladle of broth until smooth.
Pour the roux into the pot, add the sausage and cook fifteen minutes more.
Strip the meat off the bones, return it to the soup and bring the sourness up with the brine to taste. Serve with soured cream.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pastel de choclo
description: A bake of meat filling under a lid of ground sweetcorn, with an olive and an egg inside. (Pastel de choclo)
instructions: Fry the finely chopped onion until translucent, add the mince, cumin, salt and pepper and cook through. Let the pino cool; warm, it will weep.
Blitz the corn with the basil and milk to a coarse but even mass.
Cook it down with the butter over medium heat, stirring, for about fifteen minutes, until a spoon stands up in it.
Divide the pino between earthenware dishes and top each with a piece of chicken, half an egg and a couple of olives with raisins.
Cover with a two-centimetre layer of the corn mass, level it and dust with sugar.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, the last five under the grill, to a dark caramel crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Empanadas de pino
description: Baked pastries with a meat filling, an olive and an egg. Chilean food for 18 September and for any Sunday. (Empanadas de pino)
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat it in fat for twenty minutes over a low heat; it should turn sweet, not brown.
Add the meat, paprika and cumin and stew twenty minutes. By volume there should be at least as much onion as meat.
Chill the filling for at least three hours, ideally overnight.
Knead a dough from the flour, melted fat, warm milk and salt. Work it ten minutes and rest it half an hour.
Roll out twenty-centimetre rounds. On each go two spoons of filling, an olive, a quarter egg and a pinch of raisins.
Fold into a parcel, seal the edges and turn them over twice. Prick the top with a toothpick so steam can escape.
Brush with yolk and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a deep gold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pabellón criollo
description: A plate in four parts: shredded stewed beef, black beans, white rice and fried plantain. (Pabellón criollo)
instructions: Boil the beans with half the onion and some garlic until soft, an hour to ninety minutes. Salt at the end.
Simmer the beef whole in salted water for an hour and twenty minutes. Lift it out and cool it enough to handle.
Pull the meat into threads along the grain. Across the grain it shreds into crumbs.
Fry the remaining onion, pepper and garlic, add the tomatoes and cumin, then the meat, and stew twenty minutes with a ladle of the broth.
Cook the rice loose, without butter or spice; here it is the neutral part.
Slice the plantain on the diagonal and fry over medium heat until caramel on both sides.
Build the plate in sectors: rice, beans, meat and plantain side by side, unmixed.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Cachapas
description: Thick pancakes of ground fresh corn, folded around a soft white cheese. (Cachapas)
instructions: Cut the kernels from the cobs and blend them with the milk, sugar and salt to a coarse but pourable purée.
Let the batter stand ten minutes. The starch swells and the pancakes hold together.
Heat a pan to medium, butter it and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading it into a circle a centimetre thick.
Cook four minutes, until the edges dry and the underside is mottled, flip and give it three more.
Lay butter and cheese on the hot cachapa, fold it over and press it with a spatula.
Serve at once. A cooled cachapa loses its softness and turns into a dense cake.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Salteñas
description: Baked pastries whose filling stays liquid inside. The Bolivian mid-morning snack. (Salteñas)
instructions: Fry the onion with the ají and cumin, add the beef and cook through. Pour in the stock and simmer ten minutes.
Dissolve the gelatine in a couple of spoons of hot water and stir it into the stew with the potato and peas.
Cool the filling and refrigerate it for at least four hours; it has to set to a firm jelly.
Knead a dough from the flour, softened butter, sugar, achiote, salt and warm water. Rest it half an hour.
Roll fifteen-centimetre rounds. On each go a spoon of the cold jelly, a wedge of egg and an olive.
Seal the seam in a plait along the top and stand the pastries seam-up. Any gap means the broth escapes.
Bake at 220 °C for twenty-five minutes. The high heat is what sets the pastry before the jelly melts.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Silpancho
description: A plate-sized breaded steak over rice and potatoes, topped with a fried egg and raw salsa. (Silpancho)
instructions: Pound the meat under film to three or four millimetres. Work from the centre outwards or it tears.
Season and press into breadcrumbs with the flat of your hand. No egg wash is used here.
Dice the tomato, onion and beetroot small, mix with the parsley, salt and a spoon of oil.
Fry the boiled potato slices until golden and keep them warm.
Fry the steaks a minute and a half a side in hot oil; meat this thin cooks instantly.
Fry the eggs, leaving the yolks runny.
Build it: rice, potato, the steak across the whole plate, the egg, and the raw salsa over the top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Encebollado
description: A tuna soup with cassava and pickled onion. Ecuadorians eat it for breakfast and treat it as a hangover cure. (Encebollado)
instructions: Cure the onion in the juice of two limes with salt and leave it at least fifteen minutes.
Fry the garlic and tomatoes with the cumin for five minutes, add a litre and a half of water and bring it up.
Lower in the tuna whole and poach it fifteen minutes on a low heat. Fish does not tolerate a hard boil.
Lift out the fish, strain the broth and return it to the heat. Cook the cassava in it for twenty minutes, until soft.
Flake the tuna coarsely, discarding the dark parts, and return it to the pot for two minutes.
Ladle it out and top with the cured onion and its juice and coriander. Serve with a wedge of lime.

image.credit: Ministerio de Turismo Ecuador from Ecuador

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Llapingachos
description: Potato cakes with cheese inside, fried in achiote oil and served with a peanut sauce. (Llapingachos)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins, peel them hot and mash them dry. Add no liquid at all.
Warm the achiote in a spoon of oil for a minute and work the coloured oil into the mash with salt.
Roll balls, press a cube of cheese into each, close them up and flatten into cakes a centimetre thick.
Chill the cakes for half an hour; that is what holds their shape in the pan.
For the sauce fry the onion, add the peanut butter and milk and simmer five minutes to the thickness of cream.
Fry the cakes over medium heat, four minutes a side, to a golden crust.
Serve with a fried egg, the sauce and an avocado salad.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Masgouf
description: River fish butterflied and cooked standing beside an open fire. A Baghdad dish from the banks of the Tigris. (مسكوف)

ingredients.text: 2 kg Carp (whole, split along the back)

instructions: Cut the fish along the back without separating the belly, gut it and open it out like a book. Leave the spine in.
Mix the oil, turmeric, tamarind, curry powder, salt and pepper and paint the flesh with it. Leave the skin alone.
Leave the fish half an hour at room temperature; cold, it cooks unevenly.
Light the fire and let it settle to a steady flame. Stand the fish upright, flesh towards the fire, half a metre away.
Cook for an hour, turning as needed. The flesh should whiten and dry at the edges without scorching.
Move the fish skin down onto the coals, lay the onion and tomato over it and give it ten more minutes.
Serve it on the board, with flatbread, lemon and raw onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Iraqi dolma
description: Vine leaves and vegetables stuffed with spiced rice and meat, layered in one pot and cooked under a weight. (دولمة)
instructions: Rinse the rice and mix it with the mince, chopped parsley, tomato paste, baharat, oil, salt and pepper.
Cut lids off the peppers and tomatoes and hollow them. Blanch the onions whole and separate them into layers.
Roll the filling in vine leaves into tight cylinders — the rice doubles, so leave it room.
Fill the vegetables two-thirds full and put their lids back on.
Line the pot with tomato slices, then layer the parcels and stuffed vegetables, the heaviest at the bottom.
Mix water with the pomegranate molasses, lemon juice and salt and pour it in until it reaches the top layer.
Cover with a weighted plate and cook on a low heat for an hour and fifteen minutes. Serve by inverting the pot onto a platter.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mansaf
description: Lamb in a sauce of jameed, fermented dried yoghurt, over rice and flatbread. Jordan's national dish. (منسف)

ingredients.text: 2 kg Lamb on the bone (in large pieces)

instructions: Soak the jameed in warm water for four hours, break it up by hand and pass it through a sieve to an even liquid.
Simmer the lamb with the cardamom for an hour and twenty minutes, skimming. Keep the broth.
Pour the jameed liquid in with the meat and bring it up, stirring continuously in one direction.
Drop the heat to its lowest and hold it forty minutes. The sauce thickens and turns creamy.
Cook the rice in the meat broth with turmeric and a spoon of ghee.
Fry the almonds and pine nuts in ghee until golden and set them aside.
Line a platter with the bread, moisten it with sauce, spread the rice, lay the meat on top, spoon over more sauce and scatter the nuts and parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Maqluba
description: Rice with meat and fried vegetables cooked in one pot and turned out whole onto a platter. (مقلوبة)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with the onion, cinnamon and baharat for forty minutes. Lift out the meat and strain the broth.
Soak the rice in warm water for twenty minutes and rinse until the water runs clear.
Slice the aubergines into rounds, salt them and leave fifteen minutes, then pat dry and fry until browned.
Fry the cauliflower florets and potato slices until golden and drain them on paper.
Lay the potato on the bottom of the pot, aubergine up the sides, then chicken, cauliflower and rice on top. Do not press it down.
Pour in hot broth to a finger above the rice, bring it up and cook covered on a low heat for forty minutes.
Take it off the heat, rest it ten minutes, cover with a platter and invert in one movement. Scatter with pine nuts.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Brik
description: A thin sheet of pastry with an egg inside, fried so the yolk stays liquid. (بريك)
instructions: Mix the mashed potato with the tuna, chopped onion, capers, parsley, harissa, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Test with a scrap of pastry: it should surface at once and sizzle.
Lay a sheet on a plate, put two spoons of filling on one half and make a hollow in it.
Break an egg into the hollow, season it and fold the sheet over immediately, pressing the edges.
Slide the brik into the oil and fry forty seconds a side, steadying it with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tunisian lablabi
description: Chickpeas in a garlic broth poured over torn stale bread, with an egg, cumin and harissa. (لبلابي)
instructions: Boil the chickpeas in two litres of water with half the garlic for ninety minutes, until soft but whole.
Pound the remaining garlic with salt and cumin to a paste and stir it into the broth. Season.
Soft-boil the eggs, six minutes from the boil, and peel them.
Tear the bread into large pieces into deep bowls, filling them halfway.
Ladle the hot broth and chickpeas over the bread until it is thoroughly soaked.
Top with an egg, a spoon of harissa, olives, capers and tuna, then olive oil and lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Algerian couscous
description: Semolina steamed three times over a pot of meat and vegetables, with the broth served apart. (كسكس)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Lamb (on the bone, in pieces)

instructions: Brown the meat with the onion in the base of the couscoussier, add the tomato paste, spices and chickpeas and cover with water. Cook an hour.
Sprinkle the couscous with water and oil and rub it between your hands so the grains separate. Steam it fifteen minutes.
Turn the grain into a wide dish, sprinkle again, rake it apart and let it cool five minutes.
Return it to the steam for fifteen more minutes. Meanwhile add the carrot and turnip to the broth.
Rake it a third time, working in the butter, and steam it a final ten minutes.
Add the courgette and pumpkin to the broth for the last twenty minutes; they cook faster than the roots.
Mound the couscous, meat and vegetables on top. Serve the broth in a separate bowl and the harissa in a third.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chorba frik
description: A soup of freekeh, the smoked green wheat, with lamb and mint. The first thing on the table in Ramadan. (شوربة فريك)
instructions: Brown the meat with the onion and celery in ghee for ten minutes.
Add the grated tomato, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook five minutes.
Pour in two litres of boiling water, add the chickpeas and simmer forty minutes.
Rinse the freekeh, add it and cook twenty minutes more, stirring; the grain settles and catches.
Stir in the coriander five minutes before the end and loosen with water if the soup has gone too thick.
Ladle out, crumble dried mint over each bowl and add lemon juice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Cepelinai
description: Large potato dumplings with a meat filling, named after airships. Served with crackling and soured cream. (Cepelinai)
instructions: Grate the raw potato finely and wring it out in a cloth. Collect the liquid in a bowl.
Let the liquid stand ten minutes, pour off the water and stir the settled starch back into the grated potato.
Mash the boiled potato and combine it with the grated, adding the starch and salt. The mass should shape without sticking.
Mix the mince with half the finely chopped onion, marjoram, salt and pepper and roll four firm balls.
With wet hands take a lump of dough, flatten it on your palm, set the filling in it and seal it into an elongated oval.
Lower them into barely simmering salted water and cook twenty-five minutes. Do not stir; just rock the pot once in the first minute.
Render the pork fat with the remaining onion to crackling, spoon it over the cepelinai and serve with soured cream.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Šaltibarščiai
description: A cold beetroot soup on kefir, vivid pink, with cucumber, dill and boiled potatoes served alongside. (Šaltibarščiai)
instructions: Boil the beetroot until tender, cool it completely and grate it coarsely.
Cut the cucumbers into matchsticks and chop the dill and spring onion.
Mix the beetroot, cucumber and herbs with the soured cream and salt it now, before the kefir, so the salt disperses.
Pour in the cold kefir and stir. The soup turns an even pink.
Chill it for an hour. Warm šaltibarščiai makes no sense.
Boil the potatoes and serve them hot on a separate plate. Put halved eggs into the soup.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Grey peas with speck
description: Grey peas cooked soft with onion and rendered smoked pork. Latvian winter and Christmas food. (Pelēkie zirņi ar speķi)
instructions: Soak the peas twelve hours in cold water, changing it once.
Drain, cover with fresh water two fingers above and boil unsalted for an hour and twenty minutes, until soft.
Dice the pork belly and render it in a dry pan to golden crackling.
Add the chopped onion and fry it in the rendered fat until soft and golden.
Drain the peas, leaving a little liquid in the pot, and season with salt and pepper.
Stir the crackling, onion and fat into the peas and serve hot, with cold kefir in a glass.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rye bread layer dessert
description: Layers of dark rye breadcrumbs, whipped cream and cranberry jam. (Rupjmaizes kārtojums)
instructions: Crumb the stale bread in a blender or by hand to a coarse crumb.
Mix the crumbs with the sugar and cinnamon and dry them in the oven at 160 °C for twelve minutes, stirring twice.
Cool the crumbs completely. On warm crumbs the cream collapses and the layers merge.
Whip the cold cream with the vanilla sugar to firm peaks.
Layer into glasses: crumbs, jam, cream, and repeat. Finish with cream.
Chill for at least four hours, ideally overnight. Serve with cranberries on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mulgipuder
description: A mash of potato and pearl barley with pork crackling. An Estonian dish recognised as a national symbol. (Mulgipuder)
instructions: Rinse the barley and boil it in salted water for an hour, until soft.
Add the roughly cut potato to the same pot and cook twenty minutes more.
Render the pork belly to crackling, add the onion and fry until golden.
Drain most of the water from the barley and potato, keeping half a cup.
Mash with the butter and milk, leaving the barley grains still visible. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve into bowls and spoon the crackling, onion and rendered fat over the top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kama
description: A dessert of roasted mixed-grain flour stirred into kefir. Estonian breakfast and summer pudding at once. (Kama)
instructions: Whisk the kefir with the sugar and a pinch of salt until the sugar has dissolved.
Add the kama a little at a time, whisking; all at once it lumps, and the lumps never break up.
Leave it fifteen minutes for the flour to swell, then check the consistency and let it down with more kefir if needed.
Stir in the honey and divide between glasses.
Chill for an hour and serve with berries and, if you like, a spoon of whipped cream.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Draniki
description: Potato pancakes from raw grated potato, fried to a crisp edge and served with soured cream. (Дранікі)
instructions: Grate the potato and onion finely into the same bowl.
Let the mass stand three minutes and pour off the water that gathers on top, leaving the sediment.
Season with salt and pepper. Add nothing else.
Heat the oil over medium and drop the mixture in by the spoonful, flattening it to half a centimetre.
Fry three to four minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with soured cream and dill.

image.credit: Photo made by Daniel Spils and uploaded to flickr.com

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Machanka
description: A thick pork and sausage gravy on soured cream, into which pancakes are dipped. Hence the name. (Мачанка)
instructions: Brown the pork well, add the onion and fry until soft.
Add the sliced sausage and ribs, pour in a cup of water, add the bay and stew twenty-five minutes.
Whisk the flour into the soured cream until smooth and stir it into the pot.
Simmer ten minutes on a low heat, until the gravy thickens to the consistency of pouring cream.
Whisk a pancake batter from the flour, milk, eggs and salt and let it stand fifteen minutes.
Cook thin unsweetened pancakes in a dry pan.
Serve the machanka in a deep bowl with the pancakes stacked beside it. You tear off a piece and dip.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mohinga
description: Rice noodles in a thick fish broth built on banana stem. Breakfast, and Myanmar's unofficial national dish. (မုန့်ဟင်းခါး)

ingredients.text: 800 g Catfish or other oily fish

instructions: Poach the fish with the lemongrass and turmeric for fifteen minutes, lift it out and pick the flesh, discarding bones and skin. Strain the broth.
Pound the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry it in oil with the paprika until dark and fragrant.
Mash the fish with a fork and stir it into the paste, frying five minutes; it should break down into threads.
Transfer everything to the pot with the broth, add the fish sauce and simmer twenty minutes.
Slake the rice and chickpea flours in cold water to a thin slurry and pour it into the soup in a stream, stirring.
Cook twenty minutes more, until the broth thickens to the consistency of thin cream.
Boil the noodles, divide them between bowls, ladle the soup over and serve with egg, split peas, coriander and lime.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lahpet thoke
description: A salad of fermented tea leaves with fried beans, nuts and garlic. (လက်ဖက်သုပ်)
instructions: Fry the garlic slices in oil until golden and lift them out at once; a few seconds more and they turn bitter.
Toast the sesame in a dry pan until fragrant, two minutes, stirring.
Rinse the tea paste in cold water if it is very salty and squeeze it dry.
Shred the cabbage fine, cut the tomatoes into wedges and the chilli into rings.
Combine everything in a bowl with the peanuts, beans, sesame, garlic oil, fish sauce and lime juice.
Toss it with your hands immediately before serving and scatter the fried garlic over the top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fish amok
description: Fish in a coconut curry, steamed in a cup folded from banana leaf. (អាម៉ុកត្រី)
instructions: Pound the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, garlic, shallot and half the lime leaves in a mortar to a smooth paste.
Warm the paste in a pan with half the coconut milk for five minutes, until it smells right.
Take it off the heat, cool it to warm and whisk in the eggs, fish sauce, palm sugar and the rest of the milk.
Fold the fish pieces through and leave them to marinate fifteen minutes.
Fold cups from the banana leaves, or use ramekins. Line the bottom with spinach leaves.
Divide the fish and sauce between them without filling to the brim and steam for twenty minutes.
Spoon over the coconut cream, scatter with shredded lime leaves and serve with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lok lak
description: Cubes of beef seared over high heat, on salad, with a dip of lime and black pepper. (ឡុកឡាក់)
instructions: Marinate the beef in the oyster and soy sauces with garlic, sugar and half the pepper for twenty minutes.
Mix the lime juice with the remaining pepper and a pinch of salt; that is the dipping sauce.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato and cucumber slices and red onion rings on a platter.
Heat a pan as high as it goes and sear the beef in batches, a minute and a half each, without stirring constantly.
Fry the eggs, keeping the yolks runny.
Pile the beef on the vegetables, top with the eggs and give everyone their own small bowl of the dip.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Hainanese chicken rice
description: A whole chicken poached below boiling and rice cooked in its broth, with three sauces. (海南鸡饭)
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt inside and out and stuff the cavity with half the ginger and the spring onions.
Bring a pot of water to the boil, lower the whole chicken in, bring it back up and turn the heat off immediately.
Keep it covered for forty minutes without lifting the lid. It is done when the juices from the thigh run clear.
Move the chicken into iced water for ten minutes, then pat it dry and brush it with sesame oil.
Skim the fat from the broth, fry the chopped garlic and ginger in it, add the rinsed rice and toast it three minutes.
Add broth to the rice at one and a half to one, drop in the pandan leaf and cook covered for fifteen minutes.
Pound the chillies with garlic, ginger and lime into a sauce. Joint the chicken and serve with the rice, cucumber, sauce and a bowl of the broth.

image.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Terence assumed (based on copyright claims).

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chilli crab
description: Crab in a thick tomato-chilli sauce bound with egg, mopped up with fried mantou buns. (辣椒螃蟹)
instructions: Joint the crab: lift the shell, cut the body into four and crack the claws with the back of a knife.
Pound the garlic, ginger and chillies to a paste and fry it in oil for three minutes, until fragrant.
Add the sambal, ketchup, sugar and vinegar and cook two minutes, until the sauce darkens.
Pour in the stock, bring it up and add the crab pieces. Cover and cook eight minutes.
Slake the cornflour in cold water and stir it in to thicken the sauce.
Turn off the heat and pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream, stirring once in a circle.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the fried mantou.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lu rou fan
description: Minced pork belly braised in soy sauce with spices, spooned over white rice. (滷肉飯)
instructions: Dice the belly into one-centimetre cubes, keeping the fat with the meat.
Fry the sliced shallots in oil to a deep golden crisp and set half aside for serving.
In the same oil brown the pork, rendering some of its fat, for ten minutes.
Add the wine, let it cook off for a minute, then add both soy sauces, the sugar, spices and garlic.
Add water level with the meat, bring it up and braise covered for ninety minutes on the lowest heat.
Add the boiled eggs to the sauce for the last twenty minutes; they take on the colour and flavour.
Serve over rice with half an egg, blanched greens and the fried shallots on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Taiwanese beef noodle soup
description: Wheat noodles in a dark broth of beef shank with fermented bean paste and spices. (牛肉麵)
instructions: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, boil two minutes and drain; this removes the scum.
Fry the ginger, garlic and doubanjiang in oil for five minutes, until the oil turns red.
Add the tomatoes, wine and soy sauce, cook three minutes and return the meat to the pot.
Add water two fingers above the meat, drop in the star anise, cinnamon and sugar and simmer two hours.
Lift out the meat, cut it into thick slices and return it to the broth for ten minutes.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot of clean water and blanch the bok choy.
Divide the noodles between bowls, add the meat and greens, ladle over the broth and top with pickled mustard greens and spring onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nyama choma
description: Goat meat grilled slowly over coals in large pieces, with kachumbari and ugali. (Nyama choma)

ingredients.text: 2 kg Goat meat (leg or ribs, in large pieces)

instructions: Rub the meat with salt, pepper, the juice of two lemons, crushed garlic and oil. Leave it an hour.
Light the coals and let them ash over. The heat is right when you can hold a palm above the grate for five seconds.
Lay the meat on in whole pieces and grill, turning every ten minutes, for an hour and twenty.
Mix the diced tomato, onion, coriander and chilli with lemon juice and salt; that is kachumbari.
For the ugali bring a litre of water to the boil, rain in the flour, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, and work it fifteen minutes into a firm mass.
Rest the meat ten minutes, cut it small across the grain and serve with ugali, kachumbari and salt.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sukuma wiki
description: Collard greens stewed with onion and tomato. The everyday accompaniment to ugali across East Africa. (Sukuma wiki)
instructions: Strip the tough stems from the leaves, roll the leaves up and shred them fine.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the garlic and cumin and warm them a minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they collapse into a paste.
Add the greens, salt them and stir. They collapse by half within a minute.
Add half a cup of water, cover and stew ten minutes; the greens should soften but stay green.
Finish with lemon juice and serve with ugali or rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Waakye
description: Rice and black-eyed beans cooked with sorghum leaves, which turn it deep red. (Waakye)
instructions: Rinse the sorghum leaves and boil them in a litre and a half of water for ten minutes; the water turns deep red.
Take the leaves out, add a pinch of soda and the beans and cook forty-five minutes, until nearly done.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and add it to the pot. The liquid should stand a finger above the rice.
Salt it, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without stirring.
