Take it off the heat, leave it covered ten minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Fry slices of ripe plantain until caramel-coloured.
Serve with egg, gari, shito and plantain, all on one plate.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Banku with tilapia
description: Fermented maize and cassava dough worked smooth, with grilled fish and a hot pepper sauce. (Banku)

ingredients.text: 400 g Maize flour (fermented for three days)

instructions: Mix the maize and cassava doughs with a litre of water and salt to a smooth, lump-free batter.
Set it over medium heat and work it with a wooden paddle without stopping. It starts to thicken after five minutes.
Keep working it for twenty minutes, pressing it against the sides, until it turns dense and glossy.
Shape balls with wet hands and wrap each in film or a banana leaf.
Rub the fish with salt, ginger and garlic and grill or pan-fry it eight minutes a side.
Grind the tomatoes, habaneros, onion, salt and a spoon of oil in a mortar to a coarse sauce.
Serve a ball of banku, the fish and a bowl of sauce. It is eaten by hand, pinching off dough and dipping it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Thieboudienne
description: Rice cooked in the tomato broth from the fish, with herb-stuffed fish and vegetables. Senegal's national dish. (Ceebu jën)

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg Grouper or sea bream (in steaks)

instructions: Pound the parsley, garlic, chilli and salt into the rof paste and press it into slashes cut in the fish.
Fry the fish three minutes a side and set it aside.
In the same oil fry the onion until soft, add the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add two litres of water, the tamarind and the vegetables and cook twenty-five minutes.
Return the fish to the pot for ten minutes, then lift it and the vegetables out and keep them warm.
Add the rinsed rice to the remaining broth — twice as much liquid as rice — and cook covered for thirty minutes without stirring.
Turn the rice onto a large platter with the fish and vegetables on top. Share out the caught layer from the bottom separately.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chicken yassa
description: Chicken marinated in lemon under a mountain of caramelised onion with mustard. (Yassa ginaar)
instructions: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper, pour it over the chicken and onions and chill for at least four hours.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and brown it in oil on all sides.
In the same pan cook the onion from the marinade over medium heat for twenty-five minutes, until golden and soft.
Pour in the remaining marinade and the stock and add the bay leaves and the whole chilli.
Return the chicken, cover and stew thirty minutes on a low heat.
Uncover and reduce the sauce ten minutes more until thick. Remove the chilli.
Serve with boiled rice, the onions piled over the chicken.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bobotie
description: A bake of spiced mince with dried fruit under an egg and milk custard. South Africa's national dish. (Bobotie)
instructions: Soak the bread in half the milk for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the milk.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the curry powder and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the mince and cook, breaking up lumps, until it loses its pink, about ten minutes.
Stir in the bread, apricots, raisins, chutney, vinegar, salt and pepper and take it off the heat.
Press it into a dish, level it and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk, pour it over, stand the bay leaves in the custard and scatter the almonds.
Return it to the oven for twenty minutes, until the custard sets and turns golden.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chakalaka
description: A spicy vegetable relish of carrot, pepper and beans with curry. For a braai, for pap, or on its own. (Chakalaka)
instructions: Grate the carrots coarsely and cut the peppers and onions into thin strips.
Fry the onion with the garlic, ginger and chilli in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the curry powder and paprika and warm them a minute; the spices need to open up in the oil.
Add the peppers and carrot and cook five minutes over a high heat, stirring.
Add the tomatoes, season and cook seven minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the beans, warm them three minutes and take the pan off. The vegetables should still have bite.

image.credit: philipp from cape town, south africa

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Plokkfiskur
description: Flaked boiled fish mashed with potato in a white sauce. Icelandic home cooking made from leftovers. (Plokkfiskur)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, peel them and cut them into large pieces.
Poach the cod in salted water for eight minutes, lift it out and flake it by hand, removing bones and skin.
Fry the onion in butter until soft, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes, stirring.
Pour in the milk in a thin stream, whisking continuously, and bring the sauce to the thickness of cream.
Stir in the mustard, salt and pepper, add the fish and potato and warm everything through for five minutes.
Mash with a fork to a coarse, uneven texture in which the pieces are still recognisable, and scatter with chives.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kjötsúpa
description: A clear lamb soup with root vegetables and barley. One pot, four ingredients, three hours. (Kjötsúpa)

ingredients.text: 1.2 kg Lamb on the bone (shoulder or neck)

instructions: Cover the meat with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim carefully.
Simmer for an hour and a half, never letting it boil hard; the broth has to stay clear.
Add the barley and onion and cook forty minutes more.
Add the carrot, swede and potato in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the cabbage for the last ten minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Divide the meat between bowls, ladle over the broth and vegetables and serve with rye bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Potica
description: A yeasted roll with a walnut filling, coiled into a ring. Slovenian baking for every celebration. (Potica)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with a spoon of sugar and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, the yeast mixture, yolks, sugar, softened butter, zest and salt. Work it fifteen minutes.
Leave it somewhere warm for an hour and twenty, until it has doubled.
Warm the cream with the honey, pour it over the ground walnuts, add the rum and cinnamon and cool it to lukewarm.
Roll the dough into a rectangle three millimetres thick and spread the filling, leaving two centimetres clear at the edges.
Roll it up tightly from the long side, lay it in a ring tin seam down and let it prove forty minutes.
Prick the roll in several places with a skewer and bake at 170 °C for an hour, to a deep gold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jota
description: A thick soup of soured turnip or sauerkraut with beans, potato and smoked meat. (Jota)
instructions: Boil the soaked beans in a separate pot until soft, an hour. Keep the water.
Simmer the smoked ribs in a litre and a half of water for forty minutes with the bay.
Add the soured turnip or sauerkraut with some of its brine and cook twenty minutes.
Add the diced potato and sausage and cook twenty minutes more.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until golden and stir them into the soup.
Add the beans with their water, mash some of the potato in the pot and cook five minutes.
Strip the meat from the bones, return it to the soup and season with salt and pepper.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bosanski lonac
description: Meat and vegetables layered in a clay pot and cooked four hours without stirring. (Bosanski lonac)
instructions: Cut all the vegetables into large pieces; they have to survive four hours without collapsing.
Line the bottom of the pot with the diced pork fat, put the meat on it and season.
Layer on the onion, carrot, parsley root, potato, peppers, cabbage and tomato.
Tuck in the whole head of garlic and the bay leaves, pour in the wine and add water to half the height of the pot.
Cover and put it in a 150 °C oven for four hours. Do not open it and do not stir.
Serve straight from the pot, digging to the bottom so every layer reaches the plate.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bosnian burek
description: A spiral of hand-stretched pastry with a meat filling. In Bosnia only the meat one is called burek. (Burek)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil, the vinegar and salt, and work it fifteen minutes until elastic.
Divide it into four balls, oil them, cover and leave them forty minutes.
Mix the raw mince with the onion, salt, pepper and two spoons of water; the water keeps the filling from drying out.
Stretch a ball by hand on a cloth-covered table into a translucent sheet, working from the centre outwards.
Sprinkle the sheet with oil, lay the filling in a line along one edge and roll it into a long thin cylinder.
Coil the cylinders into a round tin from the centre outwards, brush with oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes.
Sprinkle the hot burek with water and cover it with a cloth for five minutes to soften the crust. Serve with yoghurt.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tavče gravče
description: White beans baked in a clay pan with onion, paprika and peppers. North Macedonia's national dish. (Тавче гравче)
instructions: Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water, bring it to the boil and drain again after ten minutes.
Cover them a third time, add one whole onion and boil an hour until soft, without salt.
Fry the sliced onion in oil until golden, take it off the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Pour off some of the bean water, leaving it level with the beans, salt them and stir in the onion mixture.
Transfer to a clay pan, arrange the dried peppers on top and scatter with mint.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, until a browned crust forms on top.
Rest ten minutes and serve straight from the pan, scattered with parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Selsko meso
description: Pork stewed with mushrooms, onion and wine in an individual clay pot, under cheese. (Селско месо)
instructions: Brown the diced pork in oil on all sides.
Add the onion and pepper and fry until soft, seven minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook over a high heat for five minutes, until their water has gone.
Take it off the heat, stir in the paprika, garlic and tomato paste, add the wine and return it to the heat for three minutes.
Divide between clay pots, top up with water to the level of the meat, season and cover.
Bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes.
Take the lids off, cover with grated kashkaval and give it ten more minutes, to a browned cheese crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lamingtons
description: Cubes of sponge dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in desiccated coconut. (Lamingtons)
instructions: Beat the butter and sugar pale, add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the sifted flour with the baking powder and salt, alternating with the milk.
Pour into a square tin and bake at 180 °C for twenty-eight minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool it completely and leave the sponge uncovered overnight.
Cut it into five-centimetre cubes.
Whisk the icing sugar with the cocoa and hot milk to a thin icing that runs off a spoon in a stream.
Dip each cube on two forks, let it drain and roll it in coconut. Leave them to set for an hour.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Australian meat pie
description: A hand-sized pie with a thick beef filling: shortcrust base, puff lid, tomato sauce on top. (Meat pie)
instructions: Brown the beef in batches so it does not release its juices, and set it aside.
Fry the onion until soft, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes.
Return the meat, add the stock, Worcestershire sauce and tomato paste and stew forty minutes, until thick.
Cool the filling completely, ideally in the fridge.
Line the tins with shortcrust, trim the edges and fill them with the cold filling.
Cover with rounds of puff pastry, seal the edges and cut a vent in the middle.
Glaze with egg and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a deep golden lid.

image.credit: fir0002 flagstaffotos [at] gmail.com Canon 20D + Canon 17-40mm f/4 L

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pavlova
description: A meringue with a crisp shell and a marshmallow centre, under whipped cream and kiwifruit. (Pavlova)
instructions: Whisk room-temperature egg whites to soft peaks in a scrupulously dry, grease-free bowl.
Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, still whisking, until the meringue is stiff and glossy.
Rub some between your fingers: if you feel sugar grains, keep going, or the shell will weep syrup.
Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla with a spatula, in three movements at most.
Shape a twenty-two centimetre circle on parchment, raising the edges and leaving a hollow in the middle.
Bake at 120 °C for ninety minutes, then turn the oven off and leave the pavlova inside until completely cold.
Whip the cream, spoon it into the hollow and top with kiwifruit, berries and passionfruit pulp just before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Hāngī-style chicken
description: Chicken and root vegetables wrapped and baked with smoked salt — a home version of the Māori earth oven. (Hāngī)
instructions: Rub the chicken with smoked salt and pepper and leave it half an hour.
Cut the sweet potato, potato and pumpkin into large pieces and the cabbage into quarters.
Wrap the wood chips in foil, pierce it in a few places and put the packet at the bottom of a deep tray.
Lay the vegetables on a rack above the chips, the chicken over them, season and dot with butter.
Seal the tray tightly with two layers of foil; no steam may escape.
Bake at 160 °C for two hours without opening it.
Take off the foil and let the chicken colour for ten minutes at 200 °C.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Poutine
description: Chips with cheese curds under hot gravy. The Québécois street classic. (Poutine)
instructions: Cut the potatoes into one-centimetre batons and soak them twenty minutes in cold water to lose the surface starch.
Dry the batons thoroughly. Wet potato spits in the fryer and never crusts.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook the roux to a nutty brown, four minutes.
Add both stocks, the Worcestershire sauce and the vinegar and simmer the gravy fifteen minutes, until thick.
Fry the potatoes at 150 °C for six minutes, until soft, and drain them on a rack.
Bring the oil to 190 °C and fry them a second time for three minutes, to a crisp shell. Salt them.
Pile the chips into a bowl, scatter the curds over them and pour on the boiling gravy. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tourtière
description: A double-crust pie of spiced pork and potato. The Québec Christmas table. (Tourtière)
instructions: Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add both minces and cook, breaking up lumps, for ten minutes.
Add all the spices, season, and pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for forty minutes, until the liquid has almost gone.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling completely.
Line a tin with pastry, add the cold filling and level it.
Cover with a second sheet, crimp the edges, cut vents and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200 °C for fifteen minutes, then at 180 °C for forty more, to a deep golden crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gallo pinto
description: Yesterday's rice fried with black beans and Salsa Lizano. The Costa Rican breakfast, every day. (Gallo pinto)
instructions: Fry the finely chopped onion, pepper and garlic in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and warm them three minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir, breaking up lumps with a spatula.
Add the Salsa Lizano, season and fry over medium heat for seven minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the chopped coriander and take it off the heat.
Serve with fried eggs, fried plantain and, if you like, soured cream or fresh cheese.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Casado
description: A lunch plate of rice, beans, salad, plantain and meat, each in its own sector. (Casado)
instructions: Marinate the chicken in lime juice, garlic, Salsa Lizano, salt and pepper for twenty minutes.
Cook the rice loose and warm the beans with a spoon of their liquid.
Dice the chayote and carrot small and stew them with garlic for ten minutes; that is the picadillo.
Fry the chicken over medium heat, six minutes a side.
Fry the ripe plantain slices to a caramel colour.
Toss the shredded cabbage with tomato, coriander, lime juice and salt.
Build the plate in sectors: rice, beans, chicken, picadillo, salad, plantain — unmixed.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Buuz
description: Large steamed dumplings of chopped mutton. The centrepiece of the Mongolian lunar new year. (Бууз)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Chop the mutton and fat by hand into pieces the size of a pea.
Mix the meat with the finely chopped onion, garlic, salt, pepper and a quarter cup of water.
Roll ten-centimetre rounds, leaving the middle thicker than the edges.
Put a spoon of filling in and pleat the edges around, leaving an opening at the top.
Grease the steamer rack with fat and set the buuz on it, not touching one another.
Steam eighteen minutes. The dough turns translucent and broth collects inside.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tsuivan
description: Home-made noodles steamed directly over the meat, then tossed through it. (Цуйван)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it thirty minutes.
Roll it thin, brush with fat, roll it up and cut across into half-centimetre strips.
Separate the strips by hand and spread them on a board so they do not stick.
Sear the mutton in the fat over a high heat, then add the onion, carrot, potato and cabbage.
Add a cup of water, season and bring it to the boil.
Lay the noodles in an even layer over the meat without stirring, cover and hold twenty minutes on a low heat.
Take the lid off, add the garlic and toss everything together. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kyrgyz beshbarmak
description: Mutton with home-made noodles in an onion sauce called chyk. The Kyrgyz version: mutton, and no potato. (Бешбармак)
instructions: Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim and simmer two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it forty minutes.
Roll it a millimetre thick and cut it into diamonds six centimetres across.
Render the mutton fat and cook the sliced onion in it until soft.
Add two ladles of broth to the onion and stew ten minutes into a thick gravy; that is the chyk.
Boil the dough diamonds in the strained broth in batches, four minutes each, and plate them straight away.
Pull the meat into sheets, lay it over the dough, spoon the chyk over and scatter with coriander. Serve the broth in bowls.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lagman
description: Hand-pulled noodles with a meat and vegetable sauce called vaja. A Dungan dish that became common across Central Asia. (Лагман)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour and warm salted water and work it fifteen minutes until smooth.
Divide it into ropes, oil them generously, coil them in a bowl and leave them an hour under film.
Stretch a rope, folding it in half and swinging it, until the strands are the thickness of a matchstick.
Sear the beef in very hot oil, then add the onion, cumin and ground coriander.
Add the vegetables in order: radish, beans, pepper, and the tomatoes and paste last.
Add a cup of boiling water, season and stew ten minutes; the vegetables should keep their bite.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water for three minutes, drain and divide between bowls. Vaja and coriander on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Qurutob
description: Flaky fatir bread soaked in reconstituted dried qurut, under fried onion and fresh vegetables. (Қурутоб)
instructions: Cover the qurut with hot water for twenty minutes and rub it by hand into an even liquid.
Pass it through a sieve to remove any grains. The liquid should be like thin soured cream.
Slice the onion into rings and fry it in oil until golden, ten minutes.
Tear the fatir into large pieces into a wide dish.
Pour the qurut over the bread and leave it five minutes to soak.
Top with the fried onion and its oil, then the tomato, cucumber and herbs.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tajik oshi palav
description: Pilaf with mutton, yellow carrot and a whole head of garlic, recognised by UNESCO as heritage. (Оши палав)

ingredients.text: 800 g Mutton (on the bone, in large pieces)

instructions: Rinse the rice through seven changes of water and soak it an hour in warm salted water.
Render the mutton fat in the cauldron and lift out the cracklings.
Brown the meat hard, add the onion and fry it golden.
Add the carrot and cook ten minutes, leaving it undisturbed for the first five so it heats rather than weeps.
Add boiling water two fingers above, along with the chickpeas, cumin, barberries and salt, and simmer the zirvak forty minutes.
Spread the rice in an even layer, press in the garlic heads and add boiling water a centimetre above the rice.
Cook on a high flame until the water has gone, mound the rice, pierce it to the bottom, cover and hold twenty minutes on the lowest heat.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kabuli pulao
description: Rice with lamb under a layer of caramelised carrot, raisins and almonds. Afghanistan's national dish. (قابلی پلو)
instructions: Soak the rice in salted water for two hours and rinse it until the water runs clear.
Fry the onion in oil until deep gold, add the meat and brown it.
Add a litre of water, the cardamom and salt and simmer an hour, until the meat is tender. Strain the broth.
Melt two spoons of sugar in a dry pan to a dark caramel and let it down carefully with a ladle of broth.
Fry the carrot with the rest of the sugar for five minutes until glossy, add the raisins and nuts and take it off.
Parboil the rice for five minutes and drain it.

Layer the rice over the meat in the pot, spoon over the caramel broth, dust with char masala, pierce to the bottom and hold covered thirty minutes on a low heat. Serve with the carrot and raisins on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Afghan mantu
description: Steamed dumplings of beef and onion under garlic yoghurt and a yellow split pea sauce. (منتو)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt, work it ten minutes and rest it forty under film.
Mix the mince with the finely chopped onion, salt, pepper and coriander. Add no water.
Boil the split peas forty minutes until soft, with a spoon of tomato paste and salt.
Crush the garlic with salt, stir it into the yoghurt and thin it with water to pouring consistency.
Roll the dough thin and cut it into eight-centimetre squares.
Add the filling and bring the corners together crosswise, leaving four open corners.
Steam twenty-five minutes. Set them on a layer of yoghurt, spoon over the pea sauce, more yoghurt, and dust with mint.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fattoush
description: A salad of vegetables and herbs with fried pieces of flatbread and sumac. (فتوش)
instructions: Tear the bread by hand into two-finger pieces and fry them in olive oil until browned.
Drain the bread on paper and dust it with half the sumac while it is still hot.
Cut the tomatoes, cucumbers and radishes into large uneven pieces; the salad should be rough rather than neat.
Tear the lettuce by hand and chop the herbs and spring onion.
Whisk a dressing from the lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, crushed garlic, the remaining sumac, oil and salt.
Toss the vegetables in the dressing, add the bread and serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kibbeh bil sanieh
description: Two layers of bulgur and meat with a filling of mince and pine nuts between them, baked in a tray. (كبة بالصينية)
instructions: Soak the bulgur in cold water for twenty minutes and squeeze it completely dry.
Blitz the lean beef with one onion to a paste and work in the bulgur, salt and half the spices.
Knead the mass five minutes, wetting your hands, until it is smooth and tacky.
Fry the remaining onion, add the minced lamb, the spices and the pine nuts and cook ten minutes.
Press half the mass into an oiled tray in a one-centimetre layer, smoothing it with a wet palm.
Spread the filling and cover with the other half of the mass, smoothed the same way.
Cut it into diamonds down to the base, pour over the olive oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, to a browned crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shuwa
description: Lamb in a spice paste, wrapped in leaves and cooked for a full day. Oman's dish for Eid. (شواء)
instructions: Grind the garlic, all the spices, the crushed dried limes, vinegar, oil and salt into a thick paste.
Cut deep slashes to the bone and rub the paste inside them and all over the outside.
Refrigerate overnight, twelve hours at least.
Wrap the meat in banana leaves, then tightly in two layers of foil. No gap may remain.
Set the parcel on a tray, pour a cup of water into the tray and bake at 130 °C for eight hours.
Unwrap it, pour off the juices and cook the rice in them. Pull the meat into threads by hand.
Serve the meat over the rice, from a shared platter, eaten by hand.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mishkak
description: Meat on skewers in a tamarind and spice marinade, grilled over coals at the roadside. (مشكاك)

ingredients.text: 800 g Beef or lamb (in small cubes)

instructions: Mix the tamarind, crushed garlic and ginger, all the spices, oil and salt into a marinade.
Cut the meat into one-and-a-half-centimetre cubes and coat it in the marinade.
Refrigerate for at least four hours, ideally overnight.
Thread the pieces onto skewers packed close, without gaps.
Get the coals hot — you should not be able to hold a palm above the grate for more than three seconds.
Grill a minute and a half on each of four sides, basting with the leftover marinade.
Slide the meat off the skewers into flatbread, add raw onion and serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sudanese ful
description: Ful beans cooked soft and mashed in the pot, with sesame oil, cheese and egg. (فول سوداني)
instructions: Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water and boil ninety minutes, until completely soft.
Pour off most of the water, leaving half a cup, salt the beans and mash them about halfway.
Crush the garlic with salt and cumin and stir it through the beans.
Turn them into a wide bowl and pour the sesame oil over without stirring it in.
Scatter over the crumbled cheese, chopped tomato, onion, chilli and halved eggs.
Serve with lemon and flatbread. It is eaten by hand from the shared bowl.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Asida with mulah
description: A stiff porridge of sorghum or wheat, served with stewed meat in a dried okra sauce. (عصيدة)
instructions: Brown the meat with the onion and garlic, then add the tomato paste and coriander.
Add water, season and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the peanut butter and rain in the ground okra in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook the sauce ten minutes; it turns thick and stringy.
Bring a litre of salted water to the boil, set a cup aside and rain in the flour, working it with a stick.
Work it fifteen minutes, adding the reserved water, until the mass is dense and smooth.
Turn the asida onto a platter with a wet spoon, make a hollow and pour the mulah into it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Zanzibar pilau
description: Rice with beef on the island's spices: clove, cardamom, cinnamon and black pepper, and no turmeric at all. (Pilau)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Simmer the beef with half the spices for forty minutes, until tender. Keep the broth.
Fry the onion in oil over medium heat for twenty minutes, to a deep brown, almost black.
Add the garlic, ginger and the remaining spices and warm them two minutes.
Add the cooked meat and the diced potato, stir and warm through five minutes.
Add the rice, pour in broth at one and a half times the volume of the rice, and season.
Bring it up, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without lifting the lid. Rest it ten minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ndizi na nyama
description: Green bananas stewed with beef in coconut milk. A Chagga dish from the slopes of Kilimanjaro. (Ndizi na nyama)
instructions: Brown the beef, add the onion, garlic and ginger and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes and curry powder and cook five minutes, until the tomatoes break down.
Add water level with the meat, season and stew thirty minutes, covered.
Peel the bananas under running water and cut them into thick rounds.
Add the bananas to the pot and cook twenty minutes, until tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm five minutes without letting it boil. Scatter with coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shorshe ilish
description: Hilsa in a ground mustard sauce, cooked by steaming. The great fish of Bengal. (সরষে ইলিশ)

ingredients.text: 60 g Mustard seeds (yellow and black in equal parts)

instructions: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for twenty minutes.
Grind them with two chillies, a pinch of salt and a little water into a smooth paste.
Rub the fish steaks with turmeric and salt and leave them ten minutes.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off and let it cool a minute; raw mustard oil is acrid.
Add the nigella, pour in the mustard paste let down with half a cup of water, and cook three minutes.
Lay the fish in a single layer, add the remaining chillies whole, cover and stew twelve minutes.
Finish with a spoon of raw mustard oil, take it off the heat and serve with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bhuna khichuri
description: Rice and lentils fried before the water goes in. Bengali food for a rainy day. (ভুনা খিচুড়ি)
instructions: Dry-roast the moong dal for five minutes, to a nutty smell, and rinse it.
Rinse the rice and dry it. Wet rice will not toast; it steams in its own water.
Heat the ghee, brown the potatoes and lift them out.
In the same ghee fry the bay, cinnamon and cardamom, then the onion and ginger until golden.
Add the rice and dal with the turmeric and cumin and toast them five minutes, stirring.
Add boiling water at twice the volume of the grain, return the potatoes, season and add the whole chillies.
Cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat, then let it stand ten minutes without opening it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Larb
description: Chopped meat with toasted rice powder, herbs and lime. The national dish of Laos. (ລາບ)

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Sticky rice (raw, for the powder)
300 g Lettuce and raw vegetables (to serve)

instructions: Toast the raw sticky rice in a dry pan for ten minutes, to a deep gold, stirring.
Grind the cooled rice in a mortar or mill to a coarse powder.
Chop the pork fine with a knife, but not to a paste; the pieces should stay distinguishable.
Cook the meat in a pan with two spoons of water over medium heat for five minutes, breaking up lumps.
Take it off the heat and let it cool to warm, about five minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, chilli, shallot and rice powder.
Add the herbs, toss and serve with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tam mak hoong
description: Green papaya salad pounded in a mortar. The Lao version, made with fermented fish padaek. (ຕຳໝາກຫຸ່ງ)
instructions: Peel the papaya and shred it into long fine strips with a knife or a som tam grater.
Pound the garlic and chillies in the mortar into a coarse paste.
Add the cut beans and bruise them lightly with the pestle.
Add the tomatoes and crush them until their juice runs.
Add the padaek, lime juice and palm sugar and mix with the pestle and a spoon.
Add the papaya and work the pestle, turning with the spoon, for two minutes, until the fibres soften.
Taste and adjust for sourness, salt and heat. Serve with sticky rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Souvla
description: Large pieces of pork or lamb on a spit, turning slowly over coals for two hours. (Σούβλα)
instructions: Cut the meat into large pieces of about two hundred grams, keeping the fat; it is needed.
Salt and pepper them generously all over and leave them half an hour at room temperature.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides, leaving the centre clear. Direct heat under the meat is not wanted.
Thread the pieces onto the spit, leaving a centimetre between them.
Turn the spit slowly and continuously for two hours. The meat should darken gradually rather than crust at once.
Dust with oregano ten minutes before the end and squeeze lemon over.
Take it off, cut it coarsely and serve in pita with onion, tomato and parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Grilled halloumi with watermelon
description: Cypriot cheese seared to a crust, with cold watermelon and mint. The island's summer plate. (Χαλλούμι)
instructions: Soak the halloumi in cold water for fifteen minutes, drain it and pat it completely dry.
Cut the cheese into centimetre slices — thinner and it dries out, thicker and it will not heat through.
Cut the chilled watermelon into large cubes and keep it in the fridge until serving.
Heat a dry pan hard and sear the halloumi two minutes a side, to dark stripes.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, honey and pepper.
Arrange the watermelon, rocket and hot cheese, spoon over the dressing and scatter with mint. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Maltese rabbit stew
description: Rabbit stewed in red wine with garlic and bay. The national dish of Malta. (Stuffat tal-fenek)
instructions: Cover the jointed rabbit with the wine, half the garlic and the bay leaves and refrigerate for a day.
Lift out the meat, dry it and brown it in olive oil. Keep the marinade.
Fry the onion and remaining garlic until soft, add the tomato paste and cook three minutes.
Return the meat, pour in the marinade, season and stew covered for an hour on a low heat.
Add the potato and carrot and stew twenty-five minutes more.
Add the peas for the last ten minutes.
Ladle off some of the sauce and dress spaghetti with it as a first course. The meat follows.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pastizzi
description: Flaky pastries filled with ricotta or mushy peas. Maltese street food on every corner. (Pastizzi)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt, work it ten minutes and rest it half an hour.
Boil the split peas with the onion for forty minutes until completely soft, mash them and season.
Mix the ricotta with the eggs, parsley, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin, spread it with fat, roll it up and chill it twenty minutes.
Cut the roll into pieces and flatten each into a round; the layers give the flakiness.
Add the filling and seal them: ricotta as an open-topped boat, peas as a closed diamond.
Bake at 220 °C for thirty minutes, to a deep gold, and serve hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chivito
description: A sandwich of thin steak, ham, bacon, cheese and a fried egg. Uruguay's national dish. (Chivito)
instructions: Pound the beef under film to four millimetres and season it.
Fry the bacon crisp and drain it on paper.
Get the pan very hot and sear the steaks forty-five seconds a side.
Lay the cheese on the meat in the pan and cover it for thirty seconds so it softens.
Fry the eggs with runny yolks and toast the cut buns in a dry pan.
Spread mayonnaise on both halves and layer lettuce, tomato, the steak with its cheese, ham, bacon and the egg.
Close it, spear it with a cocktail stick and an olive, and serve with chips.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Milanesa a la napolitana
description: A breaded cutlet under tomato sauce, ham and melted cheese. (Milanesa a la napolitana)
instructions: Pound the meat to five millimetres and season it.
Beat the eggs with crushed garlic and chopped parsley; that garlic in the egg wash is the Uruguayan touch.
Dip the pieces in the egg, then press them firmly into the breadcrumbs.
Let the coating set for fifteen minutes in the fridge.
Fry in hot oil three minutes a side, to a golden crust, and drain on a rack.
Lay the milanesas on a tray, spoon on the tomato sauce, cover with ham and cheese and dust with oregano.
Grill for four minutes, until the cheese melts and colours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pepián
description: Chicken in a thick sauce of toasted seeds and chillies. One of Guatemala's oldest dishes. (Pepián)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with an onion and salt for forty minutes. Keep the broth.
Toast the pumpkin and sesame seeds in a dry pan to a deep gold, stirring.
In the same pan char the chillies, tomatoes, tomatillos and garlic until blackened in patches.
Blend everything with two ladles of the broth and the cinnamon to a smooth sauce.
Pass the sauce through a sieve; the chilli skins left behind would spoil the texture.
Cook the sauce twenty minutes, stirring, until it thickens and darkens.
Add the chicken, potato and beans and stew fifteen minutes. Serve with rice and coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Guatemalan tamales
description: Corn dough with meat and recado sauce, wrapped in banana leaf and steamed. (Tamales)
instructions: Simmer the pork with the onion and salt for an hour. Strain and keep the broth.
Toast the seeds, sesame, chillies and tomatoes in a dry pan and blend them with broth; that is the recado.
Cook the recado twenty minutes to thicken it and season.
Slake the masa harina with warm broth, add the melted lard and work it twenty minutes over a low heat.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame for ten seconds each so they turn pliable.
On a leaf spread the dough, then a piece of meat, a spoon of recado, a strip of pepper and an olive. Wrap in two leaves.
Stack the parcels seam down in a pot and steam them for an hour and a half.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Dominican sancocho
description: A thick soup of several meats and root vegetables. Celebration food, cooked for a crowd. (Sancocho)
instructions: Marinate all the meats in lime juice, crushed garlic, oregano, salt and pepper for an hour.
Brown the meats in batches in a large pot.
Add the onion and pepper, cover with three litres of water and simmer an hour.
Add the cassava and yautía in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the sweet potato, plantain and corn and cook twenty minutes more.
Mash a couple of pieces of cassava in the pot so the soup thickens.
Stir in the coriander, check the salt and serve with white rice and avocado.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mangú
description: Mashed boiled green plantain with pickled onion, egg, fried cheese and salami. (Mangú)
instructions: Peel the plantains under water, halve them and boil in salted water for twenty minutes, until soft.
Set aside a cup of the cooking water and cool it.
Pickle the sliced onion in vinegar with salt and leave it fifteen minutes.
Mash the hot plantain with butter, adding the cold water, to a smooth purée.
Fry slices of salami and cheese in a dry pan until browned.
Fry the eggs and build the plate: purée, the onion and its vinegar on top, salami, cheese and egg alongside.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Doubles
description: Two soft fried breads called bara with spiced chickpea channa between them. Trinidad's street breakfast. (Doubles)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm water, add the flour, turmeric and salt and knead a soft dough.
Let the dough rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Boil the chickpeas with garlic for an hour, until completely soft.
Fry the onion, add the curry powder and cumin, warm them a minute and stir in the chickpeas with half their liquid.
Mash a third of the chickpeas in the pot and cook ten minutes to thicken the sauce.
Divide the dough into small balls, rest them twenty minutes and flatten them by hand into discs.
Fry the baras twenty seconds a side in hot oil; they must stay soft. Put the channa between two baras and serve with tamarind.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Callaloo
description: A thick purée of taro leaves with okra and coconut milk. The Trinidadian Sunday table. (Callaloo)
instructions: Wash the leaves, strip the tough stems and chop them coarsely.
Fry the onion and garlic in butter until soft.
Add the leaves, okra, pumpkin, thyme and the whole scotch bonnet, and cover with water two fingers above.
Simmer forty minutes covered. No less: raw taro leaves burn the mouth.
Remove the chilli and thyme, add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Break the soup down with a swizzle stick or a masher to a thick but not perfectly smooth purée.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tavë kosi
description: Lamb baked under a thick yoghurt custard with egg and rice. Albania's national dish. (Tavë kosi)
instructions: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes, dotted with butter.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour and cook two minutes to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt, add the flour mixture and beat until completely smooth.
Stir in the rice. It takes up some of the moisture and keeps the custard from splitting.
Arrange the meat and its juices in a dish and pour the yoghurt mixture over.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, until the top colours and the centre still trembles slightly.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Byrek me spinaq
description: A pie of thin pastry layered with spinach and brined cheese, each layer soaked in oil. (Byrek me spinaq)
instructions: Scald the spinach with boiling water, drain it and wring it out dry by hand.
Chop the spinach and mix it with the crumbled cheese, spring onion, dill and pepper. Salt cautiously; the cheese is salty.
Oil a tin and lay in three sheets of filo, brushing each one.
Spread a third of the filling, cover with two oiled sheets and repeat twice more.
Finish with three sheets on top, tuck the edges in and brush generously with oil.
Score it into squares down to the base with a sharp knife; cutting it after baking will not work.
Bake at 190 °C for forty-five minutes, to a deep golden crisp crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Plăcintă
description: A flat pie of stretched dough with cheese, pumpkin or apple, cooked in a dry pan. (Plăcintă)
instructions: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt, and work it ten minutes.
Divide it into six balls, oil them generously and leave them under film for forty minutes.
Mash the cheese with the egg and dill. Grate the pumpkin and mix it with sugar for the second filling.
Stretch a ball by hand on an oiled table into a thin round, until it turns translucent.
Put the filling in the middle and fold the edges to the centre, into a parcel or a round.
Flatten it with your palm to a centimetre and a half.
Cook in a hot dry pan four minutes a side, to a mottled crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Zeamă
description: Chicken soup with home-made noodles, soured with bran borș. The Moldovan remedy for everything. (Zeamă)

ingredients.text: 400 ml Bran borș (or juice of 2 lemons)

instructions: Cover the chicken with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Simmer forty minutes on a low heat with a whole onion.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour and eggs, roll it thin, let it dry and cut it into fine noodles.
Lift out the chicken and joint it, and add the carrot, pepper and potato to the broth.
After fifteen minutes add the noodles and cook five minutes.
Boil the borș separately, strain it and pour it into the soup. Cook five minutes.
Return the meat, season and stir in the lovage and parsley. Let it stand ten minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Judd mat Gaardebounen
description: Smoked pork collar, soaked and boiled, with broad beans in a cream sauce. Luxembourg's national dish. (Judd mat Gaardebounen)
instructions: Soak the meat in cold water for four hours, changing the water twice.
Cover it with fresh water, bring it up, boil ten minutes and drain.
Cover it again, add the bay leaves and simmer an hour and twenty, until tender. Keep the broth.
Pod the beans, scald them for a minute and slip the skin off each one.
Render the bacon, fry the onion in its fat, stir in the flour and cook two minutes.
Add two ladles of the broth and the cream, then the savory and the beans, and stew ten minutes.
Cut the meat into thick slices and serve with the beans and boiled potatoes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gromperekichelcher
description: Potato fritters with onion and parsley, deep-fried crisp. Christmas market food. (Gromperekichelcher)
instructions: Grate the potatoes, onions and shallots coarsely into one bowl.
Wring the mixture out in a cloth, but not bone dry; a little moisture is needed.
Mix in the eggs, flour, chopped parsley, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 175 °C. Hotter, and the edges burn before the middle is hot.
Drop the mixture in by the spoonful, flattened to half a centimetre, and fry three minutes a side.
Drain on a rack, salt them and serve hot with apple sauce.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Dograma
description: Crumbled flatbread with mutton and onion under hot broth. The Turkmen dish of Eid al-Adha. (Dogroma)
instructions: Cover the mutton with cold water, bring it up and skim thoroughly.
Simmer two hours with the bay, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Lift out the meat, cool it and pull it into threads by hand, discarding bones and sinew.
Crumble the flatbread by hand into pieces the size of a fingernail. Do not cut it.
Slice the onion thin and work it with a pinch of salt so it softens.
Mix the bread, meat and onion dry in a large bowl, and season.
Divide between bowls and pour over the strained boiling broth immediately before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ichlekli
description: A large closed pie of mutton and onion baked in ashes. The dish of Turkmen herders. (Içlekli)
instructions: Knead a stiff unleavened dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it under a cloth for thirty minutes.
Dice the mutton and fat small with a knife, and chop the onion as fine as you can.
Mix the meat, fat, onion, cumin, salt and pepper. Add no water; the onion supplies the juice.
Divide the dough in two, roll the larger piece into a round and line an oiled tin, leaving an overhang.
Spread the filling evenly, cover with the second sheet and seal the edges in a firm rope.
Make a small steam hole in the centre, brush with butter and cover with foil.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour under the foil, then uncover and give it ten more minutes to colour.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kabsa
description: Rice with chicken in a spiced broth with dried lime and tomato. The centrepiece of the Saudi table. (كبسة)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee until golden, then add the garlic, cardamom and cinnamon.
Brown the chicken on all sides, then add the tomato paste, tomatoes, carrot and baharat.
Pierce the dried limes, drop them in, add water and simmer thirty minutes.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and put it under the grill for ten minutes, to a browned skin.
Add the rice to the broth at one and a half times its volume in liquid, season, and cook twenty minutes covered.
Fry the almonds and raisins in ghee, mound the rice on a platter, set the chicken on it and scatter the nuts over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jareesh
description: Cracked wheat cooked with meat to a thick porridge, under fried onion. (جريش)
instructions: Soak the cracked wheat in cold water for two hours and rinse it.
Fry one onion in ghee, add the meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes, baharat and pierced limes, cover with water and cook forty minutes.
Add the wheat, top up with water two fingers above and cook ninety minutes on a low heat, stirring.
Remove the bones, stir in the yoghurt and beat the porridge with a spoon or a mixer until creamy and uniform.
Fry the remaining onion dark brown and spoon it over the jareesh with its oil.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Saltah
description: A meat stew served boiling in a stone pot under a whipped fenugreek froth called hulba. (سلتة)
instructions: Drain the soaked fenugreek, rinse it several times and grind it to a paste.
Whip the paste with cold water for ten minutes, by whisk or mixer, until it turns into a white froth.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the meat and brown it.
Add the tomatoes and potato, cover with water, season and stew an hour, until the meat is tender.
Heat a stone or cast-iron pot until very hot and transfer the boiling stew into it.
Break the eggs into the boiling stew and stir; they set into threads.
Spoon the hulba and a spoon of zhug on top and carry it to the table still bubbling. Serve with bread and rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bint al-sahn
description: A many-layered enriched bread brushed with ghee, drenched in honey and scattered with nigella. (بنت الصحن)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, eggs, yeast mixture, salt and two spoons of ghee, and work it fifteen minutes.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Divide it into ten balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under film.
Stretch the first ball by hand to the size of the tin, lay it in and brush it generously with ghee.
Repeat with the rest, buttering every layer. Brush the top one too and scatter it with nigella.
Bake at 190 °C for thirty-five minutes and pour the honey over immediately, while the bread is hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Machboos
description: Rice with prawns or chicken on the bizar spice mix with dried lime. The staple of the Gulf. (مجبوس)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee to a deep gold, fifteen minutes, and set a third aside.
Add the garlic, ginger, bizar and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the pierced limes, pour in water at one and a half times the volume of the rice, and season.
Bring it up, add the rice, cover and cook fifteen minutes on a low heat.
Lay the prawns over the rice, cover and give it five more minutes; they cook in the steam.
Rest it ten minutes and scatter with the reserved onion, coriander and chilli.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Luqaimat
description: Crisp balls of yeasted batter in date syrup. The Ramadan sweet of the Gulf. (لقيمات)
instructions: Steep the saffron in a spoon of warm water and leave it.
Mix the flour, cornflour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt.
Add the yoghurt, warm water and saffron infusion and whisk to a smooth loose batter.
Leave it somewhere warm for an hour; the batter should rise and bubble.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and drop the batter in by the teaspoon, dipping it in water each time.
Fry in batches for three to four minutes, moving them with a slotted spoon, to a deep gold.
Drain on paper, pour over the date syrup and scatter with sesame. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Murabyan
description: Kuwaiti rice with prawns in a broth of their own shells, with dill and dried lime. (مربيان)
instructions: Peel the prawns and keep the shells and heads.
Fry the shells in a spoon of ghee for five minutes, cover with a litre of water and simmer twenty minutes. Strain.
Rinse the rice and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee until golden, then add the garlic, turmeric and bizar.
Add the tomatoes, the pierced limes and half the dill, pour in the prawn broth and season.
Add the rice, cover and cook fifteen minutes on a low heat without opening it.
Lay the prawns and the rest of the dill on top, cover and give it five minutes. Rest ten and serve.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Harees
description: Wheat and meat cooked down and beaten into one smooth mass. Ramadan food across the Gulf. (هريس)
instructions: Soak the wheat overnight in cold water and rinse it.
Cover the meat with three litres of water, bring it up and skim.
Add the wheat, cinnamon and cardamom and simmer two hours.
Remove the bones and whole spices, season, and cook an hour more, stirring and topping up with boiling water.
Beat the mass with a wooden spoon or a mixer until entirely smooth — twenty minutes of work.
Spread it in a dish, make a hollow, pour in melted ghee and scatter with fried onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ndolé
description: Bitter leaves with peanut paste, meat and prawns. The national dish of Cameroon. (Ndolé)
instructions: Boil the leaves in salted water for ten minutes, wring them out and repeat twice more with fresh water.
Boil the peanuts twenty minutes until soft and blend them with water into a thick paste.
Brown the beef, then add the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli.
Add water and the dried shrimp and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the peanut paste and cook fifteen minutes, stirring; it catches easily.
Add the drained leaves and the fresh prawns and stew ten minutes more.
Serve with fried plantain or boiled cassava.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Poulet DG
description: Fried chicken with fried plantain and vegetables. The dish called "the director general's chicken". (Poulet DG)
instructions: Marinate the chicken in crushed garlic, ginger, thyme, salt and pepper for half an hour.
Fry the chicken in oil until browned all over and lift it out.
Cut the plantain into large pieces and fry it in the same oil, to caramelised edges.
Pour off most of the oil and fry the onion, tomatoes and pepper until soft.
Return the chicken, add the carrot, beans and the whole scotch bonnet, pour in a cup of water and stew twenty minutes.
Remove the chilli, fold in the plantain and warm it three minutes. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Attiéké with fish
description: Steamed fermented cassava couscous with grilled fish and a sharp onion salad. (Attiéké)
instructions: Grind the garlic, ginger, chilli, stock cube, salt and oil into a paste.
Slash the fish at the sides and rub the paste inside the cuts and over the skin. Leave it twenty minutes.
Break up the attiéké with your hands, sprinkle it with hot water and salt it.
Cover it and let it steam ten minutes, in a steamer or simply covered somewhere warm.
Slice the onion, tomatoes and chilli and mix them with lemon juice, salt and a spoon of oil.
Grill the fish over coals or in a griddle pan, seven minutes a side.
Serve the attiéké, fish and salad on one plate, with a wedge of lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kedjenou
description: Chicken cooked in a sealed clay pot without water. An Ivorian dish of slow heat. (Kedjenou)
instructions: Cut the onion, tomatoes, aubergines and pepper into large pieces.
Put the chicken and all the vegetables into the pot with the garlic, ginger, thyme, bay, salt and pepper.
Lay the whole scotch bonnet on top, uncut.
Cover it and seal the join with a rope of flour-and-water dough, or wrap it in foil.
Set it over the lowest heat or in a 160 °C oven for an hour and twenty.
Every fifteen minutes shake the pot, holding the lid down. Do not open it once.
Break the seal, remove the chilli and serve with attiéké or rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Matapa
description: Cassava leaves pounded with peanuts and coconut milk, with prawns. Mozambique's national dish. (Matapa)
instructions: Wash the leaves, strip the tough stems and pound them to a paste in a mortar.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until soft and add the tomatoes.
Stir in the leaves, add water to the same level and cook forty minutes on a low heat.
Add the ground peanuts and cook twenty minutes more, stirring.
Add the prawns, the whole piri-piri and salt and stew ten minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without letting it boil.
Serve with rice or with xima, the maize porridge.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Piri-piri chicken
description: Chicken spatchcocked and grilled over coals under a sauce of piri-piri, garlic and lemon. (Frango à cafreal)
instructions: Cut the chicken along the backbone, open it out and press it flat.
Blend the chillies, garlic, the juice of two lemons, paprika, vinegar, oregano, oil and salt.
Pour half the sauce into a separate bowl; that half is for basting.
Coat the chicken with the rest, working it under the skin, and refrigerate overnight.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat has to be indirect.
Grill the chicken skin up for thirty minutes, then turn it and give it fifteen more.
For the last five minutes baste with the reserved sauce mixed with melted butter. Serve with lemon.
