author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Romazava
description: Meat in broth with brèdes mafana, a bitter green that makes the mouth tingle. (Romazava)
instructions: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add both meats and the tomatoes and warm them through, without browning.
Add a litre and a half of water, season and simmer an hour.
Wash the greens and chop them coarsely, discarding tough stems.
Add the mustard greens and spinach and cook ten minutes.
Add the mafana for the last five minutes; long cooking weakens its effect.
Serve in deep bowls with a large helping of boiled rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ravitoto
description: Pounded cassava leaves stewed with pork and coconut milk. (Ravitoto sy henakisoa)
instructions: Brown the pork in large pieces on all sides.
Add the onion, garlic and ginger and fry until soft.
Stir in the cassava leaves, add water to the same level and season.
Stew covered for an hour on a low heat, stirring every fifteen minutes.
Uncover and drive off the excess liquid; the dish should be thick rather than soupy.
Add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling. Serve with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Baleadas
description: A wheat flour tortilla folded over refried beans, soured cream and crumbled cheese. (Baleadas)
instructions: Rub the flour with the fat and salt to a crumb, add the hot water and knead a soft dough.
Divide it into eight balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under a cloth.
Fry the onion in oil, add the cooked beans with some of their liquid and mash them smooth.
Fry the purée over medium heat for ten minutes, until it holds its shape on a spoon.
Roll the balls into thin twenty-centimetre rounds.
Cook them on a hot dry pan a minute a side, to spotted but not dried out.
Spread beans over half the tortilla, add cream and cheese, fold it over and serve hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Conch soup
description: Conch soup in coconut milk with cassava and plantain. The Garifuna cooking of the Caribbean coast. (Sopa de caracol)
instructions: Pound the conch with a mallet and cut it into small pieces. Squeeze lime over it.
Fry the onion, garlic and pepper in oil with the achiote until soft.
Add half the coconut milk let down with water and bring it up.
Add the conch and simmer forty minutes, until tender.
Add the cassava, plantain and carrot in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the remaining thick coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Scatter with coriander and serve with lime and fried plantain.

image.credit: Eugene Kim from San Francisco, USA

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nicaraguan gallo pinto
description: Rice fried with red beans. The Nicaraguan version: red beans, and no Salsa Lizano. (Gallo pinto)
instructions: Fry the onion, garlic and pepper in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and warm them three minutes.
Add the cold rice and stir, breaking up lumps with a spatula.
Fry over a high flame for eight minutes, leaving it undisturbed for the last three so a crust forms underneath.
Season and stir in the coriander.
Serve with fried plantain, cuajada cheese and a fried egg.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nacatamal
description: A large tamal of corn dough with pork, rice and potato, boiled in a banana leaf. (Nacatamal)
instructions: Marinate the pork overnight in sour orange juice, achiote, garlic, salt and pepper.
Soak the rice two hours and drain it.
Slake the masa harina with warm water, add the melted lard, achiote and salt, and work it fifteen minutes until smooth.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame so they turn pliable.
On a leaf place a large spoon of dough, then pork, rice, potato slices, onion, pepper, tomato, an olive and a mint leaf.
Wrap in two leaves into a tight parcel and tie it crosswise with string.
Boil them in a large pot for three hours, topping up with boiling water as it goes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Panamanian sancocho
description: Chicken soup with ñame root and culantro. Panama's cure for a hangover and for a cold. (Sancocho de gallina)
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt, garlic, oregano and lime juice and leave it twenty minutes.
Cover the chicken with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Add the onion and half the culantro and simmer an hour.
Peel the ñame, cut it into large pieces and add it to the pot with the corn.
Cook twenty-five minutes, until the ñame is soft.
Mash a couple of pieces of ñame in the broth so the soup thickens.
Stir in the remaining culantro, season and serve with a separate plate of white rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Panamanian ropa vieja
description: Shredded beef in tomato sauce with olives and capers, in the Panamanian style — drier than the Cuban. (Ropa vieja)
instructions: Simmer the beef whole in salted water with bay for an hour and a half. Keep the broth.
Cool the meat and pull it into long strands along the grain.
Fry the onion, pepper and garlic in oil until soft, eight minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cumin and oregano and cook ten minutes to thicken.
Fold in the meat, olives and capers and stew twenty minutes, adding broth a spoonful at a time.
Drive off any excess liquid uncovered; the sauce should coat the strands.
Scatter with culantro and serve with rice and fried plantain.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sopa paraguaya
description: A dense corn and cheese bake with onion which, despite its name, is eaten with a fork. (Sopa paraguaya)

ingredients.text: 500 g Paraguayan cheese or brined white cheese

instructions: Slice the onion thin and sweat it in the fat over a low heat for twenty minutes, until soft and sweet.
Pour the milk over the onion, take it off the heat and cool it to lukewarm.
Crumble the cheese and mix it with the corn flour and the sweetcorn kernels.
Stir in the onion and milk mixture and the yolks, salting cautiously; the cheese is salty already.
Whip the whites to firm peaks and fold them in with a spatula in three additions.
Spread the mixture into a greased tin in a four-centimetre layer.
Bake at 190 °C for fifty minutes, to a deep golden crust. Rest it twenty minutes before cutting.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chipa
description: Bread rings of cassava starch and cheese, with no wheat and no yeast. (Chipá)

ingredients.text: 400 g Paraguayan cheese or brined white cheese

instructions: Heat the oven to 220 °C in advance; the dough has to go into a hot one.
Beat the softened fat with the eggs and salt until smooth.
Work in the grated cheese and the aniseed, rubbing the mass with your hands until the cheese is evenly distributed.
Add the starch a little at a time, with the milk, until the dough is firm and pliable.
Roll ropes and join the ends into rings about eight centimetres across.
Bake twenty-five minutes, to browned patches. Serve warm.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Flia
description: A layered pie of thin batter, poured one layer at a time under a heated iron lid called a saç. (Flia)
instructions: Whisk the flour with the water and salt into a smooth thin batter — thicker than for pancakes, but pourable.
Let the soured cream down with cold water to the consistency of thin cream and salt it.
Butter a round tin and pour the batter in stripes from the centre outwards, like the spokes of a wheel.
Put it under the top grill for four minutes, until the layer sets and spots appear.
Sprinkle with the thinned cream and pour the next layer into the gaps between the previous stripes.
Repeat, alternating the direction of the stripes, until the batter runs out — usually twenty to twenty-five layers.
Pour over melted butter, rest it ten minutes and serve with yoghurt or honey.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tavë Elbasani
description: Lamb with rice under a yoghurt sauce, baked in an earthenware dish to a browned crust. (Tavë Elbasani)
instructions: Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes, to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt until completely smooth and add the flour mixture.
Spread the rice in an even layer in an earthenware dish and lay the meat and its juices on top.
Pour the yoghurt mixture over so it covers everything by a finger's depth.
Bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes, until the top browns and the middle still trembles slightly.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Njeguški steak
description: A pork chop with a pocket stuffed with Njeguši prosciutto and cheese, fried in breadcrumbs. (Njeguški stek)
instructions: Cut each piece along its length, stopping short of the far edge, and open it like a book.
Beat the opened meat lightly under film and season the inside.
Lay in a slice of prosciutto and a slab of cheese, close it and press the edges together.
Coat in flour, egg and crumbs, then repeat the egg and crumbs a second time.
Chill for twenty minutes; the coating sets and will not slide off in the pan.
Fry over medium heat, six minutes a side, to a deep gold.
Drain on a rack, rest it five minutes and serve with fried potatoes and lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kačamak
description: Maize porridge with potato, beaten with cheese and kajmak until it pulls into threads. (Kačamak)
instructions: Boil the cut potatoes in salted water for twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Without draining, rain in the maize flour in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook on a low heat for fifteen minutes, stirring with a wooden paddle; the porridge catches quickly.
Mash the potato in the pot together with the porridge until uniform.
Work in the crumbled cheese and kajmak, adding hot milk, and beat with the paddle for five minutes.
Turn it into a bowl, make a hollow and pour in melted butter. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ema datshi
description: Green chillies stewed in cheese. Bhutan's national dish, where chilli is a vegetable rather than a seasoning. (ཨེ་མ་དར་ཚིལ།)
instructions: Quarter the chillies lengthways. The seeds stay in; in Bhutan they are not removed.
Put the chillies, sliced onion, garlic and tomato in a pan and add water to the same level.
Bring it up and cook ten minutes, until the chillies soften.
Crumble the cheese in, drop the heat and leave it two minutes; it should begin melting on its own.
Stir it into a creamy sauce, add the butter and salt cautiously; the cheese is salty.
Serve with the red rice Bhutanese cook to a slightly sticky texture.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jasha maroo
description: Chopped chicken in a thin broth with ginger, garlic and chilli. Bhutanese everyday cooking. (ཇ་ཤ་མ་རུ།)
instructions: Chop the chicken through the bone into pieces about the size of a matchbox.
Pound the ginger and garlic to a coarse paste.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the paste and cook it two minutes.
Add the chicken and fry five minutes, until it whitens all over.
Add the tomatoes and chillies, pour in water a finger above and season.
Simmer twenty minutes; the broth should stay thin.
Stir in the coriander and serve in deep bowls with red rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mas huni
description: Tuna worked with coconut, onion and lime, with hot roshi flatbread. The Maldivian breakfast. (މަސް ހުނި)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.
Chop the onion, chillies and curry leaves as fine as you can.
Work the onion, chilli and salt with your hands until the onion releases its juice and softens.
Add the grated coconut and the flaked tuna and keep working it with your fingers until even.
Squeeze in the lime juice and mix again. Taste and adjust for salt and acidity.
Roll the dough into thin flatbreads and cook them on a dry pan a minute a side.
Serve the mas huni with the hot roshi and black tea.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Garudhiya
description: A clear broth of fresh tuna, cooked in water with salt and almost nothing else. (ގަރުދިޔަ)
instructions: Cut the tuna into large pieces and rinse them under cold water.
Cover with a litre and a half of cold water, salt it and bring it up.
Skim for the first five minutes; the clarity of the broth depends on it.
Add the curry leaves and pandan and cook twenty minutes on the lowest heat.
Remove the leaves, check the salt and take it off the heat.
Serve with rice, sliced onion, chilli and lime, each person adding them to their own bowl.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Matoke
description: Green bananas steamed in banana leaves and mashed to a purée. The staple of the Buganda table. (Matoke)
instructions: Peel the bananas with oiled hands; their sap stains the skin black.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame for ten seconds so they turn pliable.
Line the bottom of the pot with the leaf ribs; they keep the parcel off the water.
Wrap the bananas in the leaves into a tight parcel and set it on that platform.
Add water two fingers deep, cover and steam for an hour and twenty, topping up with boiling water.
Without unwrapping, press the parcel through the leaves into an even purée and return it to the steam for ten minutes.
Serve with peanut sauce or stewed beef, straight onto the leaf.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rolex
description: A vegetable omelette rolled in a chapati. Kampala street food, the name a slur of "rolled eggs". (Rolex)
instructions: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt and rest it twenty minutes.
Roll a ball thin, brush it with oil, roll it into a rope, coil it like a snail and roll it out again.
Cook the chapatis over medium heat, a minute and a half a side, and keep them under a cloth.
Shred the cabbage, carrot, onion, tomatoes and chilli as fine as you can.
Beat the eggs with the vegetables, salt and pepper; the vegetables belong inside the omelette, not on top.
Pour a portion of egg into the pan, let it set and lay a chapati on top, pressing it down.
Flip the two together, slide them onto a board omelette up and roll it tight.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sadza ne nyama
description: Stiff maize porridge with stewed beef and greens. The daily meal of Zimbabwe. (Sadza ne nyama)

ingredients.text: 800 g Beef (on the bone, in pieces)

instructions: Brown the meat, add the onion and garlic and fry until soft.
Add the tomatoes, cover with water to the same level, season and stew for an hour and twenty.
Shred the greens fine and stew them with tomato and peanut butter for fifteen minutes.
Slake a quarter of the maize meal in cold water and stir it into a litre of boiling water.
Cook that thin porridge for ten minutes, stirring with a wooden paddle.
Rain in the rest of the meal a little at a time, working it hard for fifteen minutes to a stiff mass.
Turn the sadza onto plates with a wet spoon and serve with the meat and greens.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Muriwo unedovi
description: Collard greens stewed in peanut butter with tomato. The side to sadza in every household. (Muriwo unedovi)
instructions: Strip the tough stems from the leaves, roll them up and shred them fine.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil until soft, five minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook seven minutes, until they collapse into a paste.
Let the peanut butter down with a cup of hot water until smooth and lump-free.
Stir in the greens and the slackened peanut butter, season and stew covered for twelve minutes.
Uncover and drive off the excess liquid; the sauce should cling to the leaves.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Poulet moambé
description: Chicken in a sauce of palm fruit pulp. The national dish of the Congo. (Poulet moambé)
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, garlic and lemon juice and leave it twenty minutes.
Brown the chicken in oil on all sides and lift it out.
Fry the onion with the ginger until soft, add the palm pulp and let it down with a cup of water.
Cook the sauce twenty minutes, stirring, until a layer of red oil rises to the surface.
Return the chicken, add the aubergine and the whole pili-piri and stew thirty minutes.
Stir in the spinach for the last five minutes and remove the chilli.
Serve with rice or with fufu made from cassava.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Liboke de poisson
description: Spiced fish wrapped in a banana leaf and baked in embers. (Liboke)
instructions: Slash the fish at the sides and rub it with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Grind the garlic, ginger and chilli to a paste and work it into the cuts and the cavity.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame so they turn pliable and stop cracking.
Lay tomato and onion slices on a leaf, the fish on them, then more tomato and spring onion.
Wrap in three leaves into a tight parcel and tie it with a strip of the same leaf.
Set the parcels on the coals and bake them fifteen minutes a side.
Serve them still in the leaf, with boiled cassava or rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tigadegena
description: Meat in a thick peanut sauce with vegetables. The Malian Sunday lunch. (Tigadèguèna)
instructions: Brown the meat in oil, add the onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add a litre and a half of water, season and cook forty minutes.
Slacken the peanut butter with two ladles of the broth until smooth and lump-free.
Pour the paste into the pot in a thin stream, stirring continuously.
Add the vegetables in large pieces and the whole chilli and stew thirty minutes, stirring.
Wait for the peanut oil to rise to the surface, remove the chilli and serve with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Grilled capitaine
description: Nile perch grilled whole over coals, with a yet onion sauce and fried plantain. (Capitaine braisé)

ingredients.text: 2 kg Nile perch or pike-perch (whole, gutted)

instructions: Cut deep slashes to the bone on both sides of the fish, every three centimetres.
Grind the garlic, ginger, chilli, stock cube, lemon juice and oil into a paste and work it into the cuts.
Leave the fish to marinate for an hour in the cold.
Slice the onions and sweat them in oil over a low heat for thirty minutes, to a caramel colour.
Stir the mustard and lemon juice into the onions and season; that is the yet sauce.
Grill the fish over indirect heat, twenty minutes a side.
Fry the plantain and serve the fish under the onion sauce, with the plantain and lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Osso buco alla milanese
description: Veal shin braised two hours in wine and stock, finished with a gremolata of zest and garlic. (Ossobuco alla milanese)
instructions: Tie each piece round its circumference with kitchen string so the meat stays on the bone.
Nick the membrane around the edge in two or three places, or the pieces curl as they brown.
Dust with flour and brown them in butter on both sides, four minutes a side.
Lift out the meat and soften the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery.
Add the wine and reduce it by half, scraping up what has caught on the bottom.
Return the meat, add stock to half the height of the pieces and braise covered for two hours on a low heat.
Mix the chopped zest, garlic and parsley and scatter it over the osso buco before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Melanzane alla parmigiana
description: Layers of fried aubergine with tomato sauce, mozzarella and parmesan, baked to a crust. (Melanzane alla parmigiana)
instructions: Slice the aubergines lengthways half a centimetre thick, salt them and press them under a weight for half an hour.
Pat the slices completely dry; wet ones spit in the oil and never crust.
Fry the aubergine in batches in olive oil, two minutes a side, and drain them on a rack.
Fry the garlic, add the tomatoes and cook the sauce twenty minutes to thicken, salting at the end.
Slice the mozzarella and leave it on paper to drain for ten minutes.
Layer it: sauce, aubergine, mozzarella, parmesan, basil — four times over.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes and let it stand twenty before cutting.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Hong shao rou
description: Pork belly braised in caramel and soy until it glistens. The classic of red-braising. (红烧肉)

ingredients.text: 900 g Pork belly (in 3 cm cubes, skin on)

instructions: Drop the pork cubes into boiling water for two minutes, drain and rinse them under cold water.
Dry the meat thoroughly. Wet, it spits in the caramel and cools it.
Melt the sugar in the oil over medium heat to an amber colour, stirring; it takes three or four minutes.
Add the meat and turn it for two minutes, until every cube is coated in the caramel.
Add the wine, both soy sauces, the ginger, spring onion and spices.
Add hot water level with the meat and braise covered for an hour on a low heat.
Uncover and reduce the sauce hard to a glaze, spooning it over the meat.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Cantonese steamed fish
description: A whole fish steamed with ginger and spring onion, finished with smoking oil and soy. (清蒸鱼)

ingredients.text: 800 g Sea bass or bream (whole, gutted)

instructions: Dry the fish, cut two slashes on each side and rub it with salt and wine.
Lay a few spring onion stalks on a plate and set the fish on them, so steam reaches it from below too.
Tuck half the ginger into the slashes and the cavity.
Set the plate into a boiling steamer and cook eight minutes for every centimetre of thickness.
Pour off all the liquid from the plate and discard it; it is bitter.
Scatter the remaining ginger, shredded spring onion and coriander over the top.
Heat the oil until it smokes and pour it over the aromatics, then pour the soy and sugar around the edge of the plate.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rogan josh
description: Kashmiri lamb in a yoghurt sauce with Kashmiri chilli, red from the chilli rather than from heat. (रोगन जोश)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Lamb on the bone (in pieces)

instructions: Warm the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves in the ghee until fragrant, one minute.
Add the asafoetida and the meat straight after, and brown it for ten minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the Kashmiri chilli; over a flame it burns in seconds and turns bitter.
Return it to a low heat and add the whisked yoghurt a ladle at a time, stirring between each.
Add the fennel and dry ginger, season, and pour in a cup of hot water.
Braise covered for an hour and twenty on a low heat, until the meat comes away from the bone.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until oil rises to the surface. Serve with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Masala dosa
description: A thin crisp crêpe of fermented rice and lentil batter with a spiced potato filling. (मसाला डोसा)
instructions: Soak the rice separately and the dal with the fenugreek separately, six hours each.
Grind the dal to a light fluffy paste, then the rice to a slightly grainy one, and combine them.
Salt it, cover it and leave it somewhere warm for eight to twelve hours, until it rises and smells sour.
Pop the mustard seeds in oil, then add the curry leaves, onion, chillies and ginger.
Add the turmeric and the crushed potato, season and warm it five minutes; that is the filling.
Heat a flat pan, wipe it with the oiled onion and pour a ladle of batter, spreading it in a spiral from the centre.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook until the underside browns, two minutes. Add the filling and fold it over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bouillabaisse
description: The Marseille fish soup of several species, with saffron and a rouille sauce. (Bouillabaisse)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Small bony rockfish (for the broth)
1.2 kg Firm white fish (three or four species)

instructions: Soften the onion, leek and fennel in olive oil for ten minutes.
Add the small fish whole, the tomatoes, garlic, zest and saffron and cook five minutes.
Add two litres of water, bring it up and cook forty minutes, uncovered.
Press everything through a sieve, working the flesh through, and return the broth to the pot.
Cook the potatoes in the broth for fifteen minutes, then add the larger fish in order, firmest first.
Make the rouille: egg yolk, garlic, saffron, a pinch of cayenne and olive oil in a thin stream.
Serve the broth in bowls with croûtes and rouille, and the fish with the potatoes on a separate platter.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tarte Tatin
description: An upside-down apple tart: the apples caramelise at the bottom, the pastry goes on top and becomes the base. (Tarte Tatin)
instructions: Peel the apples, halve them, core them and squeeze lemon over them.
Melt the sugar in a cast-iron pan over medium heat to an amber caramel, without stirring it with a spoon.
Take it off the heat and beat in the butter piece by piece, with the vanilla and a pinch of salt.
Pack the apple halves cut side up, tight against each other, in a circle.
Cook on the hob for twenty minutes over medium heat, until the apples sink and take up the caramel.
Cover with a round of puff pastry, tucking the edges down inside the pan, and prick it in several places.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, rest it five, and invert it onto a plate in one movement.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nikujaga
description: Beef and potato simmered in dashi with soy and mirin. The classic of Japanese home cooking. (肉じゃが)
instructions: Cut the potatoes into large pieces and soak them ten minutes in cold water to lose the surface starch.
Fry the onion in oil for two minutes, add the thinly sliced beef and cook until it loses its pink.
Add the potato and carrot and turn them so they take on the fat from the meat.
Add the dashi, sake and sugar, bring it up and skim.
Cover with an otoshibuta or a foil disc with a hole in it and simmer ten minutes over medium heat.
Add the soy and mirin and simmer fifteen minutes more, until only a little liquid is left at the bottom.
Add the beans for the last three minutes, take it off the heat and let it stand twenty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chawanmushi
description: A savoury egg custard set on dashi and steamed, with a prawn and mushrooms inside. (茶碗蒸し)
instructions: Beat the eggs with chopsticks without raising foam; the movement should cut rather than whip.
Add the cooled dashi, soy, mirin and salt and stir without whisking.
Strain the mixture twice through a fine sieve; that is the only route to smoothness.
Divide the prawn, a piece of chicken, a mushroom and a slice of kamaboko between the cups.
Pour in the custard, lift any bubbles off the surface with a spoon and cover with foil.
Steam gently for fifteen minutes with the steamer lid propped open a centimetre.
Test with a skewer: the liquid that rises should run clear. Scatter with herbs and serve hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mole poblano
description: Chicken in a dark sauce of several chillies, nuts, spices and chocolate. (Mole poblano)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with an onion and garlic for forty minutes. Strain and keep the broth.
Seed the chillies and toast them on a dry pan ten seconds a side, stopping short of blackening.
Cover the chillies with boiling water for twenty minutes to soften.
Fry the almonds, peanuts, sesame, raisins and bread in lard, one at a time and separately.
Char the tomatoes, tomatillos and garlic on a dry pan until blackened in patches.
Blend everything with broth in batches and pass it through a sieve twice.
Cook the sauce for an hour on a low heat, stirring, stir in the chocolate and salt, add the chicken and heat it through.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Cochinita pibil
description: Pork in an achiote and sour orange marinade, baked in banana leaves. (Cochinita pibil)
instructions: Slake the achiote paste with the juice of two oranges, the grapefruit and the lime to a thin slurry.
Add the crushed garlic, oregano, cumin, salt and pepper and mix it smooth.
Coat the pork in the marinade, working it in by hand, and refrigerate overnight.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame and line a deep dish with them, overlapping and with an overhang.
Put in the pork with its marinade, fold the leaves over and seal the dish with two layers of foil.
Bake at 150 °C for four hours without opening it.
Pickle the sliced red onion with the habanero in the juice of the remaining oranges. Shred the meat and serve with tortillas.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: İskender kebab
description: Slices of döner over pieces of pide, under tomato sauce, melted butter and yoghurt. (İskender kebap)
instructions: Slice the lamb very thin, season it and leave it twenty minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil, add the pepper paste and warm it a minute.
Add the passata and oregano and cook the sauce fifteen minutes to thicken it.
Cut the pide into cubes and dry them in the oven at 180 °C for eight minutes.
Sear the lamb slices over a very high flame in batches, a minute and a half each.
Spread the bread on the plates, spoon over some of the sauce, then the meat and the rest of the sauce.
Melt the butter until it sizzles and pour it over the meat. Put the yoghurt at the side and serve with fried peppers.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Turkish mantı
description: Tiny lamb dumplings, boiled and served under garlic yoghurt and paprika butter. (Mantı)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover it and rest it forty minutes, or the dough springs back as you roll it.
Mix the mince with the grated onion, salt and pepper and squeeze out the excess juice.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into two-centimetre squares.
Put a knife-tip of filling on each square and pinch the four corners up into a knot.
Boil the mantı in salted water for eight minutes and drain, keeping a ladle of the water.
Whisk the yoghurt with the garlic, plate the mantı, spoon the yoghurt over and pour on the paprika and mint butter.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fabada asturiana
description: Large white fabes beans stewed with chorizo, morcilla and cured pork. (Fabada asturiana)
instructions: Soak the beans twelve hours in cold water and drain them.
Put the beans, cured meats, onion, garlic and olive oil in a pot and cover with cold water by three fingers.
Bring it up, skim, and drop the heat until the surface barely trembles.
Cook two and a half hours, adding half a cup of cold water every thirty minutes.
Lift out the onion and garlic, crush them with the saffron and paprika and return them to the pot.
Salt it at the very end and let it stand half an hour before serving.
Lift out the meats, slice them and serve them on a separate platter, with the beans in a tureen.

image.credit: Juan J. Martínez from Valencia, España

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pulpo a feira
description: Boiled octopus on a wooden board with paprika, coarse salt and olive oil. (Pulpo á feira)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the onion and bay. Do not salt it.
Hold the octopus by the head and dip the tentacles into the boiling water for five seconds, then lift it out. Repeat three times.
Lower the octopus in whole and cook at a bare simmer for forty minutes.
Test with a fork at the thickest part of a tentacle: it should go in without resistance.
Turn off the heat and leave the octopus in the water for fifteen minutes; it finishes and softens further.
Boil the potatoes in the same water and cut them into rounds.
Cut the tentacles with scissors into centimetre pieces, lay them over the potato, dust with paprika and salt and pour over the oil.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Khao soi
description: Northern Thai noodles in coconut curry, boiled noodles in the broth and fried ones on top. (ข้าวซอย)
instructions: Set a fifth of the noodles aside, separate the strands and deep-fry them to a golden crisp.
Heat the thick part of the coconut milk in a pan, without stirring, until the oil separates out.
Fry the curry paste, curry powder and turmeric in that oil for three minutes, until deeply fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste until it is coated all over.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and some water, the fish sauce and the sugar, and simmer thirty minutes.
Boil the remaining noodles and divide them between bowls.
Ladle over the curry and chicken, top with the fried noodles, shallot, pickled greens, coriander and a wedge of lime.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Massaman curry
description: A mild curry of beef, potato and peanuts, built on spices of the Muslim tradition. (แกงมัสมั่น)
instructions: Heat the thick part of the coconut milk without stirring until the oil separates.
Fry the massaman paste in that oil for four minutes, until it darkens and smells right.
Add the beef and turn it in the paste, then add the cinnamon, cardamom and bay.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and stew gently for an hour, until the meat is tender.
Add the potato and onion in large pieces and cook twenty minutes more.
Stir in the tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce and taste: it should read sweet, sour and salty at once.
Add the peanuts, warm them five minutes and serve with jasmine rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gemista
description: Tomatoes and peppers stuffed with herbed rice and baked with potatoes in olive oil. (Γεμιστά)
instructions: Cut lids off the tomatoes and scoop out the flesh with a spoon without piercing the walls.
Blitz the flesh and add the sugar; it takes the edge off the tomato acidity.
Soften the onion in olive oil for ten minutes, until sweet.
Mix the raw rice with the onion, herbs, half the tomato purée, salt and pepper.
Fill the vegetables two-thirds full, cap them with their lids and set them in a dish.
Tuck potato wedges between them, pour over the remaining purée and douse it all with oil.
Bake covered with foil at 180 °C for an hour, then uncover and give it twenty minutes more.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Avgolemono
description: Chicken soup with rice, thickened with egg beaten into lemon juice. (Αυγολέμονο)
instructions: Cover the chicken with two and a half litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and simmer forty-five minutes.
Lift out the chicken, strain the broth and return it to the heat. Cook the rice in it for fifteen minutes.
Pull the meat into threads, discarding skin and bones.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice to an even froth in a separate bowl.
Ladle hot broth into the egg and lemon mixture, whisking without stopping, until the bowl warms up.
Pour the mixture back into the pot off the heat, return the meat and warm it through without boiling.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pelmeni
description: Small dumplings of unleavened dough with chopped meat and onion, boiled in broth. (Пельмени)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, iced water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Wrap it in film and refrigerate it forty minutes.
Chop the meat by hand or put it through a coarse plate, and mix it with the grated onion, salt and pepper.
Work the crushed ice into the filling and chill it twenty minutes.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut six-centimetre rounds.
Put a teaspoon of filling on each round, fold it into a half-moon, seal it and join the ends into a ring.
Boil them in salted broth with bay for four minutes after they surface, and serve with butter and soured cream.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Beef cut into strips and seared hard, in a soured cream sauce with onion. (Бефстроганов)

ingredients.text: 700 g Beef fillet (in strips across the grain)

instructions: Cut the beef across the grain into centimetre strips, pat them dry and pepper them.
Heat a pan hard and sear the beef in batches for ninety seconds, without turning it often.
Lift out the meat and fry the mushrooms over a high flame until their water has gone.
Add the butter and onion and fry until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the stock, stirring until smooth.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the soured cream and mustard, and season.
Return the meat with its juices, warm it a minute without boiling and scatter with parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Schweinshaxe
description: Pork knuckle roasted to a glassy crackling, with dark beer and sauerkraut. (Schweinshaxe)

ingredients.text: Coarse salt and pepper, to taste

instructions: Score the skin in diamonds every centimetre and a half, down to the fat but not into the meat.
Rub the knuckles with coarse salt, pepper, caraway and garlic, working it into the cuts.
Put them in a pot with the onion, carrot, celeriac and bay, and cover with beer and water.
Simmer for an hour, never letting it boil hard.
Move the knuckles to a tray, pat the skin dry and roast at 180 °C for an hour and twenty.
Every twenty minutes baste with beer from the pot and fat from the tray.
Raise the oven to 240 °C for the last ten minutes, until the crackling blisters.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Black Forest gateau
description: Chocolate sponge soaked in kirsch, with whipped cream and sour cherries. (Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte)
instructions: Whisk the eggs and sugar over a water bath until warm, then beat them ten minutes to a thick pale foam.
Sift the flour with the cocoa and fold it in with a spatula in three additions, then the melted butter.
Bake the sponge at 175 °C for thirty-five minutes and cool it completely, ideally overnight.
Cut the sponge into three layers and soak each with cherry syrup mixed with kirsch.
Dissolve the gelatine, whip the cream with the icing sugar and add the gelatine in a thin stream.
Assemble: sponge, cream, cherries, cream again — three times over, finishing with cream.
Cover the sides and top with chocolate shavings, decorate with cherries and chill four hours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pulled pork
description: Pork shoulder smoked ten hours at low heat and pulled into threads. (Pulled pork)

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Mustard (as a binder for the rub)
300 g Hickory or apple wood chips

instructions: Mix the paprika, sugar, mustard and garlic powders, cayenne, salt and black pepper.
Smear the shoulder with mustard as a binder and coat it all over in the dry rub.
Leave the meat in the fridge overnight, covered with film.
Bring the smoker or oven to 110 °C and take the meat out an hour ahead so it warms up.
Smoke it fat side up for six hours, spritzing with the vinegar and apple juice mix every hour.
When the internal temperature reaches 75 °C and stalls, wrap the meat in foil and return it to the heat.
Hold it to 95 °C inside, about four hours more, rest it an hour still wrapped, and pull it apart by hand.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Key lime pie
description: A condensed milk and lime filling on a cracker crumb base, set by acid rather than heat. (Key lime pie)
instructions: Crush the crackers to fine crumbs and mix them with the melted butter, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Press the crumbs into a tin, working them up the sides, and bake at 175 °C for ten minutes.
Beat the yolks with the zest of two limes until pale, about three minutes.
Add the condensed milk and beat three minutes more, until the mixture thickens.
Pour in the lime juice in a thin stream with the mixer running; the mixture thickens in the bowl.
Pour the filling into the base and bake at 160 °C for fifteen minutes, until the edges set and the centre still wobbles.
Cool it and chill it four hours, then top with cream whipped with the icing sugar.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bún chả
description: Charcoal-grilled pork in a warm sweet-sour broth, with rice vermicelli and herbs. (Bún chả)
instructions: Marinate the belly slices and the mince separately in fish sauce, sugar, shallot, garlic and pepper for an hour.
Shape the mince into flat patties a centimetre thick; they cook fast and evenly.
Slice the papaya and carrot thin and pickle them in vinegar with sugar for twenty minutes.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, water, garlic and chilli and warm it through; that is the nước chấm.
Boil the vermicelli two minutes, rinse it in cold water and divide it between plates.
Grill the belly and the patties over coals, three minutes a side, to caramelised edges.
Drop the hot meat straight into the warm sauce with the pickles and serve with the noodles, lettuce and herbs.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gỏi cuốn
description: Fresh rice paper rolls with prawn, pork, noodles and herbs, never fried. (Gỏi cuốn)
instructions: Simmer the pork belly in salted water for thirty minutes, cool it and slice it thin.
Boil the prawns two minutes, cool them and split each one lengthways.
Boil the vermicelli, rinse it in cold water and drain it well.
Let the peanut butter down with the hoisin, garlic and water to the thickness of pouring cream.
Dip a sheet of rice paper in warm water for two seconds and lay it on a damp cloth.
Lay two prawn halves cut side down in the upper third, and below them the lettuce, noodles, pork and herbs.
Fold the bottom up, tuck the sides in and roll it tight. Serve with the peanut sauce.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Galbijjim
description: Beef short ribs braised in soy with pear, until the meat falls from the bone. (갈비찜)
instructions: Soak the ribs in cold water for an hour, changing it twice, until the water runs clear.
Blanch the ribs in boiling water for five minutes, drain and rinse them under cold water.
Blend the pear, onion, garlic and ginger to a smooth purée.
Mix the purée with the soy, sugar, mirin and sesame oil and pour it over the ribs.
Bring it up, skim, and braise covered for an hour and a half on a low heat.
Add the carrot, daikon, mushrooms, chestnuts and jujubes and braise twenty-five minutes more.
Uncover and reduce the sauce to a gloss, spooning it over the ribs. Scatter with spring onion.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Samgyetang
description: A whole young chicken stuffed with glutinous rice and ginseng, simmered in its own broth. (삼계탕)
instructions: Soak the glutinous rice in cold water for two hours and drain it.
Rinse the birds, trim the excess fat at the cavity and pat them dry.
Fill each cavity two-thirds with rice, adding a ginseng root, garlic, a chestnut and a jujube.
Cross the legs and tuck one through a slit in the other; the cavity then closes without string.
Pack the birds into a pot and add cold water just to cover them.
Bring it up, skim, and simmer for an hour and a quarter.
Serve each bird in its own bowl of broth, with salt and pepper on a separate saucer.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Roast beef with Yorkshire pudding
description: A beef joint roasted whole, with an airy batter pudding baked in beef dripping. (Roast beef and Yorkshire pudding)
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest it an hour in the fridge.
Take the beef out of the fridge an hour before cooking, pat it dry and season it.
Sear the joint in a pan on all sides to a dark crust, two minutes a face.
Set it on the vegetables in a tray and roast at 200 °C for twenty minutes, then at 160 °C for forty more for a pink centre.
Lift the beef out, cover it with foil and rest it twenty minutes; it goes on cooking.
Heat the pudding tins with a spoon of dripping in each at 220 °C until the fat smokes.
Pour the cold batter halfway up the tins and bake twenty minutes without opening the door.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sticky toffee pudding
description: A moist date sponge under a hot sauce of cream and dark sugar. (Sticky toffee pudding)
instructions: Cover the chopped dates with a cup of boiling water and the bicarbonate and leave them fifteen minutes.
Mash the dates with a fork into a coarse paste, water and all.
Beat a hundred grams of the butter with a hundred and fifty of the sugar until pale, adding the eggs one by one.
Fold in the flour with the baking powder, then the date paste; the batter comes out loose, which is correct.
Pour it into a greased tin and bake at 180 °C for thirty-five minutes, to a skewer that comes out with moist crumbs.
Melt the remaining butter with the remaining sugar and the cream and cook the sauce five minutes to thicken.
Prick the warm sponge with a skewer, pour over half the sauce and serve the rest in a jug.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bigos
description: Sauerkraut and fresh cabbage stewed with several meats and dried fruit over three days. (Bigos)
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in a cup of warm water for half an hour and slice them, straining and keeping the water.
Squeeze the sauerkraut, shred the fresh cabbage and stew each in its own pot for thirty minutes.
Render the bacon to crackling, brown the pork and beef in its fat, then the onion.
Combine both cabbages, the meats, sausage, mushrooms with their water, prunes, tomato paste and spices in a large pot.
Add the wine, bring it up and stew two hours on the lowest heat, stirring occasionally.
Cool it completely and leave it a day in the cold, then bring it back to the boil and stew an hour.
Repeat the cycle once more on the third day. Serve with rye bread and a glass of vodka.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sernik
description: A dense curd cheesecake on a shortcrust base, made with twaróg rather than cream cheese. (Sernik)
instructions: Rub the flour with a hundred grams of cold butter, a spoon of sugar, a yolk and the baking powder to a crumb and bring it into a dough.
Press the dough into a tin and bake it at 180 °C for fifteen minutes, to a pale gold.
Pass the curd through a sieve twice; the smoothness of the filling depends entirely on it.
Beat the remaining butter with the sugar until pale, add the yolks one by one, then the curd, soured cream, starch, vanilla and zest.
Whip the whites with a pinch of salt to firm peaks and fold them in with a spatula in three additions.
Fold in the raisins, pour the filling onto the base and level it.
Bake at 160 °C for fifty-five minutes, then switch the oven off and leave the cake inside with the door ajar for an hour.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Moqueca baiana
description: Fish stewed in coconut milk with dendê palm oil, in a clay pot. (Moqueca baiana)

ingredients.text: 1 kg White fish (firm fillet, in large pieces)

instructions: Rub the fish with salt, pepper, crushed garlic and lime juice and leave it twenty minutes.
Slice the onion, tomatoes and peppers into rings of the same thickness.
Line the bottom of the clay pot with half the onion, tomato and pepper rings.
Lay the fish in a single layer, the prawns and remaining vegetables over it, and season.
Pour the coconut milk and dendê oil down the side, without dousing the fish from above.
Cover and cook twenty minutes over medium heat, rocking the pot but never stirring.
Scatter with coriander and spring onion and serve straight from the pot, with rice and farofa.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Coxinha
description: Deep-fried teardrops of cooked dough with a chicken filling, shaped like a drumstick. (Coxinha)
instructions: Poach the chicken in salted water for twenty minutes, lift it out and pull it into threads. Keep the broth.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the chicken, tomato paste, parsley and salt and cook five minutes.
Bring the broth and butter to the boil, add all the flour at once and work it on the heat for five minutes.
Turn the dough onto the table and knead it by hand until it is smooth and stops sticking.
Flatten a piece of dough on your palm, add filling and a little catupiry, seal it and draw it into a teardrop with a point.
Coat in egg and crumbs, repeat once more and chill them twenty minutes.
Fry in batches at 175 °C for four minutes, to a deep gold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ají de gallina
description: Shredded chicken in a creamy sauce of ají amarillo, nuts and bread. (Ají de gallina)
instructions: Poach the chicken breast in salted water for twenty minutes and pull it into fine threads by hand.
Soak the crustless bread in the milk for ten minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add the ají paste and turmeric and cook five minutes.
Blend the soaked bread with its milk, the walnuts and the fried onion until smooth.
Return the mixture to the pan and cook it ten minutes on a low heat, stirring.
Stir in the chicken and parmesan, season and warm it five minutes to the thickness of soured cream.
Serve over boiled potato and rice, garnished with egg and olives.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Causa limeña
description: Layers of yellow potato purée with lime and ají, filled with chicken or tuna. (Causa limeña)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until completely soft, peel them hot and press them through a ricer.
Work the purée by hand for five minutes, until it is even and elastic.
Cool the purée to room temperature, then work in the ají paste, lime juice, oil and salt.
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise, finely chopped red onion and coriander.
Press half the purée into a mould in a layer a centimetre and a half thick and level it.
Spread the filling and the avocado slices and cover with the other half of the purée.
Chill it two hours, garnish with egg and olives and serve cold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fesenjan
description: Duck or chicken in a thick sauce of ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses. (خورش فسنجان)
instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for five minutes, cool them and grind them almost to a paste.
Fry the onion until golden, add the turmeric and the meat and brown it all over.
Lift out the meat, add the walnut paste to the pot and pour in a litre of hot water.
Cook the sauce an hour on a low heat, stirring every ten minutes; it darkens and starts releasing oil.
Add the pomegranate molasses, cinnamon, sugar and saffron and return the meat to the pot.
Stew an hour more, until the sauce turns dark brown and thick and oil shows at the edges.
Taste and adjust the balance of sour and sweet, and serve with rice and pomegranate seeds.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Joojeh kabab
description: Chicken in a saffron marinade with onion juice and lemon, grilled over coals. (جوجه کباب)
instructions: Grind the saffron with a pinch of sugar and steep it in three spoons of warm water for fifteen minutes.
Grate the onions finely and squeeze the juice through muslin, discarding the pulp.
Mix the onion juice, half the saffron infusion, the juice of two lemons, the yoghurt, oil, salt and pepper.
Cut the chicken into four-centimetre pieces, coat it in the marinade and refrigerate it eight hours.
Thread the pieces onto flat skewers packed tight and get the coals to an even strong heat.
Grill eight minutes a side, turning the skewer every two minutes.
Mix the melted butter with the remaining saffron and brush the kebabs before serving. Serve with rice, tomatoes and sumac.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Caldo verde
description: A potato purée soup with finely shredded kale and slices of smoked chouriço. (Caldo verde)
instructions: Soften the onion and garlic in half the olive oil for eight minutes.
Add the diced potato, cover with a litre and a half of water and boil twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Blend the soup to a smooth purée and season it.
Fry the chouriço slices in a dry pan until they colour and drain them on paper.
Roll the kale leaves tightly and cut across them into threads.
Bring the purée to the boil, add the kale and cook it exactly three minutes.
Ladle it out, add the sausage slices and pour over raw olive oil.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sardinhas assadas
description: Whole sardines salted coarsely and grilled over coals, served on a slice of bread. (Sardinhas assadas)
instructions: Rinse the sardines without gutting them and pat them dry on the outside.
Bury the fish in coarse salt on all sides and leave it half an hour at room temperature.
Light the coals and let them ash over; an open flame burns the skin within a minute.
Char the peppers on the coals, peel them and dress them with oil, garlic and vinegar.
Shake the excess salt off the fish and lay them on a hot, oiled grate.
Grill four minutes a side, turning them exactly once.
Lay the sardines on slices of bread and serve with boiled potatoes and the pepper salad.

image.credit: Bosc d'Anjou from New York, NY, USA

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sate ayam
description: Chicken skewers over coals with a thick peanut sauce and sweet kecap manis. (Sate ayam)
instructions: Cut the chicken into two-centimetre cubes and coat them in a mix of kecap manis, garlic, coriander and turmeric.
Marinate for at least two hours, ideally overnight in the fridge.
Grind the peanuts to a coarse crumb, keeping a few whole for serving.
Fry the shallot, garlic and chilli in oil until soft, add the ground peanuts and cook three minutes.
Add a cup of water, the tamarind, palm sugar and kecap manis and cook the sauce ten minutes to thicken.
Thread the pieces tight onto soaked skewers, five or six to each.
Grill over hot coals two minutes a side, basting with kecap manis. Serve with the sauce and rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Soto ayam
description: A yellow chicken broth on turmeric and lemongrass, with noodles, egg and fried shallot. (Soto ayam)
instructions: Simmer the chicken in two litres of water for forty minutes, skimming for the first ten.
Slice half the shallots into thin rings, deep-fry them crisp and drain them on paper.
Pound the remaining shallot, garlic, turmeric, ginger and nuts into a bumbu paste.
Fry the paste in oil for five minutes with the bruised lemongrass and lime leaves.
Transfer the paste into the broth, season and simmer twenty minutes.
Lift out the chicken and shred it, soak the noodles and blanch the sprouts and cabbage.
Divide the noodles, chicken, vegetables and half an egg between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with fried shallot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Home-cured salo
description: Pork back fat dry-cured with garlic and spices, matured in the cold for a week. (Сало)

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg Pork back fat (from the back, skin on)

instructions: Rinse the fat, dry it thoroughly and cut it into slabs ten centimetres wide.
Cut deep slits every two centimetres in each slab, stopping short of the skin.
Push a slice of garlic and a peppercorn into each slit.
Crush the remaining peppercorns and coriander and mix them with the salt and crumbled bay.
Roll the slabs in the mixture on all sides, pressing it into the slits.
Pack them into an enamelled dish skin down, cover and refrigerate for a week.
Scrape off the excess salt, roll the slabs in paprika and keep them in the freezer. Slice them thin and serve with rye bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kyiv cake
description: Two meringue layers with nuts, filled with a charlotte buttercream. (Київський торт)
instructions: Leave the whites in an open bowl at room temperature for twelve hours.
Toast the nuts ten minutes, chop them coarsely and mix them with the flour and part of the sugar.
Whip the whites to a foam, adding the rest of the sugar a spoon at a time, to firm glossy peaks.
Fold in the nut mixture with a spatula in three additions and divide it between two tins.
Dry the layers at 150 °C for two hours and leave them in the switched-off oven until completely cold.
Cook a syrup of milk, yolks and sugar to thickness, cool it completely and beat it into the softened butter.
Split the cream: vanilla and brandy into the larger part, cocoa into the smaller. Assemble the cake and chill it six hours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chakhokhbili
description: Chicken stewed without water in its own juices with tomatoes and a mountain of fresh herbs. (ჩახოხბილი)
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces in a dry heavy pot without fat, to a golden crust.
Lift out the meat, add the butter and soften the onion in the rendered fat.
Skin the tomatoes, grate them and add them to the onion.
Return the chicken, season, add the khmeli suneli and the whole chilli and cover the pot.
Stew thirty minutes on a low heat, never adding water.
Chop all the herbs and the garlic coarsely, not to a paste.
Stir in the herbs and garlic, cover the pot, take it off the heat and let it stand ten minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Satsivi
description: Turkey or chicken in a cold walnut sauce with garlic and spices. The Georgian New Year table. (საცივი)
instructions: Simmer the bird in salted water for an hour, lift it out and roast it at 200 °C for twenty minutes to colour.
Strain the broth, skim the fat and soften the finely chopped onion in it.
Grind the walnuts twice and press the released oil out by hand into a separate cup.
Crush the garlic with salt and the spices and work it into the walnut mass.
Let the walnut mass down with warm broth to the thickness of pouring cream and stir it into the onion.
Warm the sauce twenty minutes on the lowest heat without letting it boil, and stir in the vinegar.
Joint the bird, cover it with the sauce and chill it at least six hours. Drizzle the walnut oil over before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sabich
description: Pita with fried aubergine, boiled egg, amba and salad. The Iraqi-Israeli street classic. (סביח)
instructions: Cook the eggs at the barest simmer for an hour, then cool them in cold water and peel them.
Slice the aubergines a centimetre thick, salt them and press them under a weight for half an hour.
Pat the slices dry and fry them in oil to a deep gold on both sides.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, water and salt to the thickness of pouring cream.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumbers small and mix them with the parsley, lemon and salt.
Warm the pitas, cut them into pockets and spread tahini inside.
Layer in the aubergine, sliced egg and salad, and spoon over the amba, tahini and zhug.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Malabi
description: A milk pudding set with cornflour and rose water, under a sweet syrup and nuts. (מלבי)
instructions: Slake the cornflour in a cup of cold milk until completely dissolved and lump-free.
Heat the rest of the milk with the cream and sugar until hot, without letting it boil.
Pour in the starch mixture in a thin stream, whisking without stopping.
Cook over medium heat for five minutes, until the mixture thickens to the body of double cream.
Take it off the heat, stir in the rose water and pour it straight into glasses.
Press film onto the surface so no skin forms and chill for four hours.
Before serving pour over the syrup and scatter with chopped pistachios, peanuts and coconut.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fattet hummus
description: Layers of fried pita, hot chickpeas and garlic yoghurt with browned butter and pine nuts. (فتة حمص)
instructions: Boil the chickpeas in unsalted water for ninety minutes, until completely soft, and keep the water.
Tear the pitas into two-finger pieces and fry them in oil to a golden crisp.
Whisk the yoghurt with the tahini, crushed garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Let the yoghurt mixture down with a couple of spoons of the chickpea water to the body of thick cream.
Fry the pine nuts in the ghee until golden and take them off the heat.
Spread the fried bread in a dish and top it with the hot chickpeas and a spoon of their liquid.
Pour over the yoghurt, spoon on the butter and nuts, dust with paprika and parsley and serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sfiha
description: Open flatbreads with minced lamb, tomato and pomegranate molasses, from Baalbek. (صفيحة)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water, knead a soft dough with the flour, oil and salt, and work it ten minutes.
Leave the dough to rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Grate the tomatoes and onion and drain them in a sieve, keeping a little of the juice.
Mix the mince with the grated vegetables, pomegranate molasses, tahini, baharat, salt and pepper.
Divide the dough into balls and roll them into ten-centimetre rounds.
Spread the topping in a thin layer, leaving half a centimetre at the rim, and scatter with pine nuts.
Bake at 220 °C for eight minutes, until the edges colour. Serve with lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pastilla
description: A layered pie of pigeon or chicken with almonds and cinnamon, dusted with icing sugar. (البسطيلة)
instructions: Braise the chicken with the onion, saffron, ginger, coriander and a little water for an hour, until tender.
Lift out the meat, shred it, and reduce the sauce with the onion to a thick paste.
Beat the eggs into the hot paste and stir over a low heat to coarse curds, then cool it.
Fry the almonds golden, cool them and grind them with half the icing sugar and a spoon of cinnamon.
Line a tin with overlapping sheets of pastry, buttering each, with a generous overhang.
Layer in the egg and onion mass, then the meat, then the almond layer, and sprinkle with orange blossom water.
Fold the edges in, cover with two more sheets, brush with butter and bake at 190 °C for forty minutes. Dust with icing sugar and cinnamon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chebakia
description: Flower-shaped biscuits deep-fried and steeped in honey with sesame. (الشباكية)
instructions: Toast a hundred and fifty grams of the sesame and the almonds in a dry pan and grind them to a coarse paste.
Mix the flour with the nut paste, aniseed, cinnamon, saffron, yeast and salt.
Add the melted butter, orange blossom water, vinegar and warm water and knead fifteen minutes to a smooth dough.
Rest the dough an hour under film.
Roll it thin, cut it into rectangles and make four lengthways slits in each.
Thread your fingers through alternate slits and twist each piece into a flower, pinching the ends.
Fry at 165 °C for four minutes to golden, drop them straight into warm honey for five minutes and scatter with sesame.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Molokhia
description: A soup of jute leaves, slippery in texture, with a garlic and coriander tempering. (ملوخية)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with the onion, cardamom and bay for forty-five minutes and strain the broth.
Chop the molokhia leaves finely with a mezzaluna or blitz them to an even green mass.
Bring the broth to the boil, add the leaves and immediately drop the heat to its lowest.
Hold the soup just below a simmer for ten minutes, stirring; it thickens and turns slippery.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and fry it in ghee with the coriander until deep gold.
Pour the tempering into the soup — it will hiss — and cover the pot immediately for a minute.
Serve with boiled rice, the chicken and lemon, each in its own dish.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kunafa
description: Fine shredded pastry with a cheese filling, baked and drenched in sugar syrup. (كنافة)
instructions: Boil a syrup of sugar, water and lemon juice for ten minutes, take it off, add the flower waters and cool it completely.
Soak salted cheese in cold water for two hours, changing it three times, and cut it into cubes.
Pull the kataifi apart into separate strands by hand and shorten them with scissors.
Pour the melted ghee over the pastry and rub it through with your hands until every strand glistens.
Press half the pastry into a greased tin, spread the cheese short of the edges and cover with the other half.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes to a deep gold underneath — check by lifting an edge with a spatula.
Turn it out onto a platter, pour the cold syrup over at once and scatter with ground pistachios.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Asado
description: Beef on a grate over wood embers, for hours, with nothing but coarse salt. (Asado)

ingredients.text: 2.5 kg Beef short ribs (cut across the bone)

instructions: Light the firewood to one side of the grate and let it burn down to embers, about forty minutes.
Mix the parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar, oil and chilli flakes; the chimichurri needs an hour to stand.
Rake a thin layer of embers under part of the grate and lay on the sausages; they go first.
Salt the ribs coarsely all over and lay them bone side down over a moderate heat.
Cook the ribs bone down for two hours, adjusting the embers so a palm can stay above the grate for seven seconds.
Turn the ribs and give them forty minutes meat side down, for a crust.
Add the flank for the last twenty minutes, rest the meat ten and serve it with the chimichurri.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Alfajores
description: Two crumbly cornflour biscuits joined with dulce de leche and rolled in coconut. (Alfajores)
instructions: Beat the softened butter with the icing sugar until pale, about four minutes.
Add the yolks one at a time, then the vanilla, zest and brandy.
Sift the cornflour with the flour, baking powder and salt and fold it in without long working.
Wrap the dough in film and refrigerate it an hour.
Roll it half a centimetre thick and cut four-centimetre rounds.
Bake at 170 °C for twelve minutes; the biscuits should stay pale, with only the underside going golden.
Cool them completely, sandwich them in pairs with dulce de leche and roll the sides in coconut.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tafelspitz
description: Beef rump boiled in a clear broth, with apple horseradish and fried potatoes. (Tafelspitz)
instructions: Boil three litres of water with the root vegetables, bay and peppercorns and lower the beef into it.
Skim, and hold it just below a simmer for two and a half hours, never letting it bubble.
Halve the onions and char the cut faces black on a dry pan; they give the broth its colour.
Add the charred onion and the marrow bones to the pot for the last hour.
Grate the apples and mix them with the horseradish; that is Apfelkren, and it is made just before serving.
Boil the potatoes, slice them and fry them in butter until browned.
Slice the meat across the grain, serve the broth separately and the meat with the horseradish, potatoes and chives.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sachertorte
description: A dense chocolate sponge with apricot jam under a mirror chocolate glaze. (Sachertorte)
instructions: Melt the sponge chocolate over a water bath and cool it to lukewarm.
Beat the butter with the icing sugar and vanilla until pale, add the yolks one by one, then the chocolate.
Whip the whites with the sugar to firm peaks and fold them in with a spatula, alternating with the sifted flour.
Bake at 170 °C for forty-five minutes, the first fifteen with the oven door propped open.
Cool it completely, split the sponge in two and spread the warmed sieved jam between the layers and over the sides.
Cook a syrup of sugar and water to 108 °C, take it off the heat and stir in the chocolate until smooth.
Cool the glaze to the body of cream, pour it onto the centre and spread it by tilting the cake. Let it set two hours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Halászlé
description: A fiery red fisherman's soup on paprika, made from river fish in a cauldron. (Halászlé)

ingredients.text: 800 g Small river fish (for the broth)

instructions: Cut the carp into steaks, salt them and chill them an hour; the salt firms the flesh.
Put the small fish, heads, backbones and all the sliced onion into the cauldron and cover with water.
Cook an hour over medium heat, until the fish and onion have completely broken down.
Press the broth through a sieve, working the flesh through, and return it to the cauldron. Discard the bones.
Take the cauldron off the fire and stir in both paprikas until the colour is even.
Return it to the fire, add the tomato, pepper and the hot chilli and bring it up.
Lower in the carp steaks and the roe and cook twelve minutes, only rocking the cauldron. Serve with white bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Dobos torte
description: Five thin sponge layers with chocolate buttercream under a caramel lid. (Dobos torta)
instructions: Whisk the eggs and sugar over a water bath until warm, then beat them eight minutes to a thick foam.
Fold in the sifted flour with a spatula in three additions, trying not to knock the air out.
Draw six circles on parchment and spread a thin layer of batter on each.
Bake the layers at 200 °C for six minutes each, to golden edges, and lift them off the parchment at once.
Whisk the eggs with the icing sugar over a water bath until thick, cool it and work in the softened butter and melted chocolate.
Melt the caramel sugar with lemon juice to amber and pour it over the flattest layer.
Cut the caramel layer into twelve wedges with a hot oiled knife, assemble the cake and set the wedges on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pork with dumplings and cabbage
description: Braised pork with bread dumplings and soured cabbage. Czechia's unofficial national dish. (Vepřo knedlo zelo)
instructions: Rub the pork with salt, pepper, caraway and garlic and leave it an hour at room temperature.
Brown the pork in lard on all sides, add the onion and pour in water to half the height of the meat.
Braise covered at 160 °C for an hour and a half, basting every twenty minutes.
Knead a dough from the flour, warm milk with yeast, the egg and salt and let it rise forty minutes.
Fold in the bread cubes, shape two logs and boil them ten minutes on each side.
Stew the sauerkraut with onion, caraway and sugar for twenty-five minutes.
Cut the dumplings with thread and the pork into slices, and serve with the cabbage under the pan juices.

title: Kulajda
description: A creamy mushroom soup with dill, potato and a poached egg, sharpened with vinegar. (Kulajda)
instructions: Boil the diced potato in a litre and a half of water with the caraway and bay for fifteen minutes.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in butter until their water has gone and add them to the pot.
Cook them together ten minutes so the mushrooms give their flavour to the broth.
Whisk the soured cream with the flour until smooth and lump-free.
Take the soup off the heat, stir in the cream mixture, return it to a low flame and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Add the vinegar, sugar, salt, pepper and most of the dill and taste for the balance of sour against creamy.
Poach the eggs in acidulated water and set one into each bowl, scattered with the remaining dill.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Toast Skagen
description: Prawns in a dill mayonnaise on fried bread, with roe on top. (Toast Skagen)
instructions: Drain the prawns in a sieve and let them sit for at least ten minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise with the crème fraîche, chopped dill, horseradish, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Chop the red onion as fine as you can and stir it into the dressing.
Fold the prawns into the dressing gently, taking care not to crush them.
Trim the crusts from the bread and fry the slices in butter until browned on both sides.
Pile the prawns onto each toast, top with a spoon of roe and a sprig of dill. Serve at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Swedish apple cake
description: An apple cake with cinnamon under a crisp butter crumble, served with vanilla sauce. (Äppelkaka)
instructions: Peel the apples, cut them into thick wedges and spread them in a buttered dish.
Scatter half the sugar and the cinnamon over the apples and toss them lightly in the dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour with the remaining sugar and salt, using your fingertips, to a coarse crumb.
Mix in the oats and scatter the crumble over the apples without pressing it down.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes, until the top is golden and juice bubbles at the edges.
Warm the milk and cream with the split vanilla pod, without letting it boil.
Whisk the yolks with the cornflour, pour in the hot milk in a thin stream and cook the sauce to thickness, stirring.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Stegt flæsk
description: Slices of pork belly fried crisp, with potatoes and a parsley sauce. (Stegt flæsk med persillesovs)
instructions: Pat the belly slices dry with paper and salt them on both sides.
Lay them in a single layer in a cold dry pan and turn the heat to medium.
Fry eight minutes a side, pouring the rendered fat off into a cup as it collects.
Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender and peel them hot.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes without letting it colour.
Pour in the milk in a thin stream, whisking until smooth, and cook the sauce five minutes.
Stir in the mountain of chopped parsley, the nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve with the pork, potatoes and beetroot.

image.credit: Original uploader was ChildofMidnight at en.wikipedia

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Risalamande
description: A cold rice pudding with whipped cream and almonds, under a hot cherry sauce. (Risalamande)
instructions: Rinse the rice, cover it with the milk, vanilla and salt and cook an hour on the lowest heat, stirring.
Cool the rice completely; stand the bowl in cold water and stir so no skin forms.
Scald the almonds, slip off the skins and chop them coarsely, keeping one whole.
Stir the chopped almonds, sugar and sherry into the cold rice.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it in with a spatula in three additions, without knocking it down.
Hide the whole almond in the mixture and chill the pudding at least three hours.
Cook the cherries with sugar for ten minutes, thicken with slaked cornflour and serve the sauce hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Erwtensoep
description: A thick split pea soup with smoked sausage, dense enough for a spoon to stand in it. (Erwtensoep)
instructions: Rinse the peas and cover them, with the ribs and belly, in two and a half litres of cold water.
Bring it up, skim and simmer an hour, until the peas start breaking down.
Add the potato, carrot, celeriac and onion and cook another hour, stirring so nothing catches.
Lift out the meat, strip it from the bones and return it to the soup in pieces.
Add the sliced leek and celery leaves and cook twenty minutes.
Cool it completely and leave it overnight in the fridge; the soup thickens.
Reheat it, add the sliced sausage for five minutes and serve with rye bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bitterballen
description: Balls of stiff meat ragout in breadcrumbs, deep-fried and served with mustard. (Bitterballen)
instructions: Simmer the beef in the stock for ninety minutes, until completely tender, and shred it fine.
Fry the onion in butter, stir in the flour and cook it three minutes without letting it colour.
Pour in the hot stock in a thin stream and cook it to a very thick paste, about ten minutes.
Stir in the meat, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper, spread it in a dish and chill it four hours.
Roll the set mixture into walnut-sized balls with damp hands.
Coat them in flour, egg and crumbs, chill them twenty minutes, then repeat the egg and crumbs.
Fry at 180 °C for three minutes, to a deep gold, and serve with mustard.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Colcannon
description: Mashed potato with cabbage and spring onion, a lake of melted butter in the centre. (Colcannon)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until completely soft, twenty-five minutes.
Warm the milk and cream with the sliced spring onion until hot and leave it to infuse ten minutes.
Shred the cabbage and cook it in half the butter for eight minutes, until soft.
Peel the potatoes hot and mash them with a masher, never a blender.
Strain the hot milk into the mash and work it smooth, then season.
Fold in the cooked cabbage and the infused spring onion from the milk.
Mound it up, make a well in the centre and put the remaining butter into it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Beef and stout stew
description: Beef braised three hours in dark stout with onion and root vegetables. (Beef and Guinness stew)
instructions: Pat the beef dry, season it and dust it with flour on all sides.
Brown the meat in batches in hot oil to a dark crust and lift it out.
Soften the onion in the same fat, add the tomato paste and cook it three minutes.
Pour in the stout, bring it up and scrape everything caught on the bottom; that is where the flavour is.
Return the meat, add the stock, thyme and bay and braise covered at 160 °C for two hours.
Add the carrot, parsnip and potato and braise forty-five minutes more.
Stir in the honey, taste for the balance against the bitterness and serve with soda bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shurpa
description: A clear mutton soup with coarsely cut vegetables and a mound of herbs in the bowl. (Shorva)
instructions: Cover the mutton with three litres of cold water and bring it slowly to the boil.
Skim for the first twenty minutes, never letting the broth bubble hard.
Add the chickpeas and simmer forty minutes.
Add the carrots halved lengthways and the onion in quarters and cook twenty minutes.
Add the potatoes whole, the tomatoes and the peppers and cook twenty-five minutes more.
Add the cumin, salt and the whole chilli and take it off the heat after five minutes.
Divide the meat and vegetables between bowls, ladle over the broth and pile chopped herbs on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chuchvara
description: Tiny mutton dumplings boiled in broth, with suzma and herbs. (Chuchvara)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, egg, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it forty minutes at room temperature.
Chop the mutton fine with a knife and mix it with the grated onion, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into three-centimetre squares.
Put a pea of filling on each square, fold it into a triangle and join two corners into a ring.
Bring the broth to the boil with the tomatoes and the whole chilli and drop the chuchvara in batches.
Cook five minutes after they surface, divide them between bowls with the broth, and add suzma and coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pasuts tolma
description: A lenten dolma of soured cabbage leaves with lentils, beans and grains. (Պասուց տոլմա)
instructions: Boil the beans, chickpeas and lentils separately until soft; each takes its own time.
Parboil the cracked wheat and the rice and drain them.
Fry the chopped onion in oil until golden and add the tomato paste and paprika.
Combine all the grains and pulses with the onion, season, and stir in the coriander.
Rinse the cabbage leaves of excess brine and pare down the thick ribs.
Roll the filling in the leaves into tight parcels, packing them in layers in a pot.
Add water to the level of the top layer, cover with a weighted plate and cook an hour on a low heat. Cool it completely.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gata
description: A layered sweet bread with khoriz, a dry filling of flour, butter and sugar. (Գաթա)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, softened butter, soured cream, yeast and salt and work it ten minutes.
Wrap the dough in film and chill it an hour.
Rub the filling flour with the cold butter, sugar and vanilla to a damp crumb.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, brush it with butter, fold it in three and chill it twenty minutes.
Repeat the rolling and folding once more, then roll it out a centimetre thick.
Spread the filling over half the sheet, fold the other half over and seal the edges.
Score a pattern with a fork, brush with yolk and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes, to a deep gold.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Nasi lemak
description: Rice cooked in coconut milk with pandan, served with sambal, anchovies, egg and peanuts. (Nasi lemak)
