instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and cover it with coconut milk let down with water, salt and pandan.
Add slices of ginger and cook covered for fifteen minutes, then let it stand ten.
Soak the dried chillies in boiling water for twenty minutes and blend them with the shallot, garlic and belacan.
Fry the paste in oil for twenty minutes over medium heat, until oil breaks out at the edges.
Add the tamarind, palm sugar and salt and cook the sambal ten minutes more to thicken it.
Fry the anchovies and peanuts separately until crisp and hard-boil the eggs.
Build the plate: a mound of rice, a spoon of sambal, anchovies, peanuts, half an egg and cucumber slices.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Char kway teow
description: Wide rice noodles seared over a very high flame with prawns, egg and bean sprouts. (Char kway teow)
instructions: Separate the fresh noodles into individual strips by hand, trying not to tear them.
Set everything out beside the hob — the cooking takes four minutes and there will be no time to fetch anything.
Heat the wok until it smokes, melt the lard and fry the garlic and sausage for twenty seconds.
Add the prawns and cockles and cook thirty seconds, without stirring constantly.
Push everything to the side, break the eggs into the centre, let them set for ten seconds and break them up.
Add the noodles, both soy sauces, the sambal and sugar and toss them for a minute and a half.
Throw in the sprouts and chives, toss for twenty seconds and serve immediately.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kare-kare
description: Oxtail in a thick peanut sauce with vegetables, served with bagoong shrimp paste. (Kare-kare)
instructions: Simmer the oxtail in water for three hours on a low heat, skimming. Keep the broth.
Toast the rice in a dry pan until brown and grind it to a fine powder.
Warm the annatto seeds in oil for three minutes and strain it; the coloured oil is where the dish gets its colour.
Fry the onion and garlic in the annatto oil, add the peanut butter and let it down with broth.
Stir in the rice powder and cook the sauce fifteen minutes, stirring, to the body of soured cream.
Return the oxtail to the sauce and warm it ten minutes so the meat takes it up.
Blanch the vegetables separately until just tender, lay them over the meat and serve with rice and bagoong.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Leche flan
description: A dense caramel custard made on yolks alone, steamed in a metal mould. (Leche flan)
instructions: Melt the sugar with the water to an amber caramel and pour it into the moulds, tilting them to coat the base.
Let the caramel set in the moulds while you make the custard.
Work the yolks with a whisk without beating them to a foam; air bubbles leave holes.
Stir in both milks, the vanilla and the zest, mixing slowly.
Strain the mixture twice through a fine sieve and lift any foam off the surface with a spoon.
Pour it into the moulds over the caramel and seal each one tightly with foil.
Steam for forty minutes at a gentle simmer, chill four hours and turn out onto a plate.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Injera
description: A sour, porous flatbread of teff on a three-day ferment, serving as both bread and plate. (እንጀራ)

ingredients.text: 100 ml Ersho starter (from a previous batch)

instructions: Mix the teff flour with water to the consistency of pouring cream, without lumps.
Cover it with a cloth and leave it at room temperature for three days, without stirring.
Pour off the liquid that has separated on top; it is bitter and must not be left in.
Take a cup of the batter, cook it in boiling water to a thick paste and stir it back in.
Let the batter stand another two hours and let it down with water to a very thin cream.
Heat a wide pan, oil it lightly and pour the batter in a spiral from the rim to the centre.
Cover for two minutes, until eyes appear all over the surface, and lift it off without turning.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kitfo
description: Hand-chopped raw beef worked with spiced niter kibbeh butter and mitmita spice. (ክትፎ)
instructions: Melt the butter over a low heat with the ginger, garlic, cardamom, cinnamon and fenugreek.
Hold it twenty minutes without boiling, until the foam settles and the butter turns clear.
Strain the niter kibbeh through muslin and keep it warm.
Trim every membrane and sinew from the beef and chop it very fine with a knife, almost to a paste.
Work the warm niter kibbeh, mitmita and salt into the meat by hand for two minutes.
Warm the mixture in a pan for thirty seconds to body temperature, without letting it whiten.
Serve it on injera with the ayib cheese and stewed greens alongside.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Egusi soup
description: A thick soup of ground egusi melon seeds with greens, meat and palm oil. (Egusi soup)
instructions: Simmer the beef with onion, stock cube and salt for forty minutes. Keep the broth.
Soak the stockfish in boiling water for twenty minutes and break it into pieces, removing bones.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water into a thick paste that holds its shape.
Heat the palm oil until clear and fry the onion and ground scotch bonnet for three minutes.
Drop the egusi paste into the oil by the spoonful without stirring and let the lumps set for five minutes.
Pour in the broth and add the meat, both fish, the crayfish and the locust beans, and cook twenty minutes.
Stir in the greens for the last five minutes and serve with fufu or eba.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Puff puff
description: Yeasted balls of loose batter, deep-fried crisp outside and airy within. (Puff puff)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Whisk in the flour, nutmeg and salt to a smooth loose batter without lumps.
Cover it and leave it somewhere warm for an hour; it should double and bubble all over.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and test with a drop of batter; it should surface within two seconds.
Take batter in your palm and squeeze a ball out between thumb and forefinger straight into the oil.
Fry three minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon, to an even golden brown.
Drain them on paper and serve warm, dusted with icing sugar.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Arroz con pollo
description: Chicken with rice cooked in beer and saffron, with peas, peppers and olives. (Arroz con pollo a la cubana)
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, cumin, oregano, garlic and lime juice and leave it half an hour.
Brown the chicken in olive oil on all sides and lift it out.
Sweat the onion, pepper and garlic in the same oil for twenty minutes, until completely soft; that is the sofrito.
Add the tomato sauce and the saffron steeped in a spoon of warm water and cook five minutes.
Return the chicken, add the beer and stock, bring it up and season.
Add the rice in an even layer, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without stirring.
Scatter the peas and olives over the top, cover and let it stand ten minutes before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tostones
description: Green plantain fried twice, flattened between the fryings, with a garlic dip. (Tostones)
instructions: Score the plantain skin lengthways and lever it off with a knife; a green one will not peel by hand.
Cut them across into three-centimetre pieces.
Crush half the garlic with salt and stir it into half a litre of warm water.
Fry the pieces at 160 °C for four minutes, until soft but not golden.
Flatten each piece with the base of a glass or a press to a centimetre thick.
Dip the discs in the garlic water for a second and pat them dry.
Fry them a second time at 190 °C for two minutes to a crisp shell, salt them and serve with a mojo of the remaining garlic, olive oil and lime.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Jamaican patties
description: Pastries of turmeric-yellow flaky dough with a spiced beef filling. (Jamaican beef patty)
instructions: Mix the flour with turmeric, curry powder and salt and rub in the cold fat in large pieces, not to a fine crumb.
Add the iced water and bring the dough together without kneading, then chill it half an hour.
Roll it out, fold it in three and repeat twice more, chilling between folds.
Fry the onion, spring onion, thyme and chopped scotch bonnet, add the mince and cook it through.
Add the stock, allspice and breadcrumbs and cook ten minutes to a juicy but not runny filling.
Cool the filling completely, roll out the dough and cut fifteen-centimetre rounds.
Put filling on half of each round, fold it over, crimp with a fork and bake at 200 °C for thirty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rice and peas
description: Rice cooked with red beans in coconut milk, with thyme and a whole scotch bonnet. (Rice and peas)
instructions: Boil the soaked beans in a litre and a half of water for an hour, until soft.
Add the coconut milk, garlic, spring onion, thyme and allspice and bring it to the boil.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, add it to the pot and level it with a spoon.
Lay the whole scotch bonnet on top, season, and check that the liquid covers the rice by a finger.
Cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat, without lifting the lid once.
Take it off the heat and let it stand covered for ten minutes.
Remove the chilli and the thyme sprigs, fluff the rice with a fork and serve.

image.credit: File:Rice and Peas.png: Whispyhistory conversion to jpg: Hike395

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ruisleipä
description: A dense sourdough rye bread, sour and with almost no wheat flour in it. (Ruisleipä)
instructions: Mix the starter with half the water and half the flour and leave it overnight at room temperature.
In the morning take two hundred grams of the sponge back into a jar; that is the starter for next time.
Stir in the remaining flour, water, salt, malt and caraway with a wooden spoon until even.
Cover it and let it rise three hours; the dough roughly doubles and cracks appear on the surface.
Turn the dough into greased tins with wet hands, smoothing the top with a wet spoon.
Let it prove an hour and prick the top in several places with a fork.
Bake at 250 °C for fifteen minutes, then at 180 °C for forty-five more, and rest it a day before cutting.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Poronkäristys
description: Shaved reindeer fried in butter and braised in beer, with mash and lingonberry. (Poronkäristys)
instructions: Take the reindeer from the freezer and shave it into thin curls with a sharp knife.
Melt the butter in a cast-iron pan and heat it until it just smokes.
Add the frozen shavings and fry them hard until all the water has gone.
Add the chopped onion and fry five minutes more, to a good colour.
Add the beer and water, season, and stew covered for half an hour.
Boil the potatoes and mash them with hot milk to a smooth purée.
Serve the meat on the mash with a spoon of lingonberry and pickled cucumbers.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kjøttkaker
description: Large meat patties in a brown sauce, with lingonberry and stewed peas. (Kjøttkaker)
instructions: Work the mince with the starch, salt, pepper, ginger and nutmeg for five minutes.
Add the iced water a spoon at a time, still working the mixture, until it turns tacky and even.
Fold in the grated onion and chill the mixture twenty minutes.
Shape flat oval patties with wet hands, about a hundred grams each.
Fry the patties in butter four minutes a side and move them to a pot.
Stir the flour into the pan with the remaining fat, cook it to a nutty brown and add the stock.
Pour the sauce over the patties and stew twenty minutes. Serve with potatoes, peas and lingonberry.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Skolebrød
description: A cardamom-scented bun with custard in the centre, icing and desiccated coconut. (Skolebrød)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with a spoon of sugar and leave it ten minutes.
Knead a dough from the flour, yeast mixture, sugar, cardamom, egg, salt and softened butter, working it fifteen minutes.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Cook a custard of milk, yolks, cornflour, sugar and vanilla and cool it completely under film.
Divide the dough into twelve balls, set them on a tray and prove them forty minutes.
Press a well into each bun with the base of a glass and spoon custard into it.
Bake at 200 °C for twelve minutes, cool them, pipe the icing in a ring and scatter the coconut.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Waterzooi
description: A Ghent stew of chicken or fish in a creamy broth with julienned root vegetables. (Gentse waterzooi)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with the onion, bay and thyme for forty minutes and strain the broth.
Cut the leek, carrot and celeriac into fine julienne of equal length.
Sweat the vegetables in butter for ten minutes, without letting them colour.
Add the broth and the potato in batons and cook fifteen minutes.
Joint the chicken, return it to the pot and take it off the heat.
Whisk the yolks with the cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring, until the bowl warms up.
Pour the mixture back into the pot off the heat, warm it through without boiling, and add lemon and parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Liège waffles
description: Dense yeasted waffles from a stiff dough with pearl sugar that caramelises on the outside. (Gaufre de Liège)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, yeast mixture, eggs, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt.
Work in the softened butter in stages, kneading until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour and a half, until doubled.
Work the pearl sugar in by hand, distributing it evenly but without long kneading.
Divide the dough into ten lumps and rest them fifteen minutes.
Bake them in the iron three minutes each, to a deep gold with a caramel crust.

image.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Jrenier assumed (based on copyright claims).

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
description: Veal strips in a creamy mushroom sauce with white wine, served with rösti. (Zürcher Geschnetzeltes)
instructions: Cut the veal into fine strips across the grain and pat them dry.
Heat a pan with butter and sear the meat in batches for thirty seconds, moving it onto a plate.
Fry the shallot and mushrooms in the same pan until their water has gone.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the wine, reducing it by half.
Add the stock and cream and reduce the sauce to a coating consistency, about eight minutes.
Return the meat with its collected juices, warm it a minute without boiling, and add lemon.
Scatter with parsley and serve with rösti set alongside rather than under the meat.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bircher muesli
description: Oats soaked overnight with grated apple, cream and nuts. (Birchermüesli)
instructions: Cover the oats with water or apple juice and leave them overnight in the fridge.
In the morning stir in the yoghurt, cream and condensed milk until even.
Grate the apples, skins and all, on a coarse grater straight into the bowl.
Squeeze lemon juice over the grated apple at once and stir it through so it does not brown.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for five minutes and chop them coarsely.
Stir in the honey, divide it between bowls and top with the nuts and berries.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Peka
description: Meat and potatoes under an iron bell buried in embers, three hours untouched. (Ispod peke)

ingredients.text: 2 kg Lamb or veal (in large pieces)

instructions: Build a fire of hardwood and let it burn down to substantial embers, about an hour.
Rub the meat with salt, pepper, garlic and rosemary and leave it half an hour.
Spread the potatoes, onion, carrot and tomatoes over the tray in one layer.
Lay the meat over the vegetables, pour on the olive oil and wine and add the bay leaves.
Cover with the bell and bury it in embers completely, until no metal shows.
Cook an hour and a half, then lift the bell, turn the potatoes and baste everything with the juices from the tray.
Replace the bell and embers and give it another hour and twenty. Serve straight from the tray.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fritule
description: Small doughnuts with raisins, citrus zest and rakija, deep-fried. (Fritule)
instructions: Soak the raisins in the rakija for twenty minutes, so they swell and give up their aroma.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with a spoon of sugar and leave it until it foams.
Beat the eggs with the remaining sugar, the zests, vanilla and salt.
Combine with the yeast mixture and the flour and whisk to a smooth loose batter.
Stir in the raisins with their rakija and let the batter rise an hour somewhere warm.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and drop the batter in with two teaspoons, shaping irregular balls.
Fry three minutes, turning them, to a deep gold, and dust them with icing sugar while hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sarma
description: Rolls of soured cabbage leaves with pork and rice, stewed with smoked meat. (Sarma)
instructions: Take the cabbage apart into leaves, rinse off the excess brine and pare down the thick ribs.
Fry the chopped onion in oil until soft and let it cool.
Mix both minces with the raw rice, the onion, a spoon of paprika, salt and pepper.
Roll the filling in the leaves into tight parcels, tucking the ends in.
Line the bottom of the pot with shredded cabbage trimmings and half the ribs.
Pack the sarma in layers with ribs and pork fat between them, and add water level with the top layer.
Stew two and a half hours on a low heat, adding a roux of flour, paprika and tomato paste at the end.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gibanica
description: A pie of crumpled filo sheets in a cheese and egg custard, baked to browned ridges. (Gibanica)
instructions: Mash both cheeses with a fork and mix them with the eggs, kefir, soured cream and half the oil.
Stir in the sparkling water; it lightens the custard and keeps it from setting dense.
Taste the custard for salt: brined cheese varies, and it has to be adjusted rather than measured.
Oil the tin and lay two whole filo sheets flat on the bottom, uncrumpled.
Dip each remaining sheet in the custard, crumple it like a concertina and lay it in the tin.
Pour the remaining custard over, cover with two whole sheets and brush them with oil.
Bake at 190 °C for fifty minutes, sprinkle it with water and cover it with a cloth for ten minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ciorbă de burtă
description: A sour tripe soup in a creamy garlic broth, thickened with egg yolks. (Ciorbă de burtă)
instructions: Rinse the tripe several times in cold water, rub it with salt and rinse it again.
Boil the tripe in water with half the vinegar for ten minutes and throw away that first water.
Cover it with fresh water along with the bones and root vegetables and simmer four hours.
Lift out the tripe, cut it into fine strips and return it to the strained broth.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and let it down with a ladle of the broth.
Whisk the yolks with the cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring without stopping.
Pour the mixture into the pot off the heat, add the garlic and the remaining vinegar, and warm it through without boiling.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Papanași
description: Curd doughnuts shaped as a ring with a ball on top, with soured cream and jam. (Papanași)
instructions: Wring the curd in muslin and push it through a sieve to remove any grain.
Mix the curd with the eggs, sugar, zest, vanilla, bicarbonate and salt.
Work in the semolina and flour a little at a time, until the dough is soft but stops sticking.
Rest the dough twenty minutes; the semolina swells and shaping becomes easier.
Shape six ten-centimetre rings and six balls the size of a walnut.
Fry at 165 °C for three minutes a side, to a golden colour.
Set a ring on a plate, spoon over the soured cream and jam, and crown it with a ball.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tarator
description: A cold yoghurt soup with cucumber, garlic, dill and walnuts. (Таратор)
instructions: Grate the cucumbers coarsely or dice them small and salt them.
Leave the cucumber ten minutes to give up its water, but do not pour that water away.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste so it does not turn up in pieces.
Grind the walnuts to a fine crumb, keeping a few larger pieces back.
Whisk the yoghurt with the cold water until even and add the garlic and walnuts.
Stir in the cucumber with its juice, the chopped dill and the sunflower oil.
Chill it an hour and serve with an ice cube in each bowl.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kavarma
description: Pork with mushrooms and peppers, stewed in a clay pot under an egg. (Каварма)
instructions: Brown the diced pork in oil on all sides.
Add the onion and peppers and fry seven minutes, until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook over a high flame until their water has gone.
Take it off the heat, stir in the paprika and savory, add the wine and return it to the heat for three minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season, and divide everything between the pots.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, covered.
Take the lids off, break an egg into each pot, scatter the cheese and give them eight minutes more.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Hoppers
description: Thin bowl-shaped pancakes from fermented rice batter with coconut milk, often with an egg. (Appa)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Mix the rice flour with the yeast mixture and half the coconut milk to a smooth batter.
Cover it and leave it to ferment overnight at room temperature, about eight hours.
In the morning stir in the remaining coconut milk and salt; the batter should be as thin as pouring cream.
Mix the finely chopped onion, chilli flakes, Maldive fish, lime juice and salt; that is lunu miris.
Heat a small wok, oil it and pour in a ladle of batter, swirling the pan immediately.
Break an egg into the centre, cover and cook three minutes to crisp edges. Serve with the lunu miris.

image.credit: Paul Joseph from vancouver, bc, canada

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sri Lankan fish curry
description: Fish in a coconut curry soured with goraka and built on roasted curry powder. (Malu kariya)
instructions: Soak the goraka in a cup of warm water for twenty minutes and keep the water.
Rub the fish with salt, turmeric and half the curry powder and leave it fifteen minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, pandan, cinnamon and fenugreek until fragrant.
Add the remaining curry powder and chilli and warm them a minute without letting them scorch.
Add the thinned coconut milk with the goraka water and bring it to the boil.
Lay the fish steaks in a single layer, add the goraka and cook twelve minutes, rocking the pan.
Add the thick coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling. Serve with red rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sel roti
description: A ring of fermented rice batter deep-fried crisp outside and soft within. (सेल रोटी)
instructions: Soak the rice in cold water overnight, drain it and pat it dry with a cloth.
Grind the wet rice in a blender with the milk to a smooth thick paste without grit.
Work in the sugar, melted ghee, mashed banana, cardamom, cloves and salt.
Beat the batter by hand for twenty minutes in circular movements, working air into it.
Let the batter stand an hour; it ferments slightly and turns bubbly.
Heat the oil to 165 °C and pour the batter into it in a ring, in one continuous movement.
Fry two minutes a side, turning with two chopsticks, to a golden colour.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gundruk soup
description: A sour soup of fermented dried greens with potato, soybeans and chilli. (Gundruk ko jhol)
instructions: Soak the gundruk in warm water for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the water.
Toast the soybeans in a dry pan until they darken in patches and crack.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, take it off and let it cool a minute; raw mustard oil is acrid.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and turmeric, add the tomatoes and cook five minutes.
Add the gundruk, soybeans and potato, and pour in the soaking water and a litre of water.
Cook twenty-five minutes, until the potato and beans are soft, and season.
Sizzle the dried chillies, fenugreek and timur in a spoon of oil and pour it into the soup.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Haleem
description: Meat, wheat and pulses cooked down and beaten into one smooth thick mass over six hours. (حلیم)
instructions: Soak the wheat overnight and the chana dal and barley for four hours, then rinse them.
Fry three onions in ghee until deep brown and set half aside for serving.
Brown the meat with the remaining onion, the ginger garlic paste and all the spices.
Cover with water and braise three hours, until the meat starts falling into threads.
Boil the wheat, barley and both dals in a separate pot for three hours, until completely broken down.
Remove the bones, combine the two and beat with a wooden masher for forty minutes, until uniform.
Serve with the fried onion, ginger, chilli, coriander and lemon scattered on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Seekh kebab
description: Spiced mince moulded onto a skewer and grilled over coals. (سیخ کباب)

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Green papaya paste (as a tenderiser)

instructions: Grate the onions finely and wring them dry in muslin, discarding the juice.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan until it smells nutty and let it cool.
Mix the mince with the onion, ginger garlic paste, papaya, spices, coriander and chillies.
Work the mixture ten minutes, until it turns tacky and pulls back at your hand.
Fold in the chickpea flour and chill the mixture for at least an hour.
With wet hands mould the mince onto flat skewers in an even two-centimetre layer.
Grill over hot coals four minutes a side, basting with oil. Serve with naan.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kenyan chapati
description: A soft layered flatbread of wheat dough coiled into a spiral before rolling. (Chapati)
instructions: Mix the flour with the salt and sugar, add the warm water and two spoons of oil.
Knead the dough fifteen minutes, until it is smooth and elastic.
Cover it with a damp cloth and rest it an hour at room temperature.
Divide it into eight balls, roll each into a thin round and brush it generously with oil.
Roll the round into a rope, coil it like a snail and press it flat with your palm.
Rest the coils fifteen minutes and roll each one out into a round again.
Cook them in a dry pan a minute and a half a side, brushing with oil, to browned spots.

image.credit: KittyKaht from Hong Kong, Hong Kong

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mandazi
description: Triangular doughnuts on coconut milk with cardamom, lightly sweet, for tea. (Mandazi)
instructions: Warm the coconut milk and dissolve the yeast in it with a spoon of sugar.
Mix the flour with the remaining sugar, the cardamom and the salt.
Work in the egg, melted butter and the coconut yeast mixture and knead a soft dough.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Divide the dough into four, rolling each piece into a round a centimetre thick.
Cut each round into four triangles and let them rest fifteen minutes.
Fry at 170 °C for two minutes a side, to a golden colour.

image.credit: The original uploader was ChildofMidnight at English Wikipedia.

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bunny chow
description: Half a white loaf hollowed out and filled with lamb curry. (Bunny chow)

ingredients.text: 900 g Lamb (on the bone, in pieces)

instructions: Fry the onion in oil until deep gold and add the cinnamon, cardamom and curry leaves.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste and the curry powder and cook them two minutes.
Add the lamb and brown it, turning it through the spices.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season and stew covered for an hour on a low heat.
Add the potato in large pieces and stew twenty-five minutes more.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until a spoon leaves a trail in it.
Halve the loaves, pull out the crumb, fill them with the curry and set the crumb on top.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Melktert
description: A milk tart with cinnamon: a barely-egged custard filling in a shortcrust base. (Melktert)
instructions: Rub the flour with the cold butter, a spoon of sugar and an egg into a dough and chill it half an hour.
Line a tin with the pastry and blind-bake it at 180 °C for fifteen minutes, to a pale gold.
Heat the milk with the cinnamon stick until hot and leave it to infuse ten minutes.
Whisk the remaining eggs with the sugar, flour, cornflour, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Pour in the hot milk in a thin stream, whisking constantly, and return it to the heat.
Cook over medium heat for eight minutes, until the filling thickens to the body of double cream.
Pour the filling into the base, chill it three hours and dust it with ground cinnamon before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bandeja paisa
description: A tray of beans, rice, meat, crackling, egg, arepa, avocado and fried plantain. (Bandeja paisa)
instructions: Boil the beans with the chopped green plantain for an hour and a half, until soft and thick.
Simmer the pork belly in salted water for forty minutes and dry it thoroughly.
Fry the belly skin down in deep oil until the skin blisters and crisps.
Make the hogao: fry the onion with the tomato and cumin, add the mince and cook it through.
Fry the chorizo, cook the rice and fry slices of ripe plantain to a caramel colour.
Cook the arepas on a dry pan and fry the eggs with runny yolks.
Build the tray: beans, rice, mince, chicharrón, chorizo, egg, arepa, plantain and avocado side by side.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Colombian sancocho
description: A chicken soup with cassava, plantain and corn, cooked over an open fire. (Sancocho de gallina)
instructions: Fry the finely chopped onion, spring onion, tomato and garlic with the cumin and achiote down to a paste.
Put the chicken in the pot, add half the hogao and cover with four litres of water.
Bring it up, skim and simmer forty minutes.
Add the corn in halved cobs and the cassava in large pieces and cook twenty minutes.
Add the plantain and potato and cook twenty-five minutes more.
Mash a couple of pieces of cassava in the pot to thicken the soup and stir in the remaining hogao.
Scatter with coriander and serve with white rice and avocado on separate plates.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Curanto en olla
description: Shellfish, meat and potato cakes cooked in layers in one pot without water. (Pulmay)
instructions: Scrub the shellfish through several changes of water and discard any that are already open.
Boil half the potatoes, mash them and work them with the flour and lard into firm chapalele cakes.
Line the bottom of the pot with two layers of cabbage leaves.
Lay the shellfish in as the first layer, add the wine and cover with more cabbage leaves.
Arrange the ribs, chicken, sausage and onion as the second layer and cover with leaves again.
Put the whole potatoes and the cakes on top, cover with leaves and close the lid tightly.
Cook over medium heat for an hour without opening it. Serve in layers, with the broth from the bottom in separate bowls.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Completo
description: A hot dog under mounds of mashed avocado, tomato and mayonnaise, coloured like the Italian flag. (Completo italiano)
instructions: Mash the avocados with a fork, salt and lemon juice into a coarse purée, not smooth.
Dice the tomatoes small, salt them and drain them in a sieve to lose the excess water.
Poach the frankfurters in water on a low heat for five minutes, without letting them split.
Warm the buns in steam or in the oven for two minutes; they should be soft and hot.
Put a frankfurter in each bun and spread the drained tomato over it in an even layer.
Pile the avocado over the tomato, covering it completely.
Finish with a generous stripe of mayonnaise and serve the ají sauce separately.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kuyrdak
description: Offal and meat fried in a cauldron with onion and potato on rendered tail fat. (Қуырдақ)
instructions: Soak the kidneys in cold water for an hour, changing it twice, and trim out every duct.
Render the tail fat in the cauldron to cracklings and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Sear the mutton hard to a dark crust, five minutes.
Add the heart and fry eight minutes more, stirring.
Add the kidneys, then the liver three minutes later, and fry three more; the liver must not overcook.
Add the diced onion and potato, season, add the cumin and cook covered for fifteen minutes.
Stir in the garlic and herbs, take it off the heat and serve straight from the cauldron with flatbread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shelpek
description: Thin flatbreads fried in oil, the memorial bread of Kazakh tradition. (Шелпек)
instructions: Mix the kefir with the bicarbonate and leave it five minutes; the mixture foams.
Add the egg, sugar, salt and melted butter and stir until even.
Work in the flour a little at a time and knead a soft dough that stays slightly tacky.
Cover it with a cloth and rest it half an hour at room temperature.
Divide it into seven balls and roll each into a thin twenty-centimetre round.
Prick each round in several places with a fork so it does not balloon in one bubble.
Fry them in hot oil a minute a side, to golden spots, and drain them on paper.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Azerbaijani dolma
description: Vine leaves with lamb, rice and mint, cooked under a weight, with garlic matsoni. (Yarpaq dolması)
instructions: Scald fresh leaves for a minute; soak preserved ones half an hour in cold water.
Rinse the rice and mix it with the mince, finely chopped onion, salt, pepper and cinnamon.
Chop all the herbs fine and work them into the filling; their volume should be obvious.
Put a teaspoon of filling on each leaf, tuck in the sides and roll it into a tight cylinder a finger thick.
Line the bottom of the pot with torn leaves and pack the dolma in tight layers, seam down.
Dot the top with ghee, add water level with the top layer and cover with a weighted plate.
Cook an hour on a low heat and serve with matsoni whisked with crushed garlic and salt.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Baku pakhlava
description: Diamonds of eight layers of dough with a nut filling, under a saffron syrup. (Bakı paxlavası)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk and knead a dough with the flour, yolks, a spoon of ghee and salt.
Let the dough rise an hour somewhere warm and divide it into eight equal balls.
Mix the ground walnuts with half the sugar and the cardamom; that is the filling.
Roll the first ball to the size of the tin, lay it in and brush it generously with ghee.
Alternate layers of dough and nut filling, buttering each, until the dough runs out.
Cut it into diamonds right down to the base, press a walnut half into each and brush with saffron infusion.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes and pour over a hot syrup of honey and the remaining sugar.

image.credit: James Gordon from Los Angeles, California, USA

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Iraqi biryani
description: Rice with chicken, vermicelli, nuts and raisins, every component cooked separately. (برياني عراقي)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with onion, pierced black lime and baharat for forty minutes. Keep the broth.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Fry the vermicelli in ghee to a deep brown, stirring.
Fry the potato, carrot, almonds and raisins separately and drain them on paper.
Joint the chicken and fry the pieces with the tomato paste until browned.
Cook the rice with the fried vermicelli in the strained broth for twenty minutes, covered.
Mound the rice on a platter and lay the chicken and all the fried components on top, unmixed.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kleicha
description: Biscuits of date paste and cardamom, rolled into a log and cut into slices. (كليجة)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Rub the flour with the melted ghee, mahlab, fennel, nigella and salt.
Add the yeast mixture and knead a soft dough, working it ten minutes.
Cover it and rest it an hour at room temperature.
Work the date paste with a spoon of ghee and the cardamom until pliable.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread the paste in a thin layer and roll it into a tight log.
Cut the log into centimetre slices, brush them with yolk, scatter with sesame and bake at 180 °C for twenty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tunisian chakchouka
description: Stewed peppers with tomato and harissa, eggs broken into the sauce at the end. (Chakchouka)
instructions: Char the peppers over a flame until the skin blackens, cover them with a bowl for ten minutes and peel them.
Cut the peeled peppers into strips, the tomatoes into dice and the onion into slices.
Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil until soft, eight minutes.
Stir in the harissa, tomato paste, caraway and coriander and cook them two minutes.
Add the peppers and tomatoes, season and stew twenty minutes to a thick paste.
Make wells in the sauce with a spoon and break an egg into each.
Cover and cook six minutes, until the whites set and the yolks stay liquid.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ojja with merguez
description: A fiery tomato stew with merguez lamb sausages and eggs stirred into the sauce. (Ojja bel merguez)
instructions: Fry the merguez in olive oil until browned all over and lift them onto a plate.
In the same fat fry the sliced pepper and the garlic until soft.
Stir in the harissa, tomato paste and caraway and cook them two minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season and cook fifteen minutes to thicken.
Return the sausages, cut into pieces, and warm them three minutes.
Drop the heat to its lowest, break in the eggs and stir with a spatula for three minutes into a creamy mass.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with baguette.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Muhammara
description: A paste of roasted red pepper, walnuts and pomegranate molasses, from Aleppo. (محمرة)
instructions: Char the peppers over a flame or under the grill until the skin blackens all over.
Put them in a bowl, cover it with film for fifteen minutes and remove the skin and seeds.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for five minutes, until they smell nutty.
Pound the walnuts in a mortar or pulse them briefly to a coarse crumb.
Blitz the peppers with the garlic, pomegranate molasses, lemon, cumin and Aleppo pepper.
Fold in the walnuts and breadcrumbs by hand and season, keeping the mass grainy.
Pour in the olive oil in a thin stream, stirring, and chill it an hour before serving.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shish barak
description: Small lamb dumplings baked and then cooked in a garlic and mint yoghurt sauce. (شيش برك)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it forty minutes.
Fry the onion with the mince, baharat, salt and pepper, add the pine nuts and let it cool.
Roll the dough thin and cut four-centimetre rounds.
Shape half-moons around the filling and join the ends into a ring, like tortellini.
Bake the dumplings at 200 °C for twelve minutes, until golden.
Whisk the yoghurt with the starch, egg and salt and bring it to the boil, stirring without stopping in one direction.
Lower the dumplings into the sauce, cook ten minutes and pour over ghee with garlic and mint.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Anzac biscuits
description: Oat biscuits on golden syrup and bicarbonate, without eggs, keeping for weeks. (Anzac biscuits)
instructions: Mix the oats, flour, coconut, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Melt the butter with the golden syrup over a low heat, without letting it boil.
Dissolve the bicarbonate in the boiling water and pour it straight into the butter mixture; it foams up.
Pour the foaming mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until even.
Roll walnut-sized balls and set them on a tray with generous gaps between them.
Flatten each ball with your palm to a centimetre thick; they spread further in the oven.
Bake at 160 °C for twelve to eighteen minutes and cool them on the tray rather than a rack.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Grilled barramundi
description: A whole fish on the grate with lemon myrtle and lime, part in foil and part over direct heat. (Barramundi on the barbie)

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg Barramundi or sea bass (whole, gutted)

instructions: Cut three slashes on each side of the fish and pat it completely dry.
Work the garlic with the butter, lemon myrtle, lime zest, salt and pepper.
Rub the mixture into the slashes and the cavity and tuck slices of lime and fennel inside.
Wrap the fish in foil with the seams on top so the juices do not run out.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat under the fish has to be indirect.
Cook it in the foil for twenty minutes, turning the parcel once halfway.
Unwrap it, move the fish onto an oiled grate over the coals and give it a minute a side for the crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Afghan biscuits
description: Dense chocolate biscuits with cornflakes, under icing and half a walnut. (Afghan biscuits)
instructions: Beat the softened butter with the sugar until pale, about four minutes.
Sift the flour with the cocoa and salt and fold it in with a spatula to an even dough.
Add the cornflakes and fold them through in one movement, trying not to break them.
Drop the dough onto a tray by the spoonful and press each one down lightly.
Bake at 180 °C for eighteen minutes; the biscuits stay soft to the touch and firm up as they cool.
Cool them completely on the tray, without trying to lift them hot.
Whisk the icing sugar with the cocoa and hot water into a thick icing, coat the biscuits and press a walnut half into each.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Whitebait fritters
description: Whitebait bound with egg and fried as a thin cake, with lemon and nothing else. (Whitebait fritters)
instructions: Rinse the whitebait in cold water and drain it in a sieve for ten minutes.
Pat the whitebait dry with a cloth; excess water stops the fritter setting.
Whisk the eggs with the flour, salt and pepper until smooth and lump-free.
Fold the whitebait into the egg mixture gently, taking care not to crush it.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat until it just sizzles.
Pour in a ladle of the mixture and spread it into a thin round a centimetre thick.
Fry a minute and a half a side and serve with lemon and buttered bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Butter tarts
description: Shortcrust tartlets with a butter, sugar and syrup filling, runny or set. (Butter tarts)
instructions: Rub the flour into the cold butter to a coarse crumb and bring the dough together with iced water.
Wrap it in film and chill it half an hour, without long kneading.
Roll the pastry and line muffin tins with it, taking the sides right to the top.
Melt the butter and stir in the sugar, maple syrup, vinegar, vanilla and salt.
Cool the mixture to lukewarm and only then whisk in the eggs; in a hot one they scramble.
Divide the raisins between the cases and fill them two-thirds with the mixture, no higher.
Bake at 200 °C for eighteen minutes for a runny filling, or twenty-two for a set one.

image.credit: Rob Campbell from Toronto, ON, Canada

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Montreal bagels
description: Bagels boiled in honey water and baked in a wood oven, sweeter and thinner than New York's. (Montreal bagels)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, yeast mixture, eggs, oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes until elastic.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour and twenty, until doubled.
Divide it into twelve, roll each into a rope and join the ends into a ring with a large hole.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the honey and lower the rings in three or four at a time.
Boil them a minute a side and roll them in sesame or poppy seed at once.
Bake at 230 °C for twenty minutes, to a deep golden crust, turning them once halfway.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Skyr with berries
description: Home-made skyr, the Icelandic cultured dairy, strained thick, with bilberries. (Skyr)

ingredients.text: 100 g Skyr or yoghurt as starter

instructions: Heat the milk to 85 °C, stirring, and hold it ten minutes without letting it boil.
Cool the milk to 40 °C by standing the pot in cold water.
Slacken the starter with a ladle of the warm milk and stir it back into the pot.
Add the rennet, stir for a few seconds and cover the pot.
Leave it somewhere warm for twelve hours, until the mass sets into a firm curd.
Turn the curd into a cloth and hang it over a bowl for six hours to drain the whey.
Whisk the skyr smooth and serve it with bilberries, cream and oats.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Icelandic rye bread
description: A sweet dark rye bread baked in a sealed tin for twelve hours at a low temperature. (Rúgbrauð)
instructions: Mix both flours with the sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt in a large bowl.
Warm the milk with the syrup until the syrup dissolves.
Pour the liquid into the dry ingredients and stir with a spoon to an even thick batter.
Grease a tin, pour in the batter and fill it two-thirds full.
Seal the tin with two layers of foil and tie it with string so no steam escapes.
Stand the tin in a deep tray of water and bake at 100 °C for twelve hours.
Cool it completely in the tin and rest it a day before cutting. Serve with butter.

image.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Sten assumed (based on copyright claims).

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Katong laksa
description: Rice noodles in a coconut broth with prawns, cut short and eaten with a spoon only. (Katong laksa)
instructions: Peel the prawns, fry the shells and simmer them in a litre of water for twenty minutes, then strain.
Soak the dried chillies and dried shrimp in boiling water for twenty minutes.
Blend the chillies, shallot, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, candlenuts and belacan into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil for twenty minutes over medium heat, until the oil breaks out at the edges.
Add the prawn broth and the laksa leaf and cook fifteen minutes.
Add the coconut milk, season and warm it five minutes without letting it boil.
Cut the cooked noodles into short lengths, divide them between bowls with the prawns and sprouts and ladle over the broth.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kaya toast
description: Toasted bread with kaya coconut egg jam and cold butter, with soft-boiled eggs. (Kaya toast)
instructions: Knot the pandan leaves and warm them with the coconut milk until hot, without boiling.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until it dissolves and strain the mixture through a fine sieve.
Pour the warm coconut milk into the eggs in a thin stream, stirring without stopping.
Cook the mixture over a water bath for forty minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon, to the thickness of jam.
Remove the pandan leaves and cool the kaya completely; it thickens further.
Boil the eggs exactly six minutes and serve them in a bowl with soy sauce and white pepper.
Toast the bread crisp, spread it with kaya and lay a cold slice of butter between two pieces.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gua bao
description: A steamed folded bun with braised pork belly, pickled greens and peanut sugar. (刈包)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes.
Knead a dough from the flour, yeast mixture, remaining sugar, oil and salt, working it fifteen minutes.
Blanch the belly two minutes, rinse it and braise it in the soy, wine, sugar and star anise for ninety minutes.
Let the dough rise an hour, roll it into ovals and fold each in half with a strip of parchment inside.
Prove the buns thirty minutes and steam them for twelve.
Pound the peanuts with two spoons of sugar into a coarse crumb.
Open a bun and lay in a slice of belly, the pickled greens, the peanut crumb and coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pineapple cake
description: Squares of shortcrust with a dense filling of reduced pineapple and winter melon. (鳳梨酥)
instructions: Grate the pineapple and winter melon coarsely and press out the juice through muslin.
Reduce the pressed juice separately by half; it goes back into the filling as a concentrate.
Cook the pulp with the sugar and maltose on a low heat for an hour, stirring every five minutes.
Add the reduced juice and cook the filling until a spatula leaves a trail on the pan.
Beat the butter with the icing sugar, yolks, milk powder, cheese and salt, and work in the flour and cornflour.
Chill the dough half an hour, divide it into balls and flatten each in your palm.
Wrap a ball of filling in the dough, press it into a square mould and bake at 170 °C for twenty-five minutes, turning it halfway.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Shan noodles
description: Rice noodles with a tomato and chicken sauce, pickled greens and ground peanuts. (ရှမ်းခေါက်ဆွဲ)
instructions: Fry the sliced shallot in oil until deep gold and set half aside for serving.
Add the garlic, paprika and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the minced chicken and fry it, breaking up lumps, until it whitens.
Add the chopped tomatoes and fish sauce and stew twenty-five minutes to a thick paste.
Grind the peanuts to a coarse crumb, keeping a few whole.
Boil the rice noodles, rinse them and divide them between bowls.
Spoon the sauce over the noodles and top with peanuts, fried shallot, pickled greens and coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ohn no khao swe
description: Wheat noodles in a thick coconut broth with chicken and chickpea flour. (အုန်းနို့ခေါက်ဆွဲ)
instructions: Pound the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry it in oil with the turmeric and paprika.
Add the chicken in small pieces and fry it until it whitens all over.
Add a litre of water and the fish sauce and simmer twenty minutes.
Slake the chickpea flour in a cup of cold water until completely smooth and lump-free.
Pour the slaked flour into the broth in a thin stream, whisking without stopping.
Cook ten minutes to thicken, add the coconut milk and warm it five minutes without boiling.
Boil the noodles, divide them between bowls, ladle over the broth and serve with egg, lime and chilli.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Num banh chok
description: Cold rice noodles under a fish and coconut curry with a mountain of raw vegetables and herbs. (នំបញ្ចុក)
instructions: Poach the fish in salted water for ten minutes, lift it out and pick it by hand, removing every bone.
Pound the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric and lime leaves in a mortar into a kroeung paste.
Work the picked fish into the paste in the mortar, keeping the threads distinguishable.
Warm the fish and spice mixture in a pan for five minutes, then add the prahok and the fish broth.
Add the coconut milk and warm it ten minutes without letting it boil.
Shred all the vegetables fine and pile them on a large platter.
Boil the noodles, rinse them in cold water and serve them cold under the warm curry.

image.credit: Thomas Wanhoff from Siem Reap, Cambodia

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Samlor korko
description: A thick vegetable soup with toasted ground rice, pork and prahok, from a dozen vegetables. (សម្លកកូរ)
instructions: Toast the rice in a dry pan to a deep gold and grind it to a fine powder.
Pound the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric and garlic into a kroeung paste.
Fry the paste in oil for five minutes, add the prahok and cook two minutes more.
Add the pork and brown it, then pour in a litre and a half of water.
Cook twenty minutes, then add the pumpkin, papaya and aubergine.
Add the rice powder, first stirred into a ladle of the broth, and cook ten minutes.
Add the beans and moringa leaves for the last five minutes and adjust with fish sauce and palm sugar.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Torta frita
description: Flat rounds made on rendered fat and deep-fried, which Uruguayans make when it rains. (Torta frita)
instructions: Mix the flour with the salt and baking powder in a large bowl.
Melt the lard and stir it into the hot water until even.
Pour the liquid into the flour and work it with a spoon until it cools enough to handle.
Knead by hand for ten minutes to a smooth elastic dough.
Cover it and rest it twenty minutes at room temperature.
Divide it into eight, roll each into a half-centimetre round and cut a slit in the centre.
Fry at 180 °C for a minute and a half a side and serve with sugar or dulce de leche.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Buseca
description: A thick tripe soup with white beans, chorizo and vegetables, Uruguayan winter food. (Buseca)
instructions: Rinse the tripe several times, rub it with salt and rinse it again until completely clean.
Boil the tripe in water with half the vinegar for ten minutes and throw away that first water.
Cover it with fresh water and the bay and simmer three hours, until completely tender.
Boil the beans separately until soft, an hour and a quarter, and set them aside with their liquid.
Fry the pancetta and the sliced chorizo, add the onion, carrot and celery and sweat them ten minutes.
Stir in the paprika and tomatoes, add the sliced tripe with some of its broth and the potato.
Cook twenty-five minutes, stir in the beans with their liquid, season and warm it ten more.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kak'ik
description: A red turkey soup with charred chillies and spices, a dish of the Q'eqchi' Maya. (Kak'ik)

ingredients.text: 2 kg Turkey (in pieces, on the bone)

instructions: Simmer the turkey with an onion in three litres of water for ninety minutes, skimming.
Seed the chillies and char them on a dry pan for ten seconds a side.
Char the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion and garlic on the same pan until blackened in patches.
Toast the coriander, achiote and mace on a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend everything with two ladles of the broth to a smooth red mass.
Strain the mass through a sieve into the pot with the turkey and cook twenty-five minutes.
Add the samat and mint for the last five minutes and serve with corn tamalitos.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rellenitos
description: Balls of ripe plantain purée filled with sweetened black beans and chocolate. (Rellenitos de plátano)
instructions: Boil the plantains in their skins for twenty minutes, until completely soft.
Peel them hot and mash them into a smooth purée with a pinch of salt and the flour.
Chill the purée for half an hour; warm, it will not hold as balls.
Mash the cooked beans and reduce them with the sugar, cinnamon and cloves to a thick paste.
Stir the chocolate into the hot bean paste and cool it completely.
Flatten a piece of purée on your palm, add the bean filling and seal it into a firm ball.
Fry at 170 °C for three minutes, to a browned crust, and serve with icing sugar and soured cream.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pollo guisado
description: Chicken braised in caramelised sugar with vegetables, the Dominican weekday lunch. (Pollo guisado dominicano)
instructions: Wash the chicken with lime juice, rub it with oregano, garlic, salt and pepper and leave it an hour.
Melt the sugar in the oil over medium heat to a dark amber, without stirring with a spoon.
Put the chicken pieces into the caramel and brown them on all sides.
Add the onion, pepper and tomato paste and cook five minutes, stirring.
Add a cup of water, cover and stew twenty-five minutes on a low heat.
Add the potato in large pieces and stew twenty minutes more, until tender.
Stir in the olives and coriander, reduce the sauce to a coating consistency and serve with white rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sweet cream of beans
description: A sweet dessert cream of red beans with coconut milk, sweet potato and biscuits. (Habichuelas con dulce)
instructions: Boil the soaked beans in fresh water for an hour, until completely soft.
Blend the beans with some of their liquid to a smooth mass.
Press the mass through a sieve with a spoon and discard the skins left behind.
Return it to the heat and add the coconut and evaporated milk, cinnamon, cloves and sugar.
Cook twenty minutes on a low heat, stirring so it does not catch.
Add the sweet potato in pieces and the raisins and cook twenty minutes more, until the potato is tender.
Stir in the vanilla, butter and a pinch of salt, chill it and serve it cold with biscuits.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Trinidad roti
description: A layered flatbread beaten into rags on the pan, served with chicken or goat curry. (Buss up shut)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Chicken for the curry (in pieces)

instructions: Knead a soft dough from the flour, baking powder, salt and warm water, working it ten minutes.
Cover it and rest it an hour; the dough should become pliable and stop springing back.
Marinate the chicken with the curry powder, garlic, thyme and salt and stew it with the potato for forty minutes.
Divide the dough into six balls, roll each one thin and brush it with oil.
Roll the round into a rope, coil it into a spiral and let it rest twenty minutes.
Roll the spirals out into rounds again and cook them on a dry pan a minute and a half a side, brushing with ghee.
Move the bread onto a board and beat it into soft rags with two spatulas. Serve with the curry.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pelau
description: Rice with chicken, pigeon peas and coconut milk, browned in burnt sugar. (Pelau)
instructions: Marinate the chicken in the green seasoning, ketchup, salt and pepper for at least an hour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and add the sugar, without stirring it with a spoon.
Wait until the sugar darkens almost to black and starts to smoke, and put the chicken in at once.
Fry the chicken, turning it in the caramel, until every piece is dark brown.
Add the onion, carrot, pumpkin and pigeon peas and warm them five minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, pour in the coconut milk and water to a finger above and drop in the whole chilli.
Cover and cook twenty-five minutes on a low heat without opening it. Serve with coleslaw.

image.credit: Arnold Gatilao from Oakland, CA, USA

author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Hallaca
description: Corn dough with a meat guiso, olives and raisins, wrapped in banana leaf. (Hallaca)
instructions: Warm the annatto seeds in the lard for five minutes and strain it; the coloured fat goes into both dough and guiso.
Fry the onion and pepper in the annatto fat, add all three meats and brown them.
Add the wine and stock and stew an hour, until the meat is tender and the sauce thick.
Cool the guiso completely, ideally leaving it overnight in the fridge.
Knead a dough from the masarepa, warm stock, annatto fat and salt until pliable.
Warm the banana leaves, spread a disc of dough on each and add guiso, olives, raisins and capers.
Wrap in two leaves, tie them crosswise with string and boil them for an hour and twenty.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Asado negro
description: Beef seared black in burnt sugar and braised for four hours. (Asado negro)
instructions: Pierce the meat in several places with a knife, rub it with salt, pepper and garlic and leave it an hour.
Melt the panela in oil in a heavy pot until nearly black, without stirring it with a spoon.
Lower the beef into the caramel and sear it on all sides to a black crust, about fifteen minutes.
Lift out the meat and fry the onion, pepper, carrot and leek in the same fat until soft.
Return the meat, add the tomatoes, wine, Worcestershire sauce and bay, and add water to half its height.
Braise covered for four hours on the lowest heat, turning the joint every hour.
Lift out the meat, strain the sauce, reduce it by half and slice the beef across the grain.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pique macho
description: A mountain of chips with beef, sausage, egg and fiery locoto chillies. (Pique macho)
instructions: Cut the potatoes into thick batons and soak them in cold water for twenty minutes.
Dry the potatoes and fry them twice: at 150 °C until soft, then at 190 °C until crisp.
Sear the diced beef over a high flame in batches for two minutes each and set it aside.
Fry the sliced sausages until browned and add the onion and pepper for five minutes.
Return the meat to the pan, add the tomatoes and mustard and warm it three minutes.
Fry the eggs with runny yolks and cut the locoto into thin rings.
Pile the chips on a platter, top with the meat and vegetables, the eggs and the locoto rings, and drizzle with mayonnaise and ketchup.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Api morado
description: A hot thick purple corn drink with cinnamon and cloves, with fried pastries. (Api morado)

ingredients.text: 200 g Cheese for the pastel (to serve)

instructions: Soak the purple corn in cold water overnight, keeping that water in the morning.
Grind the corn with its water in a blender to an even purple liquid.
Strain it through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp, and strain it a second time.
Add the remaining water, the cinnamon, cloves and orange peel.
Cook over medium heat for forty minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon, until it thickens.
Add the sugar and lemon juice and cook five minutes more.
Remove the spices and serve it hot in mugs, with a fried cheese pastry.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ecuadorian ceviche
description: Prawns in a tomato and lime broth, served cold with popcorn and plantain crisps. (Ceviche de camarón)
instructions: Peel the prawns, boil the shells in a litre of water for twenty minutes and strain the broth.
Poach the prawns in that broth for exactly two minutes and drop them straight into iced water.
Chill the broth completely; it becomes the base of the dressing.
Slice the red onion thin, rinse it in cold water and cure it in lime juice with salt.
Blend two tomatoes to a purée and mix it with the ketchup, mustard, orange juice and the cold broth.
Combine the prawns, cured onion, chopped tomatoes and the dressing.
Chill it an hour, stir in the coriander and serve with popcorn and plantain crisps.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fanesca
description: The Holy Week soup of twelve grains and pulses with salt cod. (Fanesca)

ingredients.text: 700 g Salt cod (soaked for a day)

instructions: Soak the cod for a day with four changes of water and poach it in milk for twenty minutes.
Boil the beans, lupini, broad beans, lentils and peas separately until soft.
Grind the peanuts with milk to a smooth mass; it is the soup's thickener.
Fry the onion in annatto oil, add the pumpkin and courgette and stew twenty minutes.
Blend the pumpkin and courgette and return them to the pot with the cod's milk.
Stir in all the cooked pulses, the rice, corn and peanut mass and cook thirty minutes.
Add the cream, cheese and pieces of cod, and serve with halved eggs and fried plantain.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Carimañola
description: Torpedo-shaped cassava croquettes with a meat filling, deep-fried. (Carimañola)
instructions: Peel the cassava, strip the woody core and boil it in salted water until completely soft.
Mash the cassava hot and work it with the egg and salt into a pliable dough.
Fry the onion, pepper and garlic, add the mince, cumin and tomato paste and cook it through.
Stir the culantro into the filling and cool it completely.
Take a lump of dough with wet hands, flatten it on your palm and put the filling in the centre.
Seal it and draw it into a torpedo with pointed ends.
Fry at 175 °C for four minutes, to a deep golden crust, and serve them hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Coconut rice
description: Rice cooked in coconut milk with caramelised coconut solids, dark and faintly sweet. (Arroz con coco)
instructions: Pour the coconut milk into a heavy pot and cook it over medium heat, stirring.
Keep cooking until the milk separates into oil and brown solids.
The moment the solids turn deep brown, add the water at once to stop the caramelisation.
Add the sugar, salt and raisins and bring it to the boil.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and add it to the pot in an even layer.
Cook uncovered over medium heat until the liquid falls to the level of the rice.
Cover it, drop the heat to its lowest and hold it twenty minutes without opening it once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kugelis
description: A potato bake from raw grated potato with bacon and onion, served with soured cream. (Kugelis)
instructions: Render the bacon to crackling, add the chopped onion and fry it golden.
Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly, collecting the liquid in a bowl.
Let the liquid stand ten minutes, pour off the water and stir the settled starch back in.
Add the hot milk and the hot fat with the onion and crackling, stirring quickly.
Work in the eggs, salt, pepper and marjoram to an even thick mass.
Pour it into a greased dish in a four-centimetre layer and level it.
Bake at 180 °C for an hour and a half, to a deep golden crust, and rest it twenty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Šakotis
description: A spiked tree cake baked layer by layer on a turning spit over a fire. (Šakotis)
instructions: Separate the whites from the yolks and whip the whites with half the sugar to firm peaks.
Beat the softened butter with the remaining sugar until pale, about eight minutes.
Add the yolks one at a time, still beating, then work in the soured cream, vanilla and zest.
Sift the flour with the starch and salt and fold it in with a spatula in three additions.
Fold in the whipped whites gently so the mixture does not collapse; the batter has to stay airy.
Heat the oven to 190 °C and pour the first thin layer onto a greased spit or into a tin.
Bake each layer three minutes to a golden colour and pour the next, until the batter runs out.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Sklandrausis
description: A rye pastry case with two layers of purée, potato and carrot, dusted with cinnamon. (Sklandrausis)
instructions: Knead a dough from the rye flour, warm water, melted butter and salt and rest it half an hour.
Boil the potatoes and carrots separately until completely soft.
Mash the potatoes with soured cream, an egg, caraway and salt into a smooth purée.
Mash the carrots with soured cream, an egg, sugar and cinnamon into a separate purée.
Roll the dough thin, cut rounds and shape rims with your fingers, folding the edges up.
Spread the potato purée as the first layer and the carrot over it, levelling with a spoon.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes and dust them with cinnamon while still hot.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Skābputra
description: Cold barley porridge on soured milk, Latvian field-day food. (Skābputra)
instructions: Rinse the barley and soak it in cold water for two hours.
Boil the barley in a litre and a half of water for an hour, until it collapses entirely.
Salt the porridge and cool it completely, stirring so no skin forms.
Work the curdled milk into the cold porridge gradually, to the consistency of a thick soup.
Leave it four hours somewhere cold so the sourness develops and evens out.
Boil the potatoes in their skins and serve them hot alongside.
Ladle it into bowls, add soured cream and scatter with spring onion and dill.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Verivorst
description: Blood sausage with pearl barley and marjoram, baked and served with lingonberry jam. (Verivorst)
instructions: Boil the barley in salted water for forty minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Render the pork fat to crackling, add the onion and fry it golden.
Cool both the barley and the fat with onion completely, or the blood sets when they meet.
Strain the blood through a sieve and mix it with the barley, fat, marjoram, allspice and salt.
Rinse the casings and fill them two-thirds full, leaving room for the barley to swell.
Tie the sausages every twenty centimetres and prick them in several places with a needle.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, dotted with butter, and serve with lingonberry jam.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kohuke
description: A curd bar in chocolate glaze, the Estonian dessert from the fridge. (Kohuke)
instructions: Push the curd through a fine sieve twice, until not a single grain remains.
Beat the softened butter with the icing sugar, vanilla and salt until fluffy.
Combine the curd with the butter mixture and work in the cream to the body of a firm cream.
Fold in the raisins and shape twelve finger-sized bars.
Lay the bars on parchment and freeze them two hours, until solid.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil over a water bath until smooth and cool it to lukewarm.
Dip the frozen bars on two forks, let them drain and set them on parchment to harden.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kalduny
description: Potato pancakes with a meat filling inside, fried and then stewed in soured cream. (Калдуны)
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for twenty minutes and chop them fine.
Fry two onions with the mince and mushrooms, add the marjoram, salt and pepper and cool it completely.
Grate the potatoes and the remaining onion finely into one bowl.
Let the mass stand three minutes and pour off the water that gathers, leaving the sediment.
Work in the egg and season the potato mass.
Put a spoon of the mass on your palm, add filling and cover it with a second spoon, sealing the edges.
Fry them three minutes a side, move them to a pan, pour over the soured cream and stew fifteen minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kholodnik
description: A cold beetroot soup on kefir with sorrel, cucumber and egg, pink and sharply sour. (Халаднік)
instructions: Boil the beetroot until tender with a spoon of vinegar so it keeps its colour, and cool it completely.
Cook the sorrel in a little water for five minutes, until it darkens, and cool it.
Grate the cooled beetroot coarsely and cut the cucumbers into matchsticks.
Mix the beetroot, the sorrel with its liquid, the cucumber and herbs with the soured cream and salt it.
Add the cold kefir and stir to an even pink.
Chill it an hour so the soup infuses and turns genuinely cold.
Boil the potatoes and serve them hot on a separate plate, with halved eggs in the soup.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Zemiakové placky
description: Thin potato pancakes with garlic and marjoram, fried crisp. (Zemiakové placky)
instructions: Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly, leaving some moisture in.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and work it into the potato mass.
Add the egg, milk, marjoram, pepper and flour and stir to a loose batter.
Heat the oil over medium and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading it very thin.
Fry three minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain them on a rack rather than paper and serve them at once.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Buchty
description: Yeast buns with plum jam or curd, baked packed together so their sides fuse. (Buchty)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and leave it fifteen minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, sponge, yolks, remaining sugar, zest, salt and half the butter.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Divide it into twelve balls and flatten each into a disc on your palm.
Put a spoon of jam or curd in each, seal the seam and turn them seam down.
Dip each bun in melted butter and pack them touching in a tin.
Prove them forty minutes, bake at 180 °C for thirty-five minutes and dust them with icing sugar.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Štruklji
description: A roll of thin dough with a curd filling, boiled in cloth and cut into rounds. (Štruklji)
instructions: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover it with a warmed bowl and rest it forty minutes; the dough has to turn pliable.
Work the curd with the eggs, soured cream, sugar and raisins until even.
Stretch the dough by hand on a cloth until translucent, as for strudel.
Spread the filling over the sheet, leaving the edges clear, and roll it up using the cloth.
Wrap the roll loosely in a clean cloth, tie the ends and lower it into boiling salted water.
Boil it forty minutes, unwrap it, cut it into rounds and fry them in butter with the breadcrumbs.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Carniolan sausage
description: A boiled pork sausage with garlic, served with horseradish and mustard, protected by origin. (Kranjska klobasa)
instructions: Dice the pork and fat and chill them to just above freezing.
Put the meat through the coarse plate of a mincer and the fat through the medium one.
Work in the curing salt, crushed garlic, pepper and iced water and knead the mixture until tacky.
Leave the mixture in the fridge for a day so the salt distributes and the colour sets.
Fill the casings tightly but without air pockets and tie them in twenty-centimetre pairs.
Air-dry the sausages two hours and cold-smoke them if you can.
Lower them into water at 75 °C and hold them twenty-five minutes without letting it boil. Serve with horseradish and mustard.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Begova čorba
description: A thick chicken soup with okra, bound with yolks and soured cream, a Bosnian classic. (Begova čorba)
instructions: Simmer the chicken and veal with the onion, carrot and celeriac for an hour, skimming.
Lift out the meat, strain the broth and pull the chicken into fine threads.
Rinse the okra under cold water and pat it dry without trimming the caps.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes without letting it colour.
Pour the broth into the roux, add the okra and cook fifteen minutes.
Whisk the yolks with the soured cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring without stopping.
Take the pot off the heat, pour in the mixture, return the meat and warm it through without boiling. Add lemon and parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tufahije
description: Apples poached in syrup and filled with walnuts under whipped cream. (Tufahije)
instructions: Peel the apples and core them without going through, so each forms a cup.
Make a syrup of water, sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon, bringing it to the boil.
Lower the apples into the syrup and poach them twenty minutes on a low heat, turning them.
Lift the apples out with a slotted spoon and cool them completely, keeping the syrup.
Mix the ground walnuts with three spoons of the syrup into a pliable mass.
Fill the apples with the walnut mass, mounded, and set them in dishes.
Spoon over the remaining syrup and top with whipped cream and a walnut half.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ohrid trout
description: Trout baked whole with lemon and herbs, from Lake Ohrid. (Ohridska pastrmka)
instructions: Rinse the trout, pat them dry and cut two slashes on each side.
Rub the fish with salt, pepper, paprika and olive oil inside and out.
Tuck lemon slices, garlic, parsley and thyme into each cavity.
Slice the potatoes thin and lay them overlapping on an oiled tray.
Set the fish on the potatoes and pour over the wine and the remaining oil.
Bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, until the skin colours.
Test at the spine and serve straight from the tray with a wedge of lemon.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pastrmajlija
description: A yeast-dough boat with cured pork and an egg, from Štip. (Пастрмалија)

ingredients.text: 600 g Pork neck (with its fat, diced)

instructions: Dice the pork into centimetre cubes, salt it generously and leave it two hours in the cold.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, sponge, oil and salt and work it ten minutes.
Let it rise an hour somewhere warm, until doubled.
Divide the dough into four and stretch each into an oval thirty centimetres long.
Fold the edges in to make a rim and spread the meat with paprika over the whole surface.
Bake at 250 °C for twenty minutes, crack an egg on top and give it five more.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Olla de carne
description: The Costa Rican meat pot with cassava, squash, corn and plantain. (Olla de carne)
instructions: Cover the shank with cold water, bring it to the boil and skim it thoroughly.
Add the onion, pepper and salt and simmer two hours, until the meat is tender.
Cut the cassava into large pieces, removing the woody core, and add it to the broth.
Twenty minutes later add the corn on the cob and the carrots.
Twenty minutes after that add the potatoes and squash in large pieces.
The plantain goes in last and cooks ten minutes, no longer.
Lift the solids out onto a platter, ladle the broth into cups and serve with rice, coriander and lime.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chorreadas
description: Pancakes of ground fresh corn, served with natilla soured cream. (Chorreadas)

ingredients.text: 200 ml Natilla or soured cream (to serve)

instructions: Cut the kernels from the cobs with a knife, running the blade down the core.
Grind the kernels in a blender in short pulses to a grainy mass.
Work in the egg, sugar, salt and corn flour to the consistency of thick cream.
Heat a pan with butter over medium until it just wisps.
Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it into a fifteen-centimetre round.
Fry three minutes a side, to golden patches and a springy centre.
Serve them hot with natilla and a slice of fresh cheese.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Montucas
description: Fresh-corn tamales with chicken, steamed in corn husks. (Montucas)

ingredients.text: 10 Fresh corn (on the cob, husks kept)

instructions: Strip the husks from the cobs whole and rinse them in warm water.
Cut off the kernels and grind them in a blender with the juice they release.
Beat the lard with salt and sugar and work in the corn mass until even.
Simmer the chicken until tender, pull it into threads and keep the broth.
Fry the onion, pepper and tomatoes with the annatto and add the chicken, olives and capers.
Spoon dough onto a husk, add filling, fold it over and tuck the ends under.
Stand the parcels upright in a pot and steam them an hour and a quarter.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Pastelitos
description: Fried corn turnovers with meat and potato under a cabbage salad. (Pastelitos de perro)
instructions: Fry the mince with the onion and annatto, add the finely diced potato and stew until soft.
Season the filling and cool it completely.
Shred the cabbage finely and pickle it in vinegar with salt for half an hour.
Mix the masa with warm water and salt to a pliable dough that does not stick to your hands.
Press a ball of dough between two sheets of film into a thin round.
Put a spoon of filling on one half, fold it over and seal the edge with a fork.
Deep-fry at 180 °C for three minutes a side and serve with the cabbage and sauce.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Vigorón
description: Boiled cassava with pork crackling and cabbage salad, served on a banana leaf. (Vigorón)
instructions: Shred the cabbage finely and mix it with the tomatoes, onion, vinegar, lime juice and salt.
Leave the curtido to pickle at least an hour, stirring it now and then.
