Cut the pork skin into squares, salt it and leave it twenty minutes.
Render the skin in its own fat over a low heat for forty minutes.
Raise the heat and fry ten minutes more, until the crackling puffs and turns crisp.
Boil the cassava in salted water until tender, having cut out the woody core.
Lay the cassava on a banana leaf, the curtido over it and the crackling on top, with the chilli.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Indio viejo
description: A thick stew of shredded beef, thickened with corn masa and mint. (Indio viejo)
instructions: Simmer the brisket with an onion and salt for an hour and a half, until fully tender.
Lift out the meat, keep the broth and pull the beef into fine threads by hand.
Fry the onion, garlic, pepper and tomatoes with the annatto to a thick base.
Slake the masa in cold broth until smooth, without a single lump.
Add the shredded meat to the vegetable base and warm it five minutes.
Pour in the slaked masa in a thin stream, stirring constantly, and cook twenty minutes.
Add the orange juice, stir in the chopped mint and serve it with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Vori vori
description: Chicken soup with corn-and-cheese dumplings, Paraguayan winter food. (Vori vori)
instructions: Brown the chicken pieces with the annatto on every side.
Add the onion, pepper, tomatoes and carrot and stew until the vegetables soften.
Pour in two litres of water, salt it and simmer forty minutes over a low heat.
Mix the corn flour with the grated cheese, egg, oregano and a pinch of salt.
Add a couple of spoons of hot broth and work it into a firm dough that holds its shape.
Roll walnut-sized balls, compacting each between your palms.
Drop the balls into the boiling broth, leave them five minutes unstirred and cook twenty. Scatter with parsley.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mbejú
description: A starch and cheese flatbread set in a dry pan without a drop of water. (Mbejú)
instructions: Mix the cassava starch with the corn flour and salt in a wide bowl.
Rub the soft fat into the dry mix with your fingers until it looks like damp sand.
Work in the grated cheese, still rubbing the mixture by hand.
Add the milk a spoon at a time, until the crumb just holds when squeezed in your fist.
Heat a dry pan over medium without adding a drop of oil.
Tip in a centimetre of crumb and press it down with a spatula across the whole surface.
Cook it five minutes, flip it with a plate and colour the second side.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Musakhan
description: Chicken with onion and sumac on taboon bread soaked in olive oil. (مسخن)
instructions: Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, allspice, cardamom and cinnamon and leave it half an hour.
Slice the onions into thin half-moons; a kilo and a half takes about twenty minutes.
Stew the onions in the olive oil over a low heat for forty minutes, until translucent and sweet.
Stir two-thirds of the sumac and salt into the onions and give them five more minutes.
Brown the chicken and roast it at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden, watching that they do not scorch.
Lay down the bread, the onions on it, the chicken on top, spoon over the pan oil and scatter with sumac and nuts.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Galayet bandora
description: Tomatoes cooked down in olive oil with chilli and garlic to a thick sauce. (قلاية بندورة)
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into large wedges, skins and seeds left in.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the onion in it.
Add the crushed garlic and the whole green chillies and warm them a minute.
Tip in the tomatoes, salt them and stew over a medium heat, stirring now and then.
Crush the tomatoes with a spoon once the skins start to lift from the flesh.
Reduce it fifteen minutes more, until the oil rises at the edges as a separate layer.
Scatter with dried mint and serve it in the pan with flatbread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Omani halwa
description: A chewy halwa of starch, rosewater and saffron, stirred two hours in a cauldron. (حلوى عمانية)
instructions: Slake the starch in half the cold water until completely smooth, with no lumps.
Boil a syrup from the sugar and the remaining water and bring it to a rolling boil.
Pour the starch mixture into the boiling syrup in a thin stream, stirring without stopping.
Steep the saffron in a spoon of hot water and add it to the mass with the cardamom.
Stir over a low heat for an hour and a half, adding the ghee a little at a time.
Work in the honey, rosewater and toasted cashews once the mass starts pulling from the sides.
Spread it in a tin in a three-centimetre layer, level it and cool it six hours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Maqdeed
description: Sun-dried meat with turmeric, boiled and then fried with onion. (مقديد)
instructions: Cut the lamb into two-finger strips along the grain.
Rub the strips all over with salt and turmeric, sparing neither.
Hang the meat in shade with a draught and dry it three to five days, until fully hard.
Soak the dried meat in cold water for two hours, changing the water once.
Boil the meat forty minutes, until it softens and starts to come apart in threads.
Fry the onion with the garlic, cumin and chilli in ghee until golden.
Add the shredded meat and fry ten minutes more, to browned edges. Serve it with rice.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Zurbian
description: Yemeni rice with lamb and potato, coloured with saffron and baked sealed. (زربيان)
instructions: Marinate the lamb in yoghurt with the hawaij and salt for two hours.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it thirty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee to a deep gold and set half of it aside.
Brown the meat with the remaining onion, add the tomatoes and cardamom and stew an hour.
Fry the potato rounds to a golden crust in a separate pan.
Boil the rice in salted water for seven minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Layer the meat, rice, potato and raisins, streak the saffron over and bake it covered for thirty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fahsa
description: Boiling lamb stew in a stone bowl, topped with frothy fenugreek hulba. (فحسة)

ingredients.text: 1 kg Lamb (meat with a little bone)

instructions: Cover the ground fenugreek with cold water and leave it six hours, changing the water twice.
Simmer the lamb with the onion and salt for an hour and a half, keeping the broth.
Break the meat into small pieces and return it to the strained broth.
Pound the garlic, chilli and coriander into a sahawiq paste in a mortar.
Add the tomatoes, hawaij and half the paste to the stew and reduce it to a thick body.
Drain the fenugreek and whip it with a spoon of cold water into a white froth.
Ladle the stew into scorching bowls, spoon the froth over and serve it boiling with flatbread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kuwaiti gereesh
description: Cracked wheat cooked down with chicken and tomato to a thick porridge under fried onion. (قريش)
instructions: Rinse the cracked wheat and soak it in cold water for an hour.
Fry two of the onions in ghee until soft and add the baharat.
Brown the chicken with the onion and add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon and pierced dried lime.
Pour in two litres of water, salt it and cook forty minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken, tip the wheat into the broth and cook it an hour over a low heat.
Mash the porridge until the grain breaks down into a uniform mass.
Fry the remaining onion to deep brown, plate the porridge with the chicken and pour the onion and its butter over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Darabeel
description: Kuwaiti buns of date paste and cardamom, rolled into spirals. (درابيل)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Steep the saffron in a spoon of hot water and knead a dough with the flour, egg, half the butter and cardamom.
Let the dough rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Warm the date paste with the remaining butter and cardamom until soft.
Roll the dough into a rectangle half a centimetre thick and spread the date paste over it.
Roll it up tight and cut it into two-centimetre rounds.
Set them cut side up, prove them twenty minutes and bake at 180 °C for twenty-five minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Rechta
description: Algerian handmade noodles steamed over broth and dressed with a white chicken sauce. (رشتة)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water, a spoon of oil and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Roll the dough into a thin sheet and cut it into two-millimetre noodles.
Spread the noodles on a cloth, dust them with flour and dry them twenty minutes.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, chickpeas, cinnamon and white pepper in two litres of water for forty minutes.
Add the turnip in wedges and cook twenty minutes more, until tender.
Steam the noodles over the broth fifteen minutes, take them off, sprinkle with oil and toss them.
Repeat the steaming twice more, mound the noodles, top with the chicken and turnip and ladle broth over.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Makroud
description: Semolina diamonds with a date filling, fried and steeped in honey. (مقروض)
instructions: Rub the semolina with the olive oil and salt by hand until it is damp all through.
Leave the mixture half an hour so the grain takes up the oil and swells.
Add the warm water with the orange blossom water a little at a time, gathering the dough without kneading.
Steam the dates soft and pound them with the cinnamon and zest into a smooth paste.
Roll the dough into a strip, lay a rope of date paste down the centre and close the edges over it.
Press the strip flat and cut it on the diagonal into four-centimetre diamonds.
Deep-fry at 170 °C until golden and drop them hot into cold honey for five minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Gurasa
description: A thick Sudanese pan bread, served with meat stew or sauce. (قراصة)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm water and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Whisk in the flour and salt to a smooth, loose batter without lumps.
Add the oil and beat another minute, until the batter goes glossy.
Cover it and leave it warm for an hour, until bubbles break the surface.
Heat a dry pan over medium and pour in a ladle of batter.
Cover it and cook five minutes, until the top sets and turns matt.
Lift it out without turning it and stack the breads under a cloth.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Salata aswad
description: A Sudanese salad of fried aubergine with peanut butter and lemon. (سلطة أسود)
instructions: Dice the aubergines, salt them and leave them twenty minutes to draw out the bitterness.
Pat the cubes dry with paper; wet ones spit in the oil.
Fry the aubergine in batches to a dark brown crust and drain it on paper.
Pound the garlic with salt into a paste in a mortar.
Let the peanut butter down with lemon juice, the garlic and water to the body of soured cream.
Chop the tomatoes, onion and chilli fine and mix them with the cooled aubergine.
Pour over the peanut dressing, toss it and let it stand fifteen minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mchuzi wa samaki
description: Tanzanian fish curry on coconut milk with tamarind and curry powder. (Mchuzi wa samaki)
instructions: Rub the fish steaks with salt and half the curry powder and leave them fifteen minutes.
Fry the fish two minutes a side to a crust and lift it onto a plate.
Soften the onion in the same pan and add the garlic and ginger.
Add the remaining curry powder and warm it a minute, until the aroma lifts.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and reduce them to a thick base without loose liquid.
Pour in the coconut milk with the tamarind and warm it without letting it boil.
Return the fish to the sauce, let it sit five minutes and serve with rice and coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Vitumbua
description: Rice cakes on coconut milk, cooked in a pan of hemispherical wells. (Vitumbua)
instructions: Drain the soaked rice and grind it with the coconut milk into a smooth, loose batter.
Stir in the yeast, sugar, cardamom, salt and grated coconut.
Leave the batter to ferment four hours in the warm, until it is covered in bubbles.
Stir the batter and check the body: it should pour in a ribbon rather than drop in a lump.
Heat the dimpled pan and brush each well with oil.
Fill the wells three-quarters full and cook three minutes, until the edges set.
Turn the cakes with a skewer and give them three minutes more, to a browned sphere.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Eru
description: A Cameroonian stew of finely shredded eru leaf with waterleaf and palm oil. (Eru)
instructions: Simmer the beef and tripe with the onion and a stock cube for an hour, until tender.
Soak the dried fish in hot water twenty minutes and flake it, taking out the bones.
Shred the eru leaf as fine as you can, rolling it tight before cutting.
Rinse the waterleaf and cut it coarsely; it wilts right down as it cooks anyway.
Put the waterleaf into the pot with the meat and let it wilt, giving up its juice.
Add the eru, fish, crayfish and chilli and stew twenty minutes with the lid on.
Pour in the palm oil, stir it through and cook ten minutes more uncovered.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Koki
description: A pudding of ground black-eyed beans with palm oil, steamed in banana leaves. (Koki)
instructions: Soak the beans four hours, then rub them between your hands so the skins come away.
Rinse the beans several times, pouring off the floating skins, until the grains are clean and white.
Grind the beans with the onion and chilli into a thick paste, adding water a spoon at a time.
Beat the mass by hand or with a spatula for ten minutes, until it lightens and turns airy.
Warm the palm oil and work it into the mass to an even orange.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame until pliable and spoon the mass onto them with the greens.
Fold the parcels, tie them and steam them an hour and a half, until firm.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kleftiko
description: Lamb baked five hours in sealed clay with not a drop of water. (Κλέφτικο)
instructions: Cut deep slits into the lamb and push a sliver of garlic into each.
Rub the meat with salt, pepper, oregano, olive oil and lemon juice.
Leave the lamb to marinate in the fridge for at least four hours.
Cut the potatoes into large wedges and lay them in the base of a clay dish.
Set the meat on the potatoes and add the bay, cinnamon and lemon halves.
Cover it and seal the join with a strip of dough or a double layer of foil.
Bake at 160 °C for five hours without opening it and rest it twenty minutes.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Koupepia
description: Cypriot vine leaves rolled with rice, mince and cinnamon, finished with lemon. (Κουπέπια)
instructions: Scald the vine leaves for a minute and spread them on a cloth.
Mix both minces with the raw rice, grated onion, tomatoes and herbs.
Work in the cinnamon, mint, salt, pepper and half the olive oil.
Put a spoon of filling on a leaf, fold the sides in and roll it into a tight cylinder.
Line the pot with torn leaves so the rolls do not catch.
Pack the rolls in tight layers seam down and weight them with a plate.
Pour in water with lemon juice and oil and cook them an hour, covered, over a low heat.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Lampuki pie
description: The Maltese pie of dorado with spinach, olives and cauliflower. (Torta tal-lampuki)

ingredients.text: 1.2 kg Dorado or sea bream (in steaks)

instructions: Fry the fish steaks three minutes a side and let them cool.
Lift the flesh off the bones, picking out every small bone.
Fry the onion, add the cauliflower florets and stew them ten minutes.
Add the spinach, tomato paste, olives, capers, sultanas and walnuts and cook it dry.
Cool the filling completely and fold the fish into it in pieces.
Line a tin with pastry, add the filling and cover it with a second sheet, crimping the edge.
Glaze it with egg, cut vents and bake at 190 °C for forty-five minutes, to a golden crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Imqaret
description: Maltese pastry diamonds with an aniseed date filling, deep-fried. (Imqaret)
instructions: Chop the dates and put them in a pan with the zests, aniseed and liqueur.
Cook the filling over a low heat for twenty minutes, to a thick even paste.
Cool the filling completely; warm, it tears the pastry as you wrap it.
Cut the margarine into the flour with salt to a crumb and bring the dough together with cold water.
Roll the dough into a long strip twelve centimetres wide.
Lay a rope of the date paste down the centre, fold the edges over and press the seam.
Cut it on the diagonal into diamonds and fry them at 180 °C, two minutes a side.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Fërgesë
description: An Albanian bake of peppers, tomatoes and curd cheese, served in its clay pan. (Fërgesë)
instructions: Char the peppers over a flame or under a grill until the skins blacken.
Put the hot peppers in a bag for ten minutes and peel them.
Soften the onion and garlic in butter and stir in a spoon of flour.
Add the chopped tomatoes and reduce them to a thick base with no loose liquid.
Cut the peeled peppers into strips and stir them into the tomato base.
Mash the curd cheese with the feta and work it into the hot mixture.
Transfer it to a clay pan and bake at 200 °C for twenty minutes, until it bubbles.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ballokume
description: Cornmeal biscuits from Elbasan, beaten by hand in a wooden bowl for the spring festival. (Ballokume)
instructions: Beat the softened butter with the sugar with a wooden spoon for twenty minutes, to a pale fluffy mass.
Add the yolks one at a time, still beating in the same direction.
Add the vanilla, salt and soda and beat five minutes more.
Work in the cornmeal a little at a time, to a firm but pliable dough.
Rest the dough fifteen minutes so the meal takes up the moisture.
Shape walnut-sized balls and set them well apart on parchment.
Bake at 170 °C for twenty minutes, to a pale gold edge, and cool them on the tray.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Moldovan sarmale
description: Small rolls of soured cabbage stewed with smoked meat under a blanket of leaves. (Sarmale)
instructions: Take the head apart into leaves and pare down the thick rib at the base of each.
Fry the onion in oil until golden and cool it completely.
Mix the mince with the raw rice, onion, dill, thyme, salt and pepper.
Halve the larger leaves and roll parcels the size of a thumb.
Line the base of a pot with leaf trimmings and pieces of smoked rib.
Pack the sarmale in tight circles, laying ribs between every other layer.
Pour over tomato juice and water, cover with torn leaves and stew at 150 °C for three hours.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Mucenici
description: Yeast figures of eight glazed with honey and walnuts for the day of the Forty Martyrs. (Mucenici)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and leave it to foam.
Knead a dough from the flour, sponge, eggs, sugar, zest, vanilla, salt and softened butter.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour and a quarter, until doubled.
Divide the dough into twelve and roll each into a forty-centimetre rope.
Twist each rope into a figure of eight, joining the ends, and set it on a tray.
Prove them thirty minutes and bake at 180 °C for twenty minutes, until golden.
Brush the hot mucenici with honey and cover them thickly with ground walnuts.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Kuurdak
description: Lamb fried in its own tail fat with onion and potato. (Куурдак)
instructions: Dice the tail fat and render it in a cauldron to golden crackling.
Lift out the crackling with a slotted spoon and set it aside; it goes back at the very end.
Cut the meat into walnut-sized pieces and fry it in batches to a dark crust.
Return all the meat to the pot, salt it, add the cumin and cover it for fifteen minutes.
Add the onion in thick half-moons and fry until it turns translucent.
Add the potatoes in large pieces and cook twenty minutes more, covered.
Return the crackling, add the garlic and coriander and serve it straight from the pot with bread.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Boorsok
description: Kyrgyz fried dough diamonds, hollow inside, for tea and the dastarkhan. (Боорсок)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm milk and leave it fifteen minutes, until it foams.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, sponge, egg, melted butter and salt.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Knock the dough back and roll it out to exactly a centimetre thick.
Cut it into four-centimetre diamonds and let them rest twenty minutes.
Heat the oil to 180 °C and lower the diamonds in in small batches.
Fry them a minute and a half a side, turning with a slotted spoon, to golden puffs.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Tushbera
description: Tajik dumplings in broth with herbs, boiled in thin dough and served in a bowl. (Тушбера)
instructions: Knead a stiff dough from the flour, egg, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it forty minutes; that is what makes it pliable.
Chop the lamb and tail fat by knife into a fine crumb.
Mix the meat with finely chopped onion, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough until translucent and cut five-centimetre rounds.
Fold the dumplings, sealing the edge and bringing two corners together into a ring.
Cook them in the boiling broth for eight minutes and serve them in a bowl with katyk and coriander.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Chakka
description: Strained cultured cheese with herbs and garlic, the Tajik spread for flatbread. (Чакка)
instructions: Line a colander with two layers of close-woven cloth and pour in the katyk.
Knot the corners of the cloth and hang the bundle over a bowl somewhere cold.
Leave it draining a full day, until the mass is as firm as soft curd.
Pound the garlic with a pinch of salt into a smooth paste.
Chop the coriander, dill, basil and spring onion as fine as you can.
Fold the herbs and garlic into the strained mass with a spatula, without mashing it.
Salt it, smooth it in a bowl, press a hollow with a spoon and pour the oil into it.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Khuushuur
description: Mongolian fried lamb pasties, flat and crisp, made for Naadam. (Хуушуур)
instructions: Knead an unleavened dough from the flour, water and salt and work it ten minutes to smoothness.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Chop the lamb fine by knife, fat and all, and mix it with the onion and garlic.
Pour the broth into the filling and work it to a loose but not runny mass.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into a twelve-centimetre round.
Put filling on one half, fold it over and crimp the edge tightly and evenly.
Fry them in a centimetre of oil, three minutes a side, to a blistered crust.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Suutei tsai
description: Mongolian salted milk tea with butter, boiled rather than brewed. (Сүүтэй цай)

ingredients.text: 20 g Green tea (brick tea if possible)

instructions: Break up the brick tea and cover it with a litre of cold water in a pot.
Bring it to the boil and cook five minutes, until the liquor darkens.
Pour in the milk and bring it back to the boil, watching that it does not run over.
Salt it and cook five minutes more over a low heat.
Ladle the tea up and pour it back from a height a dozen times.
Add the butter and stir until it disappears.
Strain it into bowls and serve it hot, with toasted flour if you like.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Ashak
description: Afghan leek dumplings under garlic yoghurt and a meat sauce. (آشک)
instructions: Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it forty minutes under film.
Chop the spring onion very fine, salt it and wring it out in a cloth.
Fry the onion with the mince, add the tomato paste and stew it twenty minutes.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and salt and leave it at room temperature.
Roll the dough thin and cut eight-centimetre rounds.
Add the leek filling, fold each into a half-moon and crimp the edge tight.
Boil the dumplings five minutes, lay them on the yoghurt, spoon the sauce over and dust with mint and chilli.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)

title: Bolani
description: An Afghan flatbread with a potato or leek filling, cooked on a dry pan. (بولانی)
instructions: Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Boil the potatoes soft, drain them and mash them without milk.
Work the spring onion, coriander, chilli, salt and pepper into the mash.
Divide the dough into six and roll each into a thin round.
Spread the filling thinly over half the round and fold the other half over, pressing the edge.
Cook them on a brush-oiled pan, four minutes a side, until spotted.
author: UniTools (theunitools.com)
